stories.title: 800-year-old 'Mazar' razed overnight:Bulldozers clear land in Etawah; saplings planted across site
stories.summary: Syed Baba's shrine in Etawah, UP, was demolished by a bulldozer on Wednesday night. When villagers arrived on Thursday morning, there was no trace of the shrine left. The entire land had been leveled. Waist-high plants had been planted. The place looked like a jungle. Seeing this, people couldn't believe that a shrine had stood there just 12 hours earlier. On Wednesday evening at 6 PM, a Forest Department team arrived with three bulldozers. More than 20 policemen were deployed on the path leading to the shrine. Movement of anyone was restricted. After this, the shrine was demolished in 7 hours. The bulldozer action continued until 1 AM. The shrine's caretaker claims that the shrine was 800 years old. The Forest Department states that the shrine was built on government land, which is why action was taken. This shrine, built over 3000 square feet, was located in the Fisher forest area of the ravines, one and a half kilometers from Etawah city. The shrine was famous by the name of Beehad Wale Syed Baba. In January, a complaint about the shrine was made on the CM portal. Following this, the forest department investigated and issued instructions to remove the shrine. The caretaker of the shrine went to the forest department's court, but their appeal was rejected. See 3 pictures- Know the full story in 5 points There is no record of who built the shrine or when it was built. Every year in February, an Urs (festival) was organized at the shrine, in which 5 to 7 thousand people participated. This time, the Urs did not take place in February. There is no official record available of when the shrine was built, who built it, or when it was established. Forest department officials also do not have any record related to its construction. The Forest Department says that over time, construction gradually increased on the protected forest land and later a permanent structure was erected here. This entire process took place without any statutory permission, hence it has been considered illegal construction. Maulana says - Claim of it being the tomb of Muhammad Ghori's general is false The tomb is looked after by Fazle Ilahi, a resident of Akalganj, Etawah city. His associate Maulana Nadeem said that this tomb is about 800 years old. Some people claim it to be the tomb of Muhammad Ghori's general Shamsuddin, but this claim is completely false and baseless. He said - Historical documents state that in 1194, a war took place in Etawah between the Islamic invader Muhammad Ghori and Sumer Singh, the commander of King Jaichand of Kannauj. In this, Ghori's general Shamsuddin and many Muslim soldiers were killed. Some of them were buried in Bais Khwaja, but no one has any information on how Shamsuddin's tomb was built in Fisher Forest.

stories.title: Boyfriend forces nursing student to take abortion pills, she dies:Buys medicines after watching YouTube; flees Varanasi hostel
stories.summary: A 19-year-old nursing student died in Varanasi after consuming abortion pills. She was 3 months pregnant. Her boyfriend had pressured her into taking the medicine. On Wednesday morning at 11:30 AM, the student's blood-soaked body was found on the hostel stairs. An electrician who came to work there first saw the student lying unconscious. When he shouted, the guard and people nearby arrived. The student was taken to Shiv Surgical Nursing Home, where doctors declared her dead. Police examined the student's call details. They spoke to her family members and the hostel guard. The guard stated that the student used to meet Mohammad Sameer, a resident of Kariyav Mirganj, Jaunpur, at the hostel. Police traced his location and arrested Sameer from his home late Wednesday evening. Upon strict interrogation, he confessed. During police interrogation, the accused stated that he had bought abortion pills after watching YouTube. After taking the medicine, his girlfriend experienced severe stomach pain. Vomiting and bleeding started. She asked to be taken to the hospital. Then she started running down the stairs herself, fainted and fell. Her clothes were soaked in blood. I panicked and left her, fleeing to my home in Jaunpur. The student's father is a constable. He is posted in Chandauli. He lives in Kashi with his family. He has two sons. The student was a GNM second-year student. Her boyfriend, Mohammad Sameer, also studies in the same college. He is a nursing third-year student. Boyfriend said - talked to doctors, but no one was ready for an abortion The boyfriend told during the interrogation that they had been in a relationship for two years. They used to travel together during holidays. One day, she told him that she was pregnant. An ultrasound confirmed it. She was three months pregnant. They talked to doctors, but no one was ready for an abortion without the consent of family members. After this, both of them planned the abortion themselves. Bought Abortion Pills After Watching YouTube The boyfriend said - Being medical students, they first read books, but couldn't decide anything. After this, they watched YouTube. After watching several channels, they agreed to take abortion pills. They also saw the method of taking the medicine on YouTube, then bought a branded medicine. It was decided that the student would take the medicine on Wednesday. On Wednesday morning at 9 AM, she reached the hostel with food for both of us from home. After coming into the room, she was scared and nervous. When asked to take the medicine, she refused. When pressured, she said - let's get married, but I didn't listen to her. Against her will, I forcibly made her take the medicine. The dose of medicine was high. Bleeding started an hour later. Half an hour later, her condition worsened even more. She said, "Take me to the hospital." Before I could say anything, she ran out of the room. I was scared seeing the blood The boyfriend said - blood was continuously flowing from her private part. The lift was closed due to a power outage. Because of this, she started going down the stairs. Then she felt dizzy due to bleeding and fell. I was scared seeing the blood. I came up to my room, locked it, and fled to my home in Jaunpur by bus. Student's abortion was also done 7 months ago According to the police, painkillers and other medicines were found in the student's bag. Her boyfriend said that the student had an abortion 7 months ago as well. Videos and photos were found on the boyfriend's phone. Chatting done with the student has also been recovered. Guard said - The student was coming to the hostel continuously for two days The guard of the boys' hostel said that the girl had been coming to the hostel continuously for the last two days. She had also come on Tuesday. She made three-four rounds from the grocery store on the road opposite to the tree inside the campus and wandered alone for a long time. On Wednesday morning at 9:20 AM, she went straight to the room, climbing the stairs alone. Later, she was found covered in blood. ACP Sarnath Vidyut Saxena said- The student's body was post-mortemed by a panel of two doctors, and its videography was also done. The boyfriend has been arrested and is being interrogated.

stories.title: Baraat on Bulldozer:Groom smokes cigarette as band and dancers follow; Moradabad Police issue fine
stories.summary: In Moradabad, the groom set off for the wedding procession on a bulldozer. The bulldozer sometimes lifted the wedding guests 10 feet up and sometimes brought them down to the road. During this, the groom kept smoking cigarettes and blowing rings. He kept dancing. He kept gesturing to the children sitting with him to dance. A video of the groom going to his in-laws' house on a bulldozer was recorded by a friend of the groom and uploaded on Instagram. The video quickly went viral. In the video, 15 wedding guests are seen sitting on the bulldozer with the groom. The groom is smoking a cigarette and blowing smoke into the air. When the police investigated the video, it was found that the wedding procession had gone from Umri Kalan village in Kanth to Sahaspur village in Bijnor two days earlier, on June 8. Taking action, the police issued a challan for the bulldozer on Wednesday, June 10. The matter falls under the Kanth police station area. See 2 pictures First, understand the whole matter step-by-step- Usman, a resident of Umri Kalan in Kanth police station area, was engaged to a girl from Sahaspur village in Bijnor. The wedding was on June 8. On Monday afternoon, after completing the 'ghudchadhi' (groom's procession on horseback) ritual with the baraatis (wedding guests) from his home, the groom rode on a bulldozer. During this, about 15 baraatis also climbed onto the bulldozer with him. Bhangra music played in front, and the bulldozer followed behind. The groom was seen dancing while sitting on the bulldozer. The youths sitting with him were seen dancing to film songs. Now read, what is visible in the video It can be seen in the video that the bulldozer is decorated with flowers. The groom, wearing a white sherwani, is sitting on its front part. Garlands of notes are around his neck. Along with the groom, about 10 to 15 people are also riding on the bulldozer. Some of them are children. The groom is smoking a cigarette and blowing smoke rings. The youths sitting with him are dancing to film songs. Bhangra is playing in front, and the bulldozer is moving behind. Some people are also making videos. A song is playing in the background - 'I haven't come here to interfere in anyone's business...' Video 2 days old, bulldozer will be seized SP Rural Kunwar Akash Singh said- The video of going to the wedding by bulldozer is from June 8. Taking action in this matter, the bulldozer has been challaned. Action will be taken to find and seize the bulldozer.

stories.title: Monkey attacks man outside exam centre:Left arm vein cut; accompanying daughter for UP Police recruitment exam in Gorakhpur
stories.summary: A father who came to Gorakhpur to help his daughter take the UP Constable recruitment exam was bitten and severely injured by a monkey. In the attack, a vein in his left hand was severed, causing continuous bleeding. Upon receiving information, the police on duty immediately took the injured person to Nehru Hospital at BRD Medical College. There, doctors brought the situation under control after providing treatment. It is being told that Vishambhar, a resident of Maharajganj district, had arrived at a school center in Pipraich with his daughter Priya on Wednesday. After the exam started, he was sitting in a garden about 200 meters away from the center, waiting for his daughter to come out. Suddenly, a black monkey attacked him. After the incident, the forest department team started searching for the monkey, but its whereabouts are still unknown. Know the full story According to information, Priya, daughter of Vishambhar Prasad, a resident of Gopalpur village in Pharenda police station area of Maharajganj district, had her constable recruitment exam in the first shift on Wednesday. To help her take the exam, he took his daughter to the Maharana Pratap Krishi Inter College center in Pipraich. His daughter entered and started giving the paper inside. Meanwhile, Vishambhar was sitting in a garden about 200 meters away from the center, waiting for his daughter to come out. Around 12 noon, a black monkey suddenly arrived there. The monkey hovered around for some time The monkey hovered around for some time and then suddenly attacked Vishambhar. In the attack, a vein in his right hand was cut, causing him to bleed profusely. After the incident, there was chaos among the people present nearby. Upon receiving the information, Sub-Inspector Shailendra Yadav, who was on duty, reached the spot and immediately took the injured person to BRD Medical College. There, doctors treated him and stopped the bleeding from the vein in his hand. Upon learning about the incident, the injured person's family also reached the hospital. After her exam ended, his daughter Priya also arrived at the hospital. Meanwhile, upon police information, a team from the forest department also reached the spot and is engaged in searching for and monitoring the monkey in the area. However, it has not been found yet.

The officers to be promoted include Resident Commissioner, Special Secretary, Additional Commissioner, ADM, Secretary, and officers from several development authorities. The promotion of Harish Chandra (1997 batch), Prabhunath (1999 batch), Anju Katiyar (2002 batch), and Amar Pal Singh (2004 batch) has been confirmed. Additionally, many officers from the 2010, 2011, and 2012 batches will also benefit from promotion. The names of officers to be promoted include Alok Verma, Dr. Vishram, Pushpraj Singh, Vivek Srivastava, Yoganand Pandey, Amit Kumar, Dr. Sunil Kumar Verma, Garima Swaroop, and Sandeep Kumar, among others. This decision will bring about administrative changes at the district, divisional, and departmental levels in many areas. The promoted officers will soon be assigned new responsibilities in their positions. She has also been a topper of the UPPSC examination. In 2018, she was the Examination Controller at the UP Public Service Commission (UPPSC). During this period, the case of the LT Grade teacher recruitment examination paper leak came to light. The UP STF arrested her in May 2019 on charges of alleged involvement in the case. After her arrest, the state government suspended her. She remained in jail for several months. After about 8 months, she was granted bail by the Allahabad High Court in 2020. Later, she was reinstated in service. PCS Rakesh Kumar Patel also promoted Rakesh Kumar Patel is a PCS officer of the 2010 batch. After promotion, he will be inducted into the Indian Administrative Service (IAS). In the recent promotion, he will be assigned new responsibilities. Rakesh Kumar Patel, a resident of Maharajganj, is currently serving as Additional Commissioner (Judicial)-IV in Lucknow division. Prior to this, he has also served as Chief Revenue Officer (CRO) in Pratapgarh. From July 2024 to July 2025, he was posted as Additional District Magistrate (ADM) in Kasganj. Considering his long experience in the administrative field, he has been promoted.

stories.title: SP MP raises issue of posts on Akhilesh’s daughter:Former minister says opposition does not target family members; calls it cheap politics
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party members are angry over objectionable posts on social media targeting Akhilesh Yadav's 23-year-old elder daughter, Aditi Yadav. Samajwadi Party MP from Ghosi seat in Mau, Rajiv Rai, on Wednesday, criticised the BJP and UP Police. He said, "This is the lowest level of politics and the pinnacle of mental derangement. Obscene and vulgar posts are being made on social media about former Chief Minister Akhilesh Yadav's daughter. UP Police has not taken any action yet. Is it because she is not the daughter of a BJP leader? Shame on you." Former minister and Samajwadi Party leader from Ayodhya, Tej Narayan Pandey (Pawan Pandey), has blamed the BJP for this. Pawan Pandey released a video on X and said, When Akhilesh Yadav raised questions about theft in the offerings of the Ram Temple, instead of giving factual answers to the allegations, BJP leaders resorted to personal attacks. Targeting Akhilesh's family is cheap politics. This is not just an attack on a political family, but an assault on the dignity of every daughter, every sister, and every mother in the state. In this matter, SP workers have filed a complaint at Hazratganj Kotwali in Lucknow. They have demanded strict action by registering an FIR against those who posted against Aditi Yadav. Now read in detail Pawan Pandey said- An attack on the dignity of every daughter, sister, and mother in the state Pawan Pandey said, instead of answering questions related to the Ram Temple donation amount, some BJP leaders and supporters are targeting the families of political opponents. It is extremely unfortunate that those who (the BJP) claim to be the biggest protectors of Sanatan culture are the ones who, in political vendetta, do things that hurt the dignity of women and daughters. In Sanatan tradition, women are considered a form of power, respect, and worship, but in the BJP's politics, when it becomes difficult to answer, character assassination and mudslinging at families become the easiest weapon. Those who are writing this must also have been born to a mother; they must also have a sister, a wife; how would they feel if something like this happened to their family? Every baseless accusation made against Akhilesh Yadav's family is not just an attack on a political family, but an assault on the dignity of every daughter, every sister, and every mother in the state. This is proof of that double standard, where slogans of 'women's respect' are raised from stages, and behind the scenes, women's dignity is made a political weapon. You are very adept at slandering others' mothers, sisters, daughters, wives, and using inappropriate words. However, when the same thing happens to you, you don't hesitate to beat your chest and cry. SP MP from Sitapur, Anand Bhadauria, said, Slinging mud on character is the pride of cowards, respecting daughters is the identity of India. Those who want to defame a daughter with fabricated stories, do they also know the consequences of public anger? SP spokesperson said - Aditi understands her good and bad SP spokesperson Nahid Lari Khan has responded to those posting on social media. She wrote on X, Aditi Yadav is a promising and highly qualified child. She has a very good understanding of right and wrong. Since she is the daughter of Akhilesh Yadav, the biggest leader of UP, the third largest state in the country, and a great warrior of PDA, the absurd people of an absurd party are writing absurd things about Aditi. It is possible that those who write cheap things have had such unfortunate incidents happen in their homes. Perhaps that is why, out of resentment, they are writing cheap things about the family of a big leader. Don't write such things. Everyone has daughters and sisters in their homes. Learn to respect women. This is not an insult to Aditi, but an insult to every daughter and sister in the country. Lohini Vahini said - if no action is taken, a big protest will be launched Raj Sahni, National Vice President of Samajwadi Lohia Vahini, said that extremely objectionable posts have been made against Aditi Yadav, daughter of SP President Akhilesh Yadav, on social media platforms. He demanded that an FIR be registered against anti-social elements spreading misleading and character-assassinating propaganda. He has handed over all evidence related to the matter and social media screenshots to the police. He said that if the police do not take action against such people, a protest will be launched. Raj Sahni said that our emotions are directly connected to Akhilesh Yadav and his family. Making such serious and baseless allegations against a daughter is extremely shameful. If someone makes even a small comment on a leader of the ruling party, immediate action is taken against them. But the character assassination of the former Chief Minister's daughter is being done on social media, and no action is being taken on it. SP spokesperson said - Will file cases against each and every one SP National Spokesperson Fakhrul Hasan Chand said, As soon as people of the party with 'character, conduct, and face' get stuck in any issue, they descend to the lowest level of their politics. They start making indecent comments on the members of the Samajwadi family. Sometimes, a BJP mayor speaks about the late mother of our respected national president, who is a leader for all of us. Now, BJP leaders and workers are commenting on social media about the daughter of the respected national president with their low, cheap mentality. The way one post after another was written on social media, BJP's power is behind it. BJP is engaging in low-level politics. Listen carefully, those who write about the Samajwadi family on social media will not be spared. We will file a case against each and every one. If it's not registered at the police station, we will get it registered under 173(3) BNSS. Be prepared, you will definitely face us in court.

stories.title: Devotee claims Baba Neem Karoli’s 'slap' transformed his life:Burn injury healed instantly; entire wedding party saved in bus accident
stories.summary: Numerous extraordinary experiences associated with Kainchi Dham and Baba Neem Karoli (Neem Karoli Baba) continue to be narrated by devotees, who regard them as direct manifestations of divine grace. One such account comes from Delhi resident Ravindra Joshi, also known as “Rabbu Dada,” who dedicated his life to the service of the saint. According to memoirs cited in Vijay Chhabaria and Dr. Deepak Patwardhan’s book Divya Anubhuti, Rabbu Dada was not only a devoted follower but also actively involved in temple construction and idol installation work across locations ranging from Taos in the United States to Bawaniya in Gujarat. Rabbu Dada first met Baba Neem Karoli during the summer of 1958 while visiting Nainital. Hearing stories of the saint’s miracles at Hanumangarhi, he felt a strong desire to meet him. For three days, Baba reportedly ignored him completely, neither speaking to him nor calling him. This behaviour left the devotee confused and restless. On the fourth day, Baba finally called him during evening prayers and remarked that the boy had been wondering why he was being ignored. “Slap” described as moment of spiritual awakening According to Rabbu Dada, Baba suddenly struck him on the head—an act he describes not as punishment but as a form of blessing. He claims that in that moment he experienced tears, mental stillness, and a sense of unity with the guru, feeling no separation between himself and the saint. Healing burn injury with a blanket Rabbu Dada also recounts several other miraculous incidents. Once, while frying puris in the kitchen, hot boiling ghee spilled onto his hand, causing severe burns. Before he could express the pain, Baba immediately asked if his hand was burnt. Upon confirmation, Baba placed his hand inside his blanket and pressed it, saying, “It is fine now, go.” According to the devotee, the pain and burning sensation disappeared instantly. Divine experiences and Uncanny predictions The devotee further recalls that Baba often consumed offerings from devotees throughout the day, tasting food prepared by different families as a gesture of blessing. He also recounts how his aunt, initially a devotee of Lord Krishna but sceptical of saints, reportedly saw Baba as Lord Krishna Himself, after which her doubts disappeared. Rabbu Dada describes another experience where Baba appeared to know about his personal habits without being told, reinforcing his belief in the saint’s omniscience. Bus accident incident during marriage journey In 1970, when Rabbu Dada’s marriage was arranged, Baba advised him to travel by train. However, he chose to travel by a private bus, which later met with an accident and overturned. Fortunately, no one suffered serious injuries. Later, Baba is said to have remarked humorously that he had to “protect everyone on the bus” since his instructions were not followed. Dream that turned into reality Rabbu Dada also recounts a dream in which he saw Baba standing near a staircase at a house in Allahabad. The next morning, he found Baba at the exact same location, an event he considers one of the most unforgettable moments of his life. Establishment of Kainchi Dham and later legacy After Baba’s passing, devotees installed his idol at Kainchi Dham. On June 15, 1976, the consecration ceremony (Pran Pratishtha) of the idol was performed with Vedic rituals. Kainchi Dham, located near Bhowali in Uttarakhand’s Nainital district, was established by Baba Neem Karoli in the 1960s along the banks of the Shipra River. It is now widely known for its spiritual significance and serene natural surroundings. Subsequently, temples dedicated to Baba were also established in Vrindavan, Lucknow, Delhi, Shimla and other locations. “Once I hold someone’s hand, I never leave them” According to Rabbu Dada, Baba Neem Karoli often assured devotees that he never abandons those he takes under his guidance. He considers the “blessing” he received after the famous slap as the greatest support of his life. As devotees recall, Baba would often say: “If I once hold someone’s hand, I never leave them.”

stories.title: Rainfall recorded in 10 cities across UP:Lucknow remains cloudy; storm and rain warning for all districts over next 3 days
stories.summary: The pre-monsoon rain spell has started in UP. Early Wednesday morning, Prayagraj, Meerut, Saharanpur, Gonda, and Bijnor experienced heavy rain with strong winds. The capital, Lucknow and the surrounding areas remained cloudy. The sun also appeared intermittently. However, due to humidity in the air, there is some relief from the heat. The Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an alert for thunderstorms, strong winds, and rain in all 75 districts of the state today. A warning for hailstones and lightning has been issued in some areas. According to the IMD, a new Western Disturbance will become active within 24 hours. This will intensify the pre-monsoon activity. The weather will remain similar for the next three days. Earlier, a storm with a speed of 90 (kmph) hit Bareilly late Wednesday night. There was heavy rainfall. Roads were waterlogged up to about 2 feet. Trees and hoardings fell in many places. As a precautionary measure, electricity was cut off in the entire city. Early morning, Noida-Ghaziabad and Sambhal had rain with strong winds. Lucknow scientist Atul Singh said- A new western disturbance is becoming active in UP. This will accelerate pre-monsoon activities. Thunderstorms and rain will continue till June 15-16. The monsoon will enter the state by its scheduled time, i.e., June 20. It will cover the entire UP within 10 days.

stories.title: UP govt schools to offer convent-style education soon:39 CM composite schools under construction; admissions from 2027 with smart classes
stories.summary: Do you want to educate your child in a good convent school, but hesitate seeing the skyrocketing fees? Then leave your worries behind. The UP government is going to make this dream of yours come true. 'CM Composite Schools' are now being opened in the state to provide world-class education like convents at very low fees. Here, there will be high-tech smart classes, science, robotics labs, and digital libraries. There will be professional teachers who can compete with private schools. Your child will get exactly the same environment as they would in convent schools. How CM Composite Schools will change the image of government schools, 39 CM Composite Schools are being built in the first phase Currently, in UP, there are separate schools for Primary, Upper Primary, and Secondary levels. However, in a Composite Model School, there will be classes from Pre-Primary (Nursery) to 12th grade. This means that primary, junior, high school, and intermediate education will be provided on the same campus. Currently, there is a plan to open 2 CM Composite Schools in every district of the state. After this, similar schools will be opened at the block level and then at the Nyay Panchayat level. The government has released a budget of 4500 crore rupees for this. In the first phase, work is underway to build one school each in 39 districts like Sitapur, Kanpur Dehat, Hardoi, Rae Bareli, Badaun, Gonda, Ayodhya, Bijnor, Muzaffarnagar, Ballia, Shravasti. The target is to start admissions in these schools from March 2027. Emphasis will be on practical knowledge instead of rote learning In these schools, education will be in English medium under the National Education Policy (NEP), 2020. However, the schools will be operated under the UP Board. The plan is to emphasise practical knowledge instead of rote learning in these schools. Students in these schools will also be trained in smart classes, digital libraries, Artificial Intelligence (AI), and robotics. Separate-level labs will also be built for students from Class 1 to 12 in the school. There will be modular Math and Science labs for primary classes. Separate modern labs for Physics, Chemistry, and Biology will be established for Classes 9 to 12. Language Center: Here, students will be able to learn regional languages like Awadhi, Braj, Bundelkhandi, and Bhojpuri, in addition to English, Hindi, and Sanskrit. Pronunciation, vocabulary, and communication skills will be enhanced through audio-visual technology. AI and Robotics Training: Robotic learning centers will be established in schools, where students will be given training related to robotics, AI, and automation. Additionally, attention will be paid to coding and skill development. Mid-Day Meal: There will be a modular kitchen for approximately 1300 children from pre-primary to class 8. Here, meals will be provided under the Mid-Day Meal Scheme. Children will be able to eat in the adjacent dining hall. Safety and Health: A CCTV control center will be established within the campus to monitor approximately 1500 students studying in the school. Meanwhile, the medical room will have facilities for 2 beds, an oxygen cylinder, a stretcher, and first aid. Children will also be given training for this. Now know how to get admission The academic session of CM Composite School will start every year from April 1, but the admission process will begin in March. Admission in these schools will primarily be based on lottery or merit. Rural, economically weaker, and local children will be given priority. For this, one will have to contact the District Basic Education Officer (BSA) office or the school. The process can also be completed through an online portal. Uniform: Through DBT, money for uniform, bag, shoes, etc., will be directly credited to the bank account. Parents will be able to purchase from the market. Fees: The fee structure will be similar to Kendriya Vidyalayas or there will be a nominal fee. How different will the teachers of CM Composite Schools be? To teach in these schools, the most qualified and experienced teachers already teaching in the education department will be screened. Additionally, the responsibility for new appointments has been entrusted to the newly formed UP Education Service Selection Commission. According to the rules of Basic Education Council schools, D.El.Ed (BTC)/ B.El.Ed will be mandatory for primary level (1 to 5), and passing TET/ CTET along with B.Ed will be mandatory for upper primary and secondary level (6 to 12). Teachers must have practical knowledge of operating digital tools and smart classes. For this, they will also be given special training. Under the Central Government's 'PM SHRI' scheme, Kendriya Vidyalayas, Navodaya Vidyalayas, and other government schools are being upgraded.

stories.title: SP plans to reuse Lok Sabha strategy in 2027 election:SC candidates may contest from general seats; MLAs unlikely to lose tickets
stories.summary: As preparations for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections gather pace, the Samajwadi Party (SP) has intensified its election planning. According to party sources, the first list of candidates has already been prepared, while work on the second list is underway. Most sitting MLAs are likely to retain their tickets in the first list. Discussions are continuing over the second list, with the party considering fielding Dalit candidates from general seats. SP is also said to be paying greater attention to reserved constituencies this time as it finalises its election strategy. Lok Sabha election formula will be adopted SP is eyeing PDA (Pichda, Dalit, Alpasankhyak - Backward, Dalit, Minority) votes. Among these, there is a special focus on the Dalit vote bank. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, SP increased its tally from 5 to 37 seats, leveraging this very vote bank. If we look at the votes received by SP in 2024 assembly seat-wise, it had a lead in 184 seats. In the Lok Sabha elections, SP made a new experiment by fielding Scheduled Caste (SC) candidates on 2 general seats. Awadhesh Prasad from Faizabad and Sunita Verma from Meerut were given tickets. The result was that despite the construction of the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya, BJP lost the Faizabad seat. Awadhesh Prasad registered a victory by more than 50 thousand votes. Similarly, the contest in Meerut was also very close. Arun Govil, who played Ram on screen, could only win the election by 10 thousand votes. BJP was trailing in 4 out of 5 assembly seats in Meerut. If SP succeeds in making inroads into this vote bank even in 2027, its chances of returning to power will increase. SP's eye on BSP's vote bank Senior journalist Rajendra Kumar says - SP will also try the formula of success achieved on Ayodhya seat in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections in the assembly elections. The party can field Dalit candidates on 40 to 50 general seats. Most of these seats will be in Western UP. Here, SP wants to win over the Dalit vote bank of BSP and Chandrashekhar's Azad Samaj Party. This vote bank earlier belonged to BSP, but it got divided after the defeat in the 2012 assembly elections. Winning on reserved seats forms the government There are 86 reserved seats in the UP Assembly. Of these, 84 seats are reserved for SC and 2 for Scheduled Tribes (ST). In the Lok Sabha elections, 17 seats are reserved for SC in the state. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, SP won 7 of these seats. One seat went to Congress. The history of UP has been such that whoever wins more than half of the reserved seats forms the government in UP. A dozen leaders are demanding tickets for their families Political experts believe that SP will not cut the tickets of its current MLAs, provided they are present in the party and have a strong hold in their assembly constituency. SP currently has 102 MLAs. Many MLAs and leaders want to get tickets for their family members. These include leaders from East to West UP. Whether family members will contest the election or the current MLAs, it has not been decided yet. The number of such seats is said to be around 12.

stories.title: Lucknow man kills younger brother, smashes head with cylinder:Drags body onto street after attack, dumps body outside, challenges onlookers
stories.summary: In Lucknow, an elder brother allegedly murdered his younger brother after the latter objected to him assaulting their parents. The accused repeatedly struck his brother on the head with a domestic LPG cylinder. He then dragged the blood-soaked victim by the leg and dumped him on the road. Shouting at bystanders, he allegedly said, “I have killed him. Let anyone do whatever they want now.” The victim’s uncle and local residents rushed him to the Trauma Centre, where doctors declared him dead. The incident took place around 3 pm on Sunday in Sector-3 of Jankipuram Extension. The deceased, Aryan Mishra (21), worked at a seed warehouse. Police have taken the accused elder brother, Abhishek Mishra (24), into custody. First 2 pictures Now the complete incident in detail Father said - he often used to assault in a state of intoxication Aryan’s father, Ramanand Mishra, works as a painting contractor. He said that his younger son Aryan worked in medicine supply at a seed warehouse in Daliganj, while his elder son Abhishek was unemployed. According to Ramanand, Abhishek frequently assaulted family members after consuming intoxicants. On Sunday morning, he first attacked him. The family somehow managed to escape and took shelter on the rooftop. Later, Ramanand and his wife prepared to leave for Yahiyaganj to purchase goods for their shop. During this time, Abhishek allegedly started beating his mother, Manju Mishra. He kicked her on the road. Local residents intervened and tried to stop him. When Aryan objected to the assault, Abhishek abused him and then attacked him with the gas cylinder. Both brothers first fought on the road Neighbour Shiv Poojan Mishra said that after the morning dispute, Ramanand left with his wife. However, the argument between the two brothers continued. A serious fight broke out on the road. Tenants living nearby and other residents intervened and separated the brothers. Abhishek was sent inside the house, while Aryan was taken into a neighbouring house adjoining their residence. However, Aryan later returned to Abhishek through the rooftop route, where another heated argument broke out between them. The neighbour said Abhishek was extremely aggressive during the confrontation. 'Abhishek was bloodthirsty' Abhishek allegedly struck Aryan on the head with the LPG cylinder, leaving him covered in blood and collapsing to the ground. Even then, his anger did not subside. He grabbed Aryan by the leg and dragged him onto the road. He then reportedly told residents, “I have killed him. Now do whatever you want.” Following the attack, Aryan’s uncle Parmanand, with the help of local residents, rushed him to the Trauma Centre in critical condition, where doctors declared him dead. Blood spread on the road Local residents said Aryan’s head had suffered severe injuries. He lay inside the house, drenched in blood and struggling for life. Blood had spread from inside the house onto the road outside. Police and forensic experts reached the scene and collected evidence as part of the investigation.

stories.title: Bihar woman accuses Ayodhya religious preacher of rape:Kathavachak and relatives booked; complainant alleges jewellery worth ₹10 lakh taken
stories.summary: A woman from Bihar has accused Ayodhya-based religious preacher Pawan Dev Maharaj (42) of rape, alleging that he brought her to Ayodhya on the pretext of taking her for Darshan at the Ram Temple, sexually assaulted her, and later conducted a sham marriage ceremony before abandoning her. The woman also alleged that Pawan Dev Maharaj and his family retained jewellery and valuables worth nearly ₹10 lakh and threatened her when she protested. Police registered an FIR on Saturday night based on the woman's complaint. The case pertains to the Bikapur Kotwali area, around 25 km from Ayodhya district headquarters. Woman claims they met during religious event in Bihar According to the complainant, she is a resident of Siwan district in Bihar. She is married and has two children. She alleged that she first met Pawan Dev Maharaj during a religious discourse (Katha) held in Champaran on July 10, 2023. The woman claimed that after the event, the storyteller took her phone number and the two remained in contact. "He used to send me photographs and videos of himself. Gradually, we became close," she alleged. 'Brought me to Ayodhya on promise of Ram temple Darshan' The woman alleged that Pawan Dev later visited Muzaffarpur in Bihar and invited her to accompany him to Ayodhya, promising VIP darshan at the Ram Temple. According to her complaint, she and her son travelled with him to Ayodhya on July 10, 2025. She claimed that he accommodated them at his home, where his mother and younger brother, Anand Mishra, were present. The complainant alleged that after his mother left for her parental home the next day, Pawan Dev sexually assaulted her. Alleged marriage promise after assault The woman stated that she protested and threatened to approach the police following the alleged assault. According to her, Pawan Dev apologised and promised to marry her. She further alleged that he kept her with him because he feared that an immediate police complaint and medical examination could expose the incident. Woman claims temple marriage took place The complainant said she informed her family about the alleged incident, but eventually trusted Pawan Dev's promise of marriage. According to her, the two underwent a marriage ceremony at Naka Hanumangarhi temple on August 17, 2025. She alleged that after the ceremony, she moved into his family home, where his mother, father Pandit Ramakant Shastri, and brother resided. The woman further claimed that she became pregnant during this period. Sent back to parental home, she alleges According to the complaint, on November 4, 2025, Pawan Dev and his younger brother allegedly forced her to return to her parental home. She claimed that when she resisted, she was told that remaining there could lead to police action and legal complications for the family. Jewellery worth ₹10 lakh allegedly retained The woman alleged that she had brought jewellery gifted by both her marital and parental families when she came to Ayodhya. However, she claimed she returned home with only a few clothes, while her jewellery and other valuables remained with the accused. She estimated the value of the jewellery at around ₹10 lakh. The complainant further alleged that Pawan Dev Maharaj and his father later visited her residence and assaulted her during an argument. She also accused them of threatening to kill her if she continued pursuing the matter. Woman says her life has been ruined The complainant stated that her first husband had already filed a divorce case against her. She said she now has neither employment nor a permanent place to live. "My life has been ruined. Either I should be accepted as a wife, or strict action should be taken against the accused," she said. Who is Pawan Dev Maharaj? Pawan Dev Maharaj is a resident of Malethu Kanak village in Ayodhya's Bikapur area. He describes himself as a disciple of renowned Kathavachak Devkinandan Thakur and has built a reputation in religious circles through public discourses over the past few years. On May 13, 2026, he was appointed National Spokesperson of the Karni Sena. He has since been associated with various social and religious issues linked to the organisation. His father, Pandit Ramakant Shastri, is a priest who performs religious rituals and ceremonies. Know about Ayodhya-based Kathavachak accused Pawan Dev Maharaj Police begin investigation Police officials said an FIR has been registered and all aspects of the allegations are being investigated. Authorities stated that further legal action will be taken based on available evidence, witness statements, and the findings of the investigation. Given the sensitive nature of the case, police said they are verifying all facts and claims made by both sides before proceeding further.

stories.title: Akhilesh Yadav alleges crores missing from Ram temple donations:Calls govt's silence suspicious, seeks court intervention
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav has alleged that crores of rupees from donations offered by devotees at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya have gone missing, calling it a matter of serious concern for worshippers worldwide. In a post on X on Sunday, Akhilesh claimed that a large amount of donation money collected at the temple could not be accounted for and demanded accountability from both the temple trust and the government. Akhilesh raises questions over missing donation funds Akhilesh wrote that the issue was highly sensitive for devotees of Lord Ram worldwide. "For worshippers of Lord Ram across the world, this is an extremely sensitive matter. Crores of rupees from the donations offered at the Ram Temple have reportedly gone missing." He said the alleged disappearance of such a large amount of money was a matter of grave concern and required a clear explanation from those responsible for managing the temple's affairs. Criticism of temple trust and government The Samajwadi Party chief also targeted the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust and the government over the issue. According to Akhilesh, the alleged disappearance of crores of rupees in donations has placed the temple trust in an embarrassing position. "The disappearance of crores of rupees is an extremely shameful situation for the temple trust. No one wants to come forward and offer an explanation." Seeks suo motu action by court Akhilesh urged the judiciary to take suo motu cognizance of the matter, arguing that it is directly linked to the faith of lakhs of devotees. He said the issue concerns the deep religious sentiments and trust that followers of Lord Ram place in the temple. Former minister claims ₹7.5 crore may have been stolen from Ram Temple donations Former Ayodhya MLA and ex-Minister of State for Forests and Entertainment Tax Pawan Pandey has claimed that between ₹5 crore and ₹7.5 crore may have been stolen from donation funds collected at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, Pandey challenged temple authorities to publicly deny the allegations if they were false and called for a thorough investigation into the matter. Pandey said that if no theft had occurred, Champat Rai, the general secretary of the temple trust, should come forward and categorically deny the allegations. "If there has been no theft, Champat Rai should come forward and swear in the name of Lord Ram that these allegations are false. If the claims are true, then an FIR should be registered," Pandey said. He added that it remains unclear for how long the alleged discrepancies may have been occurring and whether any members of the trust benefited from the missing funds. "An investigation should determine how long this has been happening and whether any trust members received the money," he said. How donation counting works at the Ram temple According to the established procedure at the Ram Temple, donations are counted by bank employees in the presence of trust representatives. The counting process is conducted under CCTV surveillance. After being counted, the donation amount is recorded in registers and stored in lockers located within the temple complex. The funds are then deposited in a bank the following day. The trust's primary account is maintained at the Ayodhya Dham branch of the State Bank of India. Audit process overseen by TCS The auditing of donation funds is reportedly monitored by Tata Consultancy Services (TCS). Details regarding donations received by the temple are generally shared during meetings of the temple trust. The last such disclosure was reportedly made in December 2025. Temple trust reported ₹4,575 crore in total receipts During a meeting of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust held on December 13, 2025, trust officials reportedly stated that total receipts had reached ₹4,575 crore. According to figures presented at the meeting: Ram Temple receives more than ₹1 crore in donations daily The consecration ceremony of Lord Ram Lalla at the Ayodhya temple took place on January 22, 2024. Over the past two years, the temple has emerged as one of India's largest religious destinations. Its primary sources of income are donations from devotees and interest earned on bank deposits. According to a report cited from the Global Wealth Index 2026, the temple's assets include: The report estimated the temple's total asset value at between ₹6,000 crore and ₹8,000 crore. Trust formed following Supreme Court verdict The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust was established by the Central Government on February 5, 2020, following the Supreme Court's verdict in the Ayodhya land dispute case. The government appointed nine founding members, including senior advocate Keshav Parasaran. Later that day, the then receiver of the acquired Ram Janmabhoomi land and divisional commissioner, Manoj Kumar Mishra, formally transferred charge of the trust's assets and bank accounts to trust member Vimalendra Mohan Pratap Mishra. First trust meeting held in February 2020 The trust's first formal meeting took place on February 20, 2020. During the meeting: No response from trust chairman Dainik Bhaskar reported that it attempted to contact trust chairman Nritya Gopal Das for a response to the allegations raised by Akhilesh Yadav. However, the trust chairman did not answer the call. 'Government's silence is suspicious' The Samajwadi Party leader further questioned the government's response, stating that its silence over the allegations was suspicious. "The government's silence is suspicious." He maintained that the matter deserves a thorough inquiry and transparent clarification because of its significance to the wider Hindu community and devotees of Lord Ram around the world. As of now, no response from the temple trust or the government was mentioned in Akhilesh Yadav's statement.

stories.title: Bus crushes infant, two women in Ghazipur:Mother, aunt killed on bike; father and toddler survive horrific crash
stories.summary: Three members of a family, including a four-month-old infant, were killed after a private bus allegedly rammed into their motorcycle in Uttar Pradesh's Ghazipur district on Saturday. The victims were identified as Kajal Giri (20), her four-month-old daughter Sejal, and Ritu Giri (22), Kajal's sister and the sister-in-law of the motorcycle rider. The child's father, Prateek Giri, and his one-and-a-half-year-old daughter, Shreya survived the crash. Police have arrested the bus driver and seized the vehicle. Horrific crash near Sharifpur underpass The accident took place near the Sharifpur underpass on the Saidpur–Bahariyabad Highway, around 35 kilometres from the Ghazipur district headquarters. According to police, Prateek Giri (25) was returning to his home in Mirzapur from his in-laws' house in Azamgarh. Riding on a single motorcycle with him were his wife Kajal, daughters Shreya and Sejal, and his sister-in-law Ritu Giri. Two bags were also hanging from the bike. Police said the speeding private bus hit the motorcycle while taking a turn near the underpass. The impact threw Prateek and toddler Shreya away from the motorcycle. Kajal, infant Sejal, and Ritu fell beneath the front wheel of the bus, which ran over them, killing all three on the spot. Pictures of the accident Human remains scattered across the road The collision was so severe that pieces of flesh, broken bangles, and blood were scattered across the road. Police personnel who reached the scene collected the remains and sent the bodies for postmortem examination. Due to the condition of the infant's remains, officers reportedly used a polythene bag to transport the body. The injured were rushed to a nearby hospital for treatment. Family was returning from in-laws' home Prateek Giri, a resident of Shahpur village in Mirzapur's Adalhat area, had travelled to Azamgarh to drop off his ailing mother-in-law after her treatment in Varanasi. His wife Kajal, younger daughter Sejal, elder daughter Shreya, and sister-in-law Ritu were already staying at the in-laws' residence in Nagwa Mathiya village. On Saturday morning, the family left for Mirzapur on a motorcycle. About 60 kilometers into the journey, the fatal collision occurred. Driver caught by bystanders Following the crash, the bus driver allegedly attempted to flee. Bystanders chased and caught him before assaulting him. Police later intervened and took him into custody. Saidpur Station House Officer Rajesh Tripathi and a police team arrived at the scene and shifted the injured to the Community Health Centre in Saidpur. Prateek was later referred to the district hospital with serious injuries, including a fractured arm and chest injuries. Toddler Shreya was discharged after treatment and handed over to relatives. Witnesses said the frightened child continued crying after the accident until female police personnel comforted her while waiting for family members to arrive. Family devastated by triple tragedy After receiving information about the accident, Prateek's father, Kundan Giri, and brother-in-law Pankaj reached the hospital. Relatives were inconsolable after learning of the deaths of Kajal, Sejal, and Ritu. Kundan Giri said both his sons, Pankaj and Prateek, work in Mumbai in the tailoring and embroidery business. He said Prateek had returned from Mumbai on May 9 to help arrange medical treatment for his mother-in-law. "Pankaj has no children. He is still in Mumbai and has been informed about his wife's death. He is on his way back. Our entire family has been shattered," Kundan said. Police investigating bus owner Police said the bus was travelling from Mohammadabad in Ghazipur to Varanasi when the accident occurred. SHO Rajesh Tripathi confirmed that three of the five people riding the motorcycle were killed, while Prateek sustained serious injuries. "The bus driver has been arrested and the vehicle has been seized. Efforts are being made to contact the bus owner. All three bodies have been sent for postmortem examination," he said. The investigation into the accident is ongoing.

stories.title: Gorakhpur to hold boxing team trials on June 8:Players from four districts compete for spots in Saharanpur championship
stories.summary: The process of selecting the Gorakhpur Division team for the State Coordination Sub-Junior Boxing Championship has begun, with district and divisional-level trials scheduled to identify the best boxers across various weight categories. The Regional Sports Office announced the trial schedule on Saturday. District and Divisional trials scheduled at Regional Sports Stadium According to the Regional Sports Office, the selection trials will be conducted on Monday at the Regional Sports Stadium in Gorakhpur. District-level trials will begin at 8 a.m., where athletes will compete for a place in the divisional selection round. Players who perform well at the district stage will advance to the divisional trials. The divisional selection trials for the boys' category will start at 11 a.m. Boxers from four districts to participate In addition to Gorakhpur, players from Deoria, Kushinagar, and Maharajganj districts will participate in the divisional trials. A divisional team will be selected based on performances in various weight categories. The selected athletes will represent Gorakhpur Division at the upcoming state-level championship in Saharanpur. State Championship schedule The State Coordination Sub-Junior Boxing Championship for the boys' category will be held in Saharanpur from June 10 to June 13. Meanwhile, the divisional selection trials for the girls' category will also take place at the Regional Sports Stadium on June 8, beginning at 11:30 a.m. The girls' state-level championship is scheduled to be held in Saharanpur from June 15 to June 18. Eligibility criteria Only athletes born between January 1, 2012, and December 31, 2013, will be eligible to participate in the competition. Players attending the trials must report to the stadium at the designated time and bring all required documents. Officials said the final selection will be made based on the athletes' performance during the trials and in accordance with the prescribed competition rules.

stories.title: 10 days later, only bones found in Lucknow:Family awaits DNA results after daughter's body could not be recovered
stories.summary: A heartbreaking case has emerged in Lucknow, where only two bones and some hair believed to belong to a 19-year-old BSc student from Sitapur were recovered nearly 10 days after her alleged murder. The remains were discovered in a forested area of Lucknow's Bakshi Ka Talab (BKT) region on Saturday. The victim's father identified the belongings found at the scene—including clothes and slippers—as those of his daughter. The remains have been preserved and sent for DNA testing to confirm the identity. Father: "We never got our daughter's body" The grieving father said his daughter had been abducted and murdered, but even after 10 days, the family was unable to recover her body. "My daughter was kidnapped and killed. I don't know what all she went through. Ten days after the murder, we still did not get her body. Only two bones and some hair were found. Had the police acted in time, at least we could have received her body and performed her last rites." According to him, the police preserved the bones and hair samples after the victim's alleged boyfriend led investigators to the location. The father visited the postmortem facility but was ultimately handed only a small packet containing some of his daughter's hair for the funeral rites. Student went missing on May 25 The victim was a 19-year-old first-year BSc student from Sitapur district's Sandana area. According to her father, she studied with Vishal Pal and his sister Shivani Pal, both residents of Saraiya village. The father alleged that Vishal developed a relationship with his daughter through his sister and eventually lured her away. On May 25, the student left home for college as usual but never returned. The family later suspected that Vishal and his sister had taken her away. Her mobile phone was switched off, adding to the family's concern. The father approached the police, but he alleges that no immediate action was taken. An FIR was eventually registered by Sandana Police Station on May 28. Only two bones and hair recovered Police said that because the body had allegedly remained in a forested area for around 10 days, animals had consumed most of the remains. When investigators reached the location, only: were found. The bones were taken to the postmortem facility, where X-rays were conducted before they were preserved for forensic examination. The remains have now been sent for DNA testing to determine whether they belong to the victim. Medical experts said the limited remains may make it difficult to conclusively determine the exact cause of death. Family alleges police deleted photos The victim's father claimed that police collected the remains in a cloth at the scene. According to him, when family members attempted to photograph the recovered remains, police officers took their mobile phone and deleted the images and videos. He said no satisfactory explanation was provided for the action. The recovered evidence was then transported to the postmortem facility. Hair handed over for last rites Following the postmortem process, the father said he was given a small polythene packet containing some of his daughter's hair to perform her last rites. Some hair samples were retained for forensic testing, while the bones were preserved as DNA evidence. The father said he was not handed any other remains recovered from the site. "If the police had acted in time, perhaps we would at least have received her body for a proper funeral," he said. Father says, ‘Police took him to Lucknow after 10 days’ The father alleged that despite his daughter disappearing on May 25, authorities failed to take prompt action. He said the family staged protests and demonstrations after receiving no response for five days. According to him, the protest continued for three days before being called off following assurances from local police officials. The next day, nearly 10 days after the disappearance, police brought him to Lucknow. "In Sitapur, I was told that my daughter had been found. But when I reached Lucknow, they took me directly to a forest. There, I saw her clothes trapped in bushes. Her slippers, bones, and hair were also there, but her body was missing." After he identified the belongings, police took possession of the bones and hair for forensic examination. Accused boyfriend shot in leg during alleged escape attempt On June 6, a team from Sandana Police Station took accused Vishal Pal to identify evidence related to the case. According to police, while near an orchard along the road in Rampur Madhia village, Vishal asked to stop to relieve himself. Police allege that he then snatched a pistol from a constable and attempted to flee after opening fire. Officers returned fire, striking him in the right leg. He was apprehended and admitted to a hospital for treatment. Accused confesses to murder, police claim During interrogation, police said Vishal admitted that he and the student were in a relationship. According to investigators, he told police that the student had become pregnant and was around three months pregnant. He allegedly claimed she had begun pressuring him to marry her. Police say Vishal confessed that he took her to a secluded location on his motorcycle and strangled her to death in an attempt to avoid marriage. The investigation remains ongoing, and authorities are awaiting forensic and DNA test results to establish the identity of the recovered remains and strengthen the case against the accused.

stories.title: Gym trainer accused of converting businessman's son:Name changed after Nikah; FIR filed against 10 including three clerics
stories.summary: A case involving alleged religious conversion has surfaced in Shamli district, where the son of a wealthy pharmaceutical businessman was allegedly converted from Hinduism to Islam by a woman gym trainer, according to a police complaint filed by his father. The complaint alleges that the 25-year-old trainer, Chandni Qureshi, developed a relationship with the businessman’s son, Ayush Malik, and later facilitated his religious conversion and marriage under Islamic rites. Police have registered an FIR against Chandni, six of her family members, and three clerics on charges including alleged forced conversion and extortion. Authorities have begun an investigation, and Chandni Qureshi and her father have been taken into custody for questioning. Businessman's son allegedly converted, given new name According to police, 27-year-old Ayush Malik, the only son of local pharmaceutical trader Devraj Malik, was allegedly converted to Islam and given the name "Rehman." Police said Ayush reportedly grew a beard, began wearing a skullcap, and was seen attending a mosque. Photographs that have surfaced allegedly show him offering prayers at a mosque and wearing traditional Muslim attire while sitting at his medical store. The developments triggered protests from local Hindu organizations, which threatened demonstrations outside the gym trainer's residence. First 3 pictures FIR filed against 10 people Following the controversy, Devraj Malik filed a police complaint on Saturday evening against: The complaint alleges that Ayush was subjected to religious conversion and that the accused extorted money from him over several years. Malik further alleged that a forged nikahnama (Islamic marriage document) was prepared and that pressure was exerted on the family to convert. The complaint also claims threats were issued, including alleged threats to kill Ayush if he refused to embrace Islam. How the relationship began According to police, the relationship dates back nearly five years. Ayush Malik, who holds a Bachelor of Pharmacy degree and runs a medical store, reportedly began visiting a local gym known as Qureshi Plus Gym. Chandni Qureshi, a resident of Qureshi Basti in Shamli, worked there as a trainer. Investigators say the two developed a close relationship, and approximately four years ago an Islamic marriage ceremony was allegedly conducted in secret. Police claim Ayush began noticeably changing his appearance around six months ago, growing a beard and increasingly participating in Islamic religious practices. Video by Hindu religious leader brought matter to public attention The case gained wider attention on June 4 after Swami Yashveer, head of a yoga and spiritual center in Muzaffarnagar, released a video discussing the matter. In the video, he alleged that the son of the owner of Bharat Medical Store had been influenced by Chandni Qureshi and that the Malik family was facing pressure related to religious conversion. Following the video's circulation, several Hindu organizations began protesting and demanded action. Father denies family converted Speaking to the media, Devraj Malik denied reports that his entire family had converted. "I and my wife remain Hindus. We visit the Hanuman temple every morning and evening for worship," he said. Malik alleged that his son's conversion was orchestrated by Chandni Qureshi, members of her family, and clerics associated with a mosque near Azad Chowk. He claimed that psychological pressure was exerted on Ayush over several years and that he was ultimately compelled to adopt Islam. Police investigation underway Shamli Superintendent of Police NP Singh said a case has been registered and an investigation is underway. Police are examining the allegations made in the FIR, including claims of forced religious conversion, extortion, and coercion. Authorities have not yet announced any arrests, and the allegations remain under investigation. The case has generated significant local attention and has become the latest religious conversion-related controversy to emerge in western Uttar Pradesh.

stories.title: Varanasi history-sheeter Anil Yadav dies by suicide:Accused in over 24 cases, gangster once carried ₹50,000 reward
stories.summary: A history-sheeter from Varanasi's Luxa police station area, Anil Yadav alias Patti, allegedly died by suicide on Sunday morning after hanging himself at his residence. Anil, who had a criminal history sheet opened against him and was once carrying a reward of ₹50,000 on his arrest, was facing more than two dozen criminal cases across various police stations in Varanasi. Police reached the spot after receiving information about the incident and sent the body for postmortem examination. An investigation is underway. Alleged domestic dispute before death According to police, Anil Yadav, a resident of Aurangabad locality, returned home around 2 a.m. on Saturday night in an intoxicated condition. A dispute reportedly broke out between him and his wife over an unspecified issue. Following the argument, he allegedly hanged himself inside the house. The incident caused shock and grief among family members. Police suspect domestic discord Luxa Station House Officer Raju Kumar said preliminary findings suggest that the incident may be linked to domestic discord. "At first glance, the matter appears to be related to a family dispute. However, all angles are being investigated to ascertain the exact reason behind the suicide," he said. Police are questioning family members, though officials said relatives have not yet been able to provide clear information regarding the circumstances leading to the incident. Accused in student murder case Anil Yadav was also accused in the murder of a student from Ghazipur studying at Vidyapeeth, who was killed in the Siddhagiri Bagh area. Due to his criminal activities, authorities had previously announced a reward of ₹50,000 for information leading to his arrest. More than two dozen criminal cases registered According to police records, Anil Yadav alias Patti had more than 24 criminal cases registered against him at police stations including Luxa, Dashashwamedh, Sigra, and Shivpur. The cases included serious charges such as murder, robbery, and other violent crimes. Police officials said he had been released from jail a few months ago and had since been living at home. Postmortem report awaited The body has been sent for postmortem examination, and police are awaiting the report. Officials said the exact circumstances surrounding the death will become clear only after the postmortem findings and completion of the investigation. For now, legal proceedings are underway, and police continue to examine all aspects of the case.

stories.title: Women break down as demolition continues at Sambhal:Plead to save area's only mosque; administration say govt land
stories.summary: The anti-encroachment operation at the Mustafa Qadri Mosque entered its second day on Sunday, with the Sambhal administration continuing demolition work on what it says is an illegal structure erected on government land. A video that surfaced during the administration operation shows women and young girls from the Muslim community weeping and pleading with officials to spare the mosque. Folding her hands before the administration, one woman said, This is the only mosque in our village. We humbly request that it not be demolished. We have done nothing wrong. We have no objection to temples or any other religious places and respect all faiths. We only ask that our mosque be allowed to remain. Please do not destroy it. Officials said nearly 50 per cent of the structure was demolished on Saturday, and the remaining portion is expected to be removed on Sunday. First 3 pictures ‘Mosque built on cemetery land’, say administration The mosque is located in Kaserua village in the Nakhasa area of Sambhal district. According to the administration, the structure had been built on land officially recorded as a graveyard. Following orders from the Tehsildar Court, authorities launched an eviction drive to free approximately 120 square metres of government land from encroachment. The front portion of the mosque and several pillars have already been demolished. A 55-foot minaret was also pulled down using a crane. Senior district officials, including the District Magistrate and Superintendent of Police, were present during the operation. Posters and Flag recovered during demolition Officials said posters carrying the message "I Love Mohammad" and a green flag were recovered from the first floor of the mosque. Sambhal Superintendent of Police KK Bishnoi stated that action would be taken against those responsible for printing and displaying such posters. Court ordered eviction after appeal failed The Tehsildar Court passed an eviction order against the mosque committee on April 21. The committee later challenged the order before the District Magistrate's court. However, no stay order was granted, allowing the administration to proceed with the demolition. Tehsildar Dhirendra Kumar Singh subsequently formed a special team for the operation. Naib Tehsildar Deepak Kumar Jurel was appointed in charge of the demolition drive. The administration deployed four JCB machines, dumpers, tractors, and around 20 sanitation workers with support from the Revenue Department, Sambhal Municipality, and Sirsi Nagar Panchayat. Other encroachments also found on government land Revenue records show that plot number 409 is officially designated as graveyard land. Authorities claim that around 120 square metres of this land were occupied by the mosque. Three residential houses have also allegedly been constructed on the same plot. Officials further stated that: Villagers say Mosque is centuries old Mosque caretaker Zakir Hussain said the mosque is several hundred years old and was rebuilt around 20–25 years ago at a cost exceeding ₹5 million (₹50 lakh). Villagers alleged that their arguments were not adequately heard during proceedings before the Tehsildar Court. Resident Javed said villagers had not received advance notice of the demolition. "We only learned about it in the morning. Had we been informed a few days earlier, it would have been different. This is a very old mosque. We have been offering prayers here since the time of our elders." He added that the mosque predates two land-consolidation exercises conducted in the area. According to him, around 300 worshippers attend Friday prayers at the two-storey mosque. The village population is approximately 1,000, of whom nearly 500 are Muslims. Mosque committee failed to produce evidence, says Tehsildar Tehsildar Dhirendra Kumar Singh said the administration acted after receiving complaints seeking protection of graveyard land. According to him, an investigation found that the mosque had been constructed on cemetery land. Action was initiated under Section 67 of the Revenue Code, and the mosque committee was given a full opportunity to present its case. "However, the committee could not provide any documents or evidence proving that the mosque stood on private land. The court therefore passed an eviction order," Singh said. FIR Registered Earlier This Year In January 2026, an FIR was registered against seven individuals based on a complaint filed by a revenue official. The accused were alleged to have submitted misleading facts and documents in an attempt to have the land declared as Waqf property and to facilitate illegal occupation of village community land. Officials have said the campaign against encroachments on government land will continue and that future actions will be based on revenue records. Previous demolition actions in Sambhal The Sambhal administration has carried out several similar operations in recent months. According to officials: Religious structures removed Highway and Urban encroachments Other actions The latest demolition at Kaserua village has once again drawn attention to Sambhal's ongoing campaign against alleged encroachments on public land, particularly those involving religious structures.

stories.title: Premanand's favorite Johnny-Jojo found:Talking teddy bears stayed locked in suitcase; owner credits Banke Bihari for reunion
stories.summary: The famous talking teddy bear characters Johnny and Jojo, known for making spiritual leader Premanand Maharaj laugh during a memorable interaction, were reunited with their owner after going missing for nearly 24 hours in Vrindavan. The teddy bears, used by Jaipur-based ventriloquist Rahul Mishra in his performances, were accidentally left behind in a suitcase inside an e-rickshaw after a religious pilgrimage around Vrindavan. Their recovery came after a day-long search involving both police and local efforts. Read how Johnny, Jojo, and Rahul Mishra, who were separated, were reunited First, read the conversation with Rahul Mishra, then with Johnny Q: How did Johnny and Jojo go missing? Rahul Mishra: We were performing the Vrindavan Parikrama with Haridas Maharaj and entertaining people along the route through Johnny and Jojo's performances. After completing the Parikrama, we boarded an e-rickshaw to return to our hotel. The suitcase carrying Johnny and Jojo was with us. We reached near our hotel around 1 a.m. on the night between Thursday and Friday. In a hurry, I paid the fare and got down but forgot the suitcase in the e-rickshaw. The driver drove away before we realized it. We called out to him, but he could not hear us. Q: Whom did you approach for help, and how were they found? Rahul Mishra: We searched for the e-rickshaw driver throughout the night but couldn't find him. Then we filed a complaint with the police, who formed a search team. Our manager suggested that while the police were doing their job, we should continue searching as well. So we all joined the effort. Finally, around 1:30 a.m. on the night between Friday and Saturday, we found the e-rickshaw driver right in front of the Banke Bihari Temple. By Banke Bihari Ji's grace, Johnny and Jojo were found within 24 hours Q: Do you believe your prayer to Banke Bihari Ji was answered? Rahul Mishra: Yes. Even the local police station in-charge told us to have faith in Banke Bihari Ji and assured us that Johnny and Jojo would be found within a day. That's exactly what happened. Q: Where had the e-rickshaw driver kept the suitcase? Rahul Mishra: I don't know the exact location, but the driver took me deep into a forested area. There was a small hut where he had kept the suitcase under a bed. He then returned it to me. Q: What would you like to say to the Vrindavan Police? Rahul Mishra: I would simply like to thank them. The police provided tremendous support in helping us find Johnny and Jojo. All three of us are very grateful. QA with Johnny Q: Johnny, where had you gone? Johnny: (laughing) Oh sir, what can I say? I didn't even get water. Q: Were you missing for 24 hours? Johnny: Yes, I stayed inside that suitcase for 24 hours. It was the first time something like that happened. Q: Did you get anything to eat or drink? Johnny: No, I got neither food nor water. Q: What did you say to Banke Bihari Ji while you were inside the suitcase? Johnny: I prayed to Banke Bihari Ji and asked him to get me out of that place. Then suddenly my boss arrived and rescued me. Q: Are you fine now? Johnny: Yes, now I am completely healthy and fit. How Johnny and Jojo make people laugh Johnny and Jojo may appear to be ordinary teddy bear characters, but the real talent lies in Rahul Mishra's ventriloquism skills. He speaks without visibly moving his lips, creating the illusion that the voices are coming directly from the teddy bears. This art form is known as ventriloquism, in which the performer projects speech in a way that makes it seem as though a puppet or dummy is speaking independently. Meeting Premanand Maharaj a year ago About a year ago, Johnny and Jojo interacted with Premanand Maharaj in Vrindavan. During the conversation, the spiritual leader laughed continuously and remarked: "How do these toys speak on their own? This is an amazing art form." Rahul later said that Premanand Maharaj rewarded Johnny and Jojo with ₹500 each as a token of appreciation. He also honored Rahul and offered him prasad. According to Rahul, devotees gathered around him afterward and said they had rarely seen Premanand Maharaj laugh so much. Rahul Mishra's journey from theatre to ventriloquism Rahul Mishra, a resident of Jaipur, began his career in theatre. However, due to limited earning opportunities, he launched a YouTube channel in 2015. Friends gifted him a puppet, which became the basis for his early videos. His content later went viral on TikTok, but his real breakthrough came after he refined his ventriloquism skills and began performing on larger platforms. Rahul has appeared on the set of Bigg Boss and showcased his talent on India's Got Talent. Today, Johnny and Jojo remain among the most recognizable ventriloquist characters in India, and their brief disappearance in Vrindavan has added yet another memorable chapter to their journey.
