stories.title: Aparna remembers Prateek Yadav on his birthday:Daughter played 'Happy Birthday' on piano
stories.summary: Twenty-five days after the death of Prateek Yadav, the younger son of Mulayam Singh Yadav and stepbrother of Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, his wife Aparna Yadav paid an emotional tribute to him on what would have been his birthday. Aparna shared a photograph with Prateek and their younger daughter Padmaja on Facebook, writing, "As you always said, you would stay young forever." Prateek (38) died of a cardiac arrest in Lucknow on May 13. He would have celebrated his birthday on June 7. Their elder daughter, Prathama, remembered her father by playing the tune of "Happy Birthday" on a white piano that Prateek had gifted her. See 3 pictures Family continues to remember Prateek Apart from the Facebook post, Aparna also shared an Instagram story featuring Prateek participating in a car-racing event. Earlier, younger daughter Padmaja had got a tattoo inked on her arm depicting her father embracing her affectionately. The artwork shows Prateek holding his daughter close to his chest. Funeral and Thirteenth-day rituals Prateek Yadav passed away at the age of 38 on May 13. His last rites were performed on May 14 at Baikunth Dham crematorium in Lucknow. The funeral pyre was lit by his father-in-law, Arvind Singh Bisht. On May 16, his ashes were immersed at the VVIP Ghat in Haridwar. Aparna travelled to Uttarakhand with her daughters on a chartered flight. Aditya Yadav, son of Shivpal Singh Yadav, accompanied the family. The 13th-day Hindu ritual was held on May 25 at Aparna's residence on Vikramaditya Marg in Lucknow. Aparna personally served food to family members, including Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav. Witnesses said she became emotional when mourners raised slogans of "Prateek Bhaiya Amar Rahein", and tears welled up in her eyes. Among those who attended the ceremony were Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, who offered condolences to the family, along with Shivpal Yadav, Dimple Yadav, Rajya Sabha MP Sudhanshu Trivedi, folk singer Malini Awasthi, and actor Rajpal Yadav. Several parts of Lucknow also displayed condolence hoardings in memory of Prateek. Postmortem confirmed cardiac arrest According to the postmortem report, Prateek Yadav died due to cardiac arrest. Doctors at Lucknow Medical College found a significant number of blood clots in his lungs. The clots caused both his heart and lungs to stop functioning, leading to his death. Prateek had been admitted to a private hospital in Lucknow in critical condition on April 30. He showed signs of improvement after three days and reportedly returned home without completing treatment. Doctors later revealed that he was suffering from pulmonary embolism, a serious condition in which blood clots block arteries in the lungs, disrupting blood circulation. Educated in Britain, stayed away from politics Prateek was the son of Mulayam Singh Yadav's second wife, Sadhana Gupta. Sadhana Gupta was first married to Chandra Prakash Gupta in 1986, and Prateek was born in 1987. Following their divorce in 1990, Sadhana grew close to Mulayam Singh Yadav. In 2003, Mulayam married Sadhana and publicly acknowledged Prateek as his son. Prateek studied at University of Leeds and remained largely away from active politics. He was involved in real estate and fitness-related businesses. He married Aparna Yadav in 2012 after a long courtship. The couple had two daughters. Brief separation before reconciliation Earlier this year, on January 19, Prateek unexpectedly announced his decision to divorce Aparna, alleging that she had made his life difficult. However, the couple reconciled just nine days later. Sharing a photograph with Aparna on Instagram, Prateek wrote, “All is Good.” A love story that began in their teens Prateek and Aparna's relationship began in 2001 when they first met at a cultural event in Lucknow. Aparna, then around 13 or 14 years old, performed a song on stage, which reportedly caught Prateek's attention. The two met again at a family function and exchanged email addresses. Their friendship gradually developed through regular email conversations, and Prateek eventually expressed his feelings through an email. With the consent of both families, the couple got engaged in 2011 and married in a grand ceremony in Saifai in 2012. Today, as family members continue to mourn his untimely death, Prateek Yadav's birthday has become a moment of remembrance, marked by emotional tributes from his wife and daughters.

stories.title: After Atiq-Mukhtar era, young gangs emerge in UP:Shankar Pandey and Robin Singh among rising names
stories.summary: The decline of traditional mafia networks led by figures such as Atiq Ahmed and Mukhtar Ansari has not ended organised crime in Uttar Pradesh. Instead, a new generation of young gang leaders is emerging, operating through social media, contract killings, and extortion rackets that now stretch beyond the state's borders. Recent investigations into high-profile murders and extortion cases suggest that several youth-led gangs from Uttar Pradesh are increasingly involved in organised criminal activities across India. Today, in 'Sunday Big Story', we understand this new syndicate of crime flourishing in UP Two major cases linked to Uttar Pradesh gangs Case 1: UP youths accused in killing of West Bengal CM's aide On May 6, 2026, the day West Bengal election results were announced, Chandranath Rath, personal assistant to Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, was shot dead in Kolkata. When the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) took over the probe, investigators traced the conspiracy to Uttar Pradesh. The agency arrested Rajkumar Singh from Muzaffarnagar, Naveen Singh from Ballia, Vikas Mishra from Lucknow, and Mayank and Vicky from the Buxar border region. All the accused are between 20 and 28 years old and allegedly operated as a professional contract-killing gang. Case 2: 'King of Ghazipur' accused in hotelier's Sson's murder On May 29, luxury hotel owner Vinod Rai's son, Vineet Rai, was shot dead in broad daylight in Ghazipur. Police said Vineet had been receiving extortion threats demanding ₹1 crore. The alleged mastermind behind the murder is Shankar Pandey, leader of the notorious "Katra Gang." Pandey, who projected himself on social media as the "King of Ghazipur," frequently posted Instagram reels featuring convoys of SUVs, including Scorpio and Fortuner vehicles. One of his associates, Kamlesh Bind, was later killed in a police encounter. Lawrence Bishnoi gang's influence visible across UP Investigators and police officials say local gangs in Uttar Pradesh are increasingly influenced by the network of gangster Lawrence Bishnoi. Three recent examples highlight this trend: Shooter Jeetu killed in STF encounter In February 2025, the Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force (STF) gunned down Lawrence Bishnoi gang shooter Jitendra Singh alias Jeetu in Noida. Jeetu was wanted for the murder of a Ghaziabad businessman and had absconded after being released on parole. Police alleged that he was carrying out contract killings on behalf of gangster Rohit Godara. Baba Siddique murder case The two shooters accused of killing veteran Maharashtra politician Baba Siddique in Mumbai — Shivkumar Gautam and Dharmaraj Kashyap — were residents of Bahraich district in Uttar Pradesh. Investigators believe both men were attempting to establish themselves within larger organized crime networks linked to the Bishnoi gang. Extortion demands in Bishnoi gang's name Several high-profile extortion threats have also been issued in the name of the Bishnoi gang. Targets reportedly included: Social media becoming a recruitment tool for new-age gangs Police say WhatsApp and Instagram have become major platforms for young criminals seeking quick notoriety and easy money. Investigators have found instances where gang members allegedly offered assault services for as little as ₹500 to ₹1,000 through social media networks. Uttar Pradesh Police is now monitoring and tracing such accounts. Pincode 221715 gang A group of youths from Belthara Road in Ballia formed a gang named after the area's postal code — "221715." According to police, gang members allegedly accepted payments ranging from ₹500 to ₹1,000 to assault individuals. Internal rivalry later led to the murder of one of the group's members, Ayush Yadav. AK-47 and Red gangs Along the Gorakhpur–Maharajganj border, gangs known as the "AK-47 Gang" and the "Red Gang" have gained notoriety. Members reportedly display AK-47 insignia on their vehicles and motorcycles. A violent gang war between the groups in October 2025 led to extensive firing, after which police arrested 28 youths. Kannauj and Auraiya gangs Authorities have also identified several youth gangs in central Uttar Pradesh, including the "Bichchu Gang" in Kannauj and the "Mada Gang" and "Boss Gang" in Auraiya. Police records indicate that members of these groups have been linked to serious crimes, including murder. After the elimination of Atiq Ahmed's 'Inter State Gang-227', UP Police and administration have started re-listing gangs. Former DGP said - Repeat offenders are eliminated in 'Yogi Raj' Former Uttar Pradesh DGP Brijlal says police are actively tracking and dismantling these emerging gangs. According to him, the gangs that operated in the past were far more dangerous, while today's gangs tend to seek visibility and influence through social media. "Police are taking strict action against those involved in criminal activities on the ground. Many offenders are unable to continue their operations after committing a major crime because law enforcement acts swiftly against them. Those who repeatedly engage in criminal activities eventually face decisive action under the Yogi government. There are several examples of this," he said. A new criminal ecosystem While Uttar Pradesh has witnessed the decline of several traditional mafia syndicates, investigators say a new criminal ecosystem is emerging — one driven by social media influence, young recruits, contract killings, and interstate extortion networks. The challenge for law enforcement now is not only dismantling established gangs but also preventing the rapid rise of digitally connected criminal groups that are increasingly expanding their reach beyond Uttar Pradesh.

stories.title: UP Monsoon delayed, likely to arrive by June 24:Temperature set to rise sharply as heatwave intensifies; Maharajganj sees heavy rain
stories.summary: The spell of storms and rain across Uttar Pradesh over the past two weeks has finally subsided, with temperatures now rising sharply across the state. On Sunday, clear skies and bright sunshine were recorded in all 75 districts. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has said that with the western disturbance weakening, there are no immediate signs of rainfall. In the next 24 hours, temperatures are expected to rise by 5–6°C, potentially reaching 47–48°C in parts of the state. A heatwave warning has been issued for the next three days starting June 9. According to the IMD, relief is likely only after June 11, when pre-monsoon showers may begin again. The monsoon, however, is expected to arrive in Uttar Pradesh around June 24—4 to 6 days later than usual—and is likely to cover the entire state within 10 days of its onset. Earlier on Saturday, several districts including Varanasi, Kaushambi, Mau, Ballia and Ghazipur witnessed heavy rain, strong winds of up to 50 kmph, and lightning activity. Gorakhpur also experienced a dust storm that brought temporary relief from the heat. In Amethi, a tragic incident occurred when a mud wall collapsed, killing a mother and daughter and seriously injuring a son. On Saturday, Jhansi remained the hottest city in the state at 42.5°C, followed by Banda (42.2°C), Jalaun and Fatehpur (41.4°C each), and Varanasi (41.2°C). Azamgarh recorded the lowest night temperature at 20°C. Senior scientist Atul Kumar Singh said- All systems of storms and rain in UP have ended. Currently, the weather is likely to remain dry. There will be intense heat until pre-monsoon rains. Heat wave conditions will prevail. Monsoon may enter the state via Gorakhpur route by June 24. Indications are that the monsoon may also weaken in 20 to 25 days. What will the weather be like for the next 3 days? Know here June 7: There is a possibility of light rain across the state. Bright sunshine will appear intermittently, which may increase humidity. June 8: Weather will remain clear across the entire state. Bright sunshine will appear. There is no possibility of rain. June 9: Bright sunshine will appear in most districts across the state. Winds may blow at a speed of 30 km per hour. This will provide relief from humidity. Wind will blow at a speed of 60-70 KM along with rain in these districts Saharanpur, Shamli, Muzaffarnagar, Baghpat, Meerut, Ghaziabad, Hapur, Gautam Budh Nagar, Bulandshahr, Aligarh, Mathura, Hathras, Bijnor, Amroha, Moradabad, Sambhal Nautapa did not scorch in UP this time, temperature dropped by 10C Talking about Nautapa, it remained ineffective in UP this time. Due to storms, rain and hailstorms in many districts of the state, the temperature dropped by about 10C. On the first day of Nautapa, i.e., May 25, the mercury had reached 47.6C, which fell to 38C. However, now the effect of western disturbance has started ending. This will increase the heat again. The mercury will cross 45C. There will be less rainfall during monsoon in UP, know the reason Between June and September, Uttar Pradesh is also expected to receive below-normal rainfall. Dr. M Mahapatra, Director General of the Meteorological Department, said that this year there are signs of La Nina-like conditions in the Pacific Ocean ending and moving towards El Nino. Which will cause less rainfall. This means there are indications that the south-west monsoon will be weaker than normal this year. Additionally, the reduced snow formation in the Northern Hemisphere during January-March this year may also affect the monsoon. Last year monsoon was 10 to 15% more than normal According to the Meteorological Department, during the 2025 monsoon season (June to September) in Uttar Pradesh, an average rainfall of 870 to 900 mm was recorded. This was approximately 10 to 15 percent more than the normal monsoon average.

stories.title: Congress leader's engineer son found hanging in hotel's room:Deceased stayed with burqa-clad woman; family alleges he was murdered
stories.summary: In Kanpur on Saturday, the body of the only engineer son of a senior Congress leader was found hanging from a noose in a hotel. Upon receiving information from the staff, police and the forensic team reached the spot. During investigation, cigarette filters and a liquor bottle were found in the room. It also came to light that he had come to the hotel with a girl wearing a burqa, but she had left later. Police are now searching for the girl through her Aadhaar card and mobile number. The truth of the entire matter can be ascertained by questioning her. Meanwhile, the Congress leader's family members have alleged murder and demanded an investigation into the entire matter. The incident is from Aman Paradise Hotel located in Saket Nagar. Police engaged in search for young woman who arrived in burqa Haji Mohammad Fazal Khan, who lives in the Talaq Mahal area of Karnalganj police station area, is a Congress leader. He has been associated with the party for about 20 years, but has never held any position. He is active in politics from the Sishamau assembly seat. He has been close to senior Congress leader Ahmed Patel. He has been in constant touch with senior Congress leaders. His family consisted of his wife Shahdab, married daughter Amber, and son Gayash Khan (32). Gayash was not yet married. After completing his B.Tech from Pune, he was working in a private company in Delhi on a package worth lakhs. However, for the past 6 months, he had been at home due to work from home. Ghayas had gone out with friends on Friday. He told his family members that he would not come home at night. After this, the family members were also reassured. However, on Saturday, when news of their son's death arrived, there was chaos in the family. Family members reached the hotel management on receiving the information and identified the body. He had returned to the hotel again after dropping the girl at night Hotel Aman Paradise manager Saurabh Kumar said - Ghayas had arrived at the hotel with a girl on Friday. Around 7:30 PM at night, he left the hotel to drop off the girl. After some time, he returned and went to his room. He had also ordered dinner online. On Saturday morning at 11:30 AM, when his room door didn't open, we informed the police. In the presence of police, the room was opened with a master key, and Ghayas body was found hanging from the fan with the support of a bedsheet. Family members said - His leg was bent on the bed, this is not suicide but murder During the investigation, the police from Kidwai Nagar station and the forensic team found liquor bottles and cigarette filters in the room. The family members stated that the brand of cigarette filters found was not the one he used to smoke. Not only this, they also alleged that the body was hanging from the fan above the bed with the support of a bedsheet. Both legs of the body were bent. Committing suicide in this manner is not possible. The family members have demanded an investigation into the case, alleging murder. The family says that the girl with whom he had reached the hotel should also be called and interrogated. DCP South Deependra Nath Chaudhary stated- After investigation, the body has been sent for post-mortem. The initial investigation suggests it appears to be a case of suicide. Still, based on the allegations of the family members, the case is being investigated. Besides, the entries of people coming to the hotel and CCTV footage are being examined. The girl who reached the hotel with Gayash will also be interrogated.

stories.title: Padma Shri Jaspal Rana’s mortal remains reach Varanasi:Last rites to be held at Manikarnika Ghat; death occurred yesterday
stories.summary: The body of international shooter Jaspal Rana arrived at Varanasi Airport by charter plane on Saturday afternoon at around 3:52 PM. The body was kept at the air cargo complex located in the old terminal building of the airport. A large number of people paid tribute there. After this, Jaspal Rana's body was taken to Rajghat for the last rites. From here, it will be brought by boat to Manikarnika Ghat, and the last rites will be performed there. The pyre has been prepared for this. At The Casa Resort on Chandmari Ring Road, the body was taken out of the box and placed on a bier. After this, the final journey departed for Manikarnika Ghat. During this, Defense Minister Rajnath Singh's son and Jaspal Rana's brother-in-law, MLA Pankaj Singh, were also present. Pankaj Singh had arrived at the airport around 12:15 PM. Apart from family members, BJP state minister Shankar Giri, former Azamgarh district president Jai Nath Singh, and several public representatives and dignitaries were present at the tribute program. First, see 3 pictures Padma Shri Jaspal Rana's uncle Rajendra Rana said - Jaspal Rana had expressed his wish many times that his last rites be performed at Manikarnika Ghat. Keeping this wish in mind, the family has decided to perform the last rites in Varanasi. Jaspal Rana, 49, passed away on Friday morning. He had been admitted to Max Saket Hospital in Delhi for the past 11 days. His health deteriorated on the flight while returning from Germany, after which he was admitted to the hospital. Manu Bhaker broke down while bidding final farewell to her guru Olympic medalist Manu Bhaker had reached Dehradun on Friday itself to bid a final farewell to her coach Jaspal Rana. Seeing the coach's mortal remains, she could not control herself and broke down, embracing Jaspal Rana's father Narayan Singh Rana. Jaspal Rana's role in Manu Bhaker's career has been extremely crucial. He continuously guided Manu from the junior level to the international stage. Jaspal Rana's training and experience are also considered a major reason behind Manu's two medals at the Paris Olympics. Over 600 Medals, Made History at 2006 Asiad Jaspal Rana is considered one of the most successful players in Indian shooting history. He has more than 600 medals to his name in various national and international competitions. In 1994, he set a world record with a gold medal at the Junior World Shooting Championship in Milan. That same year, he gained international recognition by winning a gold medal at the Hiroshima Asian Games. The 2006 Doha Asian Games are considered a golden chapter in his career. There, he scored a world-equalling 590 points in the 25-meter center fire pistol and won three gold and one silver medal. Friendship with Rahul Gandhi began at the shooting range Jaspal Rana's connections were not limited to the sports world. He had personal relationships with Rahul Gandhi as well as CM Pushkar Singh Dhami. According to some family sources, Rana and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi first met at a shooting range. Their shared passion for shooting brought them closer, and this relationship continued even after they entered politics. After joining Congress in 2012, Jaspal Rana was seen actively participating in party programs. His many meetings and public events with Rahul Gandhi remained a topic of discussion. Upon his demise, Rahul Gandhi also expressed grief, recalling his contribution to Indian shooting. From BJP to Congress, Father Remained in a Different Party After sports, Jaspal Rana also became active in politics. In 2009, he contested the Tehri Lok Sabha seat on a BJP ticket, though he could not win. Later, he joined Congress. At that time, his father Narayan Singh Rana was active in BJP, while Jaspal was campaigning for Congress. The separate political paths of father and son were among the well-known political stories of Uttarakhand during that period. Also connected to Rajnath Singh's family Jaspal Rana's sister, Sushma Singh, is married to Defense Minister Rajnath Singh's son and Noida MLA, Pankaj Singh. Due to this relationship, his family has also been connected to prominent political figures of the country. Jaspal Rana, who remained active in sports, politics, and and social life, has left behind a legacy that includes a long chain of medals, records, disciples, and inspiration. Father was in ITBP, handed Rana a pistol in childhood Jaspal Rana was born on June 28, 1976, in Uttarkashi. However, he was originally from Tehri. His father, Narayan Singh Rana, was deployed in the Indo-Tibetan Border Police, or ITBP. Later, he also became the first Sports Minister of Uttarakhand. He had a special fondness for shooting and it was he who handed his son a pistol at the tender age of 10. The sporting environment in the family was so strong that his sister Sushma Singh and brother Subhash Rana also became national-level shooters. From a young age, Jaspal spent most of his time at the shooting range, and it was from here that the journey began which placed him among the world's best shooters. First medal at the age of 12, Arjuna Award at 18 In the National Shooting Championship held in Ahmedabad in 1988, 12-year-old Jaspal Rana drew the nation's attention by winning a silver medal. After this, he consistently performed brilliantly in national competitions and emerged as the new face of Indian shooting. His talent can be gauged from the fact that he was honored with the Arjuna Award at the mere age of 18. Achieving this feat at such a young age was considered a great achievement in that era.

stories.title: Aligarh’s Sergeant Jitendra Sharma dies in Assam plane crash:Air Force AN-32 aircraft goes down; 5 personnel lose their lives
stories.summary: On Saturday morning at 10 AM, an Indian Air Force AN-32 transport aircraft crashed during landing at Rauria Air Force Station in Jorhat, Assam. Five Air Force personnel, including Sergeant Jitendra Sharma from Aligarh, died in the accident. One pilot was also martyred in the accident. These include Squadron Leader Prashant Singh, Flight Lieutenant Shubham Kumar, Sergeant Jitendra Sharma, Agniveervayu Khemaram Kumawat, and Agniveervayu Danish Alam. Following the accident, the Air Force has ordered a Court of Inquiry for investigation, while the co-pilot is undergoing treatment in the hospital. Danish was from Bihar and Khemaram was from Rajasthan. Sergeant Jitendra Sharma was from Salpur village in Aligarh. The accident occurred when the aircraft was attempting to land at the airbase. After the accident, it caught fire and broke into two pieces. This was an AN-32 cargo aircraft, used for transporting troops and supplies. The cause of the accident has not been revealed. The Indian Air Force stated that the aircraft was on a routine flight. It also appealed not to speculate until the initial results are out. Orders for a Court of Inquiry have been issued. Air Force preparing to replace AN-32 aircraft According to news agency ANI, the Indian Air Force is preparing to replace its old AN-32 and IL-76 transport aircraft. For this, new Medium Transport Aircraft (MTA) will be purchased to meet the future needs for transporting troops, weapons, and military equipment. 3 photos of the accident The fire brigade and army personnel present at the airbase reached the spot and brought the fire under control. AN-32 Cargo to extinguishplane capable of landing even in hilly and difficult terrains The Indian Air Force has a fleet of approximately 100 Antonov AN-32 tactical transport aircraft. Although the IAF initially purchased 125 such Soviet-origin planes, the number of active-duty planes has now reduced to approximately 100. Since 1980, the AN-32 has served as the backbone of the IAF's medium-lift transport capabilities. Due to its robustness during operations in hot weather and high-altitude areas like the Himalayas, it is considered very important. Air Force Aircraft Accidents from January to June January 21, 2026- An IAF trainee aircraft crashed during a routine flight in Uttar Pradesh. Both pilots safely ejected. No civilian casualties were reported. However, a Court of Inquiry was constituted for investigation. February 7, 2026- An HAL Tejas fighter jet veered off the runway during takeoff. Later reports cited a software glitch as the cause. The pilot survived, though he sustained injuries. March 5, 2026- An Su-30MKI crashed during training in Assam's Karbi Anglong region. Both pilots died. One of these pilots was also associated with Operation Sindoor. April 17, 2026- An Air Force fighter jet made a hard landing at Pune International Airport. The plane's 'undercarriage,' meaning the lower part of the aircraft, was damaged, causing it to hit the runway. This closed the runway for 11 hours.

stories.title: Pilgrim bus crash in UP leaves 3 dead, 36 injured:Driver may have dozed off, say passengers; 2 buses collide head-on
stories.summary: Three devotees were killed and at least 36 others injured after a private bus carrying pilgrims from Rajasthan collided head-on with a UP Roadways bus in Uttar Pradesh's Kasganj district early Saturday. The pilgrims, all members of an extended family from Bharatpur, were travelling to Soron for a holy dip in the Ganga when the accident occurred around 4 am. According to passengers, the private bus had left Bharatpur at about 11 pm on Friday. Several passengers alleged that the driver may have dozed off moments before the collision, causing the vehicle to drift into the opposite lane and crash into the oncoming state-run bus. The deceased were identified as Girraj Singh (85) of Farso village, Pitam (65), and Ram Dhakeli (80), both residents of Nagla Kurwariya in Bharatpur's Bayana area. Deepak, one of the passengers, said around 40 family members were travelling together when the accident took place near Kasganj. "The driver appeared to have fallen asleep shortly before the crash," he alleged. The impact left the front portions of both buses badly damaged and triggered panic among passengers. Local residents rushed to the spot and helped rescue those trapped inside the vehicles. Police and ambulance teams shifted the injured to Kasganj District Hospital. After receiving primary treatment, several passengers were referred to hospitals in Bharatpur. Some were admitted to RBM Hospital, while others were taken to private healthcare facilities. Police said an investigation is underway to determine the exact cause of the accident. See other pictures of the accident

stories.title: 1,200 scientists and experts to gather at BHU tomorrow:CM Yogi to inaugurate national convention; AI risks and ethics on agenda
stories.summary: Kashi, the religious and cultural capital, is now going to witness the country's biggest scientific discourse. The 7th National Convention of Vigyan Bharati is being organised on June 13 and 14 under the joint auspices of Banaras Hindu University and the Vedic Science Centre. Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will participate as the chief guest in the inaugural session of this two-day mega convention on the morning of June 13. This session will set the direction for future discourse related to science, technology, innovation, and national development in the country. Over 1200 stalwarts from India and abroad will gather Approximately 1200 delegates from India and various corners of the world are participating in this two-day national convention. Members of Vigyan Bharati, renowned scientists, researchers, academicians, policymakers, industry representatives, and experts in various technical fields will be seen on one platform at this grand gathering. Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary of the Ministry of AYUSH, Government of India, will be the special guest, and Dr. Shekhar C. Mande, President of the Indian National Science Academy, will also be present at the inaugural session. Padma Shri Prof. Ashutosh Sharma to deliberate on artificial intelligence and ethics On the second day of the convention, a special session will be organized on the most important and contemporary topic, 'Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Ethics'. Former Secretary of the Department of Science Technology, Government of India, and Padma Shri awardee Prof. Ashutosh Sharma will lead this session. In this, technical experts and policymakers will deeply deliberate on how to ensure the responsible and ethical use of Artificial Intelligence for the benefit of society. Country's Top think tanks to formulate strategy on 'One Health' and 'Net Zero' According to Dr. Shivkumar Sharma, National Organizing Secretary of Vigyan Bharati, the main objective of this convention is to prepare a concrete action plan for a scientifically empowered and self-reliant India by having meaningful discussions on contemporary scientific and social challenges. For this, two major sessions will be organized: Under the leadership of Dr. B. N. Gangadhar, Chairman of the National Medical Commission, experts related to medicine, health, and research will deliberate on this topic. Under the leadership of Manu Srivastava, Principal Secretary of the Energy Department, Government of Madhya Pradesh, dimensions related to sustainable development and energy transition will be discussed. Former Vice Chairman of NITI Aayog and senior RSS functionaries will also participate During the session, a public lecture will be delivered by renowned economist and former Vice Chairman of NITI Aayog, Dr. Rajiv Kumar. Additionally, a special address by Dr. Krishna Gopal, Sah-Sarkaryavah of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh, and a special lecture by Sunil Ambekar, All India Prachar Pramukh, have been organized. Prof. Ramnarayan Dwivedi, a member of the steering committee, informed that a comprehensive discussion will also be held on an important proposal related to the "Science, Technology and Innovation Policy for India" on this platform. Concluding session to be held in the presence of Minister of state for defence, Sanjay Seth This two-day event will conclude on June 14. In the closing session, Sanjay Seth, Minister of State for Defence, Government of India, will participate as the chief guest. Along with him, NITI Aayog members Prof. Abhay Karandikar and Prof. Govardhan Das will be present as special guests. Ankit Rai, Regional Organizing Secretary of Vijnana Bharati, stated that this national convention will prove to be a milestone in strengthening the scientific capabilities of the country and realizing the resolve of 'Developed India' by 2047.

stories.title: Speeding Creta mows down 4 in Saharanpur:Mother, son, daughter and granddaughter killed on spot
stories.summary: In Saharanpur, 4 members of a family died in a road accident. The family was on a single motorcycle. A speeding Creta car coming from behind hit them from the rear. The accident was so horrific that all four people on the motorcycle fell 10 feet away from the road into a ditch. The Creta car also overturned and fell into the ditch. Nearby people took all four injured to the hospital, where doctors declared them dead. The accident occurred on Saturday at 2 PM near Dhaulakuan in the Biharigarh area on Behat Road. Eyewitnesses stated that a minor was driving the Creta car. Police are investigating this claim based on the car's registration number. According to the police, Lavish (26) of Malkpur, his mother Rajdulari (55), sister Anjana alias Tannu (20), and three-year-old daughter Ruhi died in the accident. Two pictures of the accident Accident happened while returning home from in-laws' house Ankit, the uncle of the deceased, said - Lavish had gone to his in-laws' house in Kothri with his mother, sister, and daughter Ruhi (3). From there, he was returning to his village Malkpur on a bike. Lavish used to support his family by working as a laborer. He was the second of three brothers. Lavish got married in 2022. He has a wife and a young son at home. Ruhi, who lost her life in the accident, was the elder daughter. Police investigation revealed that the car was being driven by the minor son of Tahir, who lives in Kothri Bahalolpur-2. He fled the scene after the accident. Police have seized the car. The vehicle is said to be registered in Tahir's name. Police are engaged in further action and investigation in the matter.

stories.title: Yogi warns against comments on Akhilesh’s daughter:Says such things will not be tolerated; urges political workers to maintain restraint
stories.summary: CM Yogi reacted for the first time to the objectionable remark made against Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav's daughter, Aditi. He said on Saturday in Azamgarh - A daughter is a daughter, and she should be respected. I was seeing in recent days that some people had made wrong remarks against the daughter of the SP chief. I immediately told the police to register an FIR. No derogatory remark against a daughter will be tolerated. The CM said- We have been brought up with the tradition where it is said that a village's daughter is everyone's daughter, a village's sister is everyone's sister. We have not discriminated. Akhilesh ji, if you preach to others, then preach to your followers as well to exercise some restraint in their language. They should also think before making comments. Yogi said - What kind of language do SP people use towards sisters, deceased people, senior leaders, daughters, and elders? Akhilesh ji, explain it to them. If they don't understand, hand them over to us, we will make them understand. CM Yogi also inaugurated and laid the foundation stone for 39 development projects worth 955 crore in Azamgarh. Minister Omprakash Rajbhar was also present on the stage. Read CM Yogi's 4 major points- 1- Those who divide are not your well-wishers The CM said - Azamgarh is a district where there are handicrafts, artisans, food-providing farmers, and energetic youth. Then why did this district struggle for its identity? Why did a crisis of identity arise before that district? It is with this question that I repeatedly come to Azamgarh, because this pain is not just Azamgarh's, but ours too. Those who divided us, who split us all, they kept getting your support repeatedly, but they are not your well-wishers. 2- Before 2017, Azamgarh was struggling for its identity Yogi said - Remember Azamgarh before 2017, which was struggling for its identity. Back then, there was no university here, no Purvanchal Expressway, no airport was functioning properly, nor was there a music college in Hariharpur. Even Azamgarh's saree was not getting any platform then. There was no place for Mubarakpur's black pottery either. Today, a craftsman associated with black pottery met me and happily said that ever since the double-engine government came to power in Uttar Pradesh, our business has grown many times over. 3- Earlier, the poor had no one to listen to them The Chief Minister said - Earlier, the poor had no one to listen to them, but ever since our government was formed, the work that could not be done for centuries has been completed. Earlier, Azamgarh's name used to come up in every terrorist incident. Youths' jobs were being compromised. There was no scheme for daughters, nor any plan for their safety and advancement. Our government has worked to give due respect to Maharaja Suheldev. 4- Foreign invaders should not be honored The CM said - Earlier, events were held in Bahraich in the name of invaders Salar Mian and Ghazi Mian. When our government came, we said - this will not do. We got it stopped. We said that these are symbols of slavery. Foreign invaders should not be honored. Today, a large statue of Maharaja Suheldev has been installed here. Wherever you go, you will be recognized by Maharaja Suheldev. The Harihar Gharana here is famous all over the world. Here is Bhojpuri artist Dinesh Lal Nirahua, who is working to sweeten people's hearts with his voice. Rajbhar said - This time we will defeat SP in Azamgarh Om Prakash Rajbhar said - People say that Azamgarh is a stronghold of the Samajwadi Party. SP's stronghold means Yadavs' stronghold. Tell me, do Rajbhar, Nishad, Bind, and other castes live here or not? In this election, we will turn the stronghold into a 'gadhahi' (pit). We will work to defeat SP from here. FIR against 4 in Aditi Yadav comment case An FIR was registered in Kanpur-Pratapgarh on Thursday in connection with objectionable posts made on social media regarding Aditi Yadav (23). A case was registered against Bharat Patel, Nageshwar Singh Baghel, and Vinod Yadav on the complaint of Praveen Yadav, National Secretary of the Advocates' Association, in Kanpur. Additionally, on the complaint of Samajwadi Party General Secretary Abdul Qadir Jilani in Pratapgarh, a case was registered against an ID named Sheetla Sujan Kavi. All four are accused of making objectionable posts against Aditi on social media. This tarnished the image of Akhilesh Yadav and his family in society. Therefore, strict action should be taken against them. Read what was said about the objectionable posts on Aditi Yadav -

stories.title: 4 friends record video before crash:Car speeding at over 100 kmph hits parked truck; all die on spot
stories.summary: Anupam, who lost his life in a road accident in Prayagraj, had his wife fill her hairline with vermilion for the last time. When Anupam's body arrived home from Unnao on Saturday morning, his wife Priya became unconscious. Crying, she sat near the body. During this, a woman brought a vermilion box. A relative applied vermilion on Anupam's hand, then Priya bowed her head and filled her hairline with vermilion, and touching her husband's feet, she burst into tears. Whoever witnessed this scene had tears well up in their eyes. The mother also clung to the body. Crying, she said, 'Show me his face just once. Now I will never get my son back. I beg you, just let me see his face once.' Anupam had died along with his four friends in a road accident on the Ganga Expressway in Unnao on Friday. All four were going to Shimla for a trip. On Saturday, the bodies of the four friends were brought to their homes. The three friends, Uday, Anupam, and Vijay, were cremated at Chhatnag Ghat in Prayagraj, while Aman Kashyap's last rites were performed in his ancestral village, Mandhata in Pratapgarh. See 2 pictures Uday was cremated by his father and Vijay by his brother. On Saturday, the funeral procession of Uday Singh, the only son of his parents, left the house first. Seeing the condition of the parents while bidding farewell to their son, people's eyes welled up. Father Ram Singh lit the pyre. After this, Vijay Kumar's funeral procession began. Vijay's pyre was lit by his elder brother Roshan Lal. Anupam Gupta's father, Ajay Gupta, arrived in Prayagraj from Kolkata in the afternoon. After this, Anupam's last rites were performed. They were going to Shimla in a Tata Punch Anupam Gupta (32), Uday Singh (28), Vijay (40) from Jafarpur Babuganj, Phulpur police station area, and Aman Kashyap (28) from Mandhata, Pratapgarh district, were friends. On Friday morning around 10 am, they left for Shimla in a Tata Punch car. Aman had come to his aunt's house in Babuganj, from where the four friends started their journey together. Around 3:30 PM, their car collided from behind with a truck parked on the side of the road on the Ganga Expressway in Unnao. The impact was so strong that the car was torn to pieces. The front part was badly crushed. All four friends died in the accident. They were all stuck to their seats. The doors were cut to pull all four out of the car. All four friends had their own businesses Anupam Gupta operated a shop named Gupta Mobile Internet in Jafarpur Babuganj. He was married. Meanwhile, Vijay ran a tent house business. His family includes his wife Sunita, two sons Mayank and Eeshanth, and a daughter Ishika. Uday Singh owned a footwear shop and is survived by his wife Khushi and two-year-old son Ayush. Aman Kashyap was unmarried and had come to Babuganj to visit relatives. All four friends were educated Anupam owned a mobile shop, while Vijay was running a tent house business. Uday had a shoe and slipper shop. Aman owned several shops in Pratapgarh. Anupam's parents live in Calcutta. His father works for LIC. Anupam had graduated. He ran a mobile shop. His wife Priya had gone to her maternal home. Anupam's in-laws are in Bhadri Kunda, Pratapgarh. They had been married for two years. Uday Patel alias Babuji was an only child. He owned a shoe and slipper shop. Uday had completed ITI. He had done his apprenticeship from Gujarat in the IFFCO company. He had come home a year ago. Here, he had started a business. Vijay had graduated. Currently, he was doing a tent business.

stories.title: CM Yogi targets foreign forces in speech:Says excessive pesticide use is harming farmland; opens national convention at BHU
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said in Varanasi for a long time, there has been a perception in our country that Indians are good for nothing and only foreigners are superior. Foreign powers, leftist ideology, and anti-India elements tried to do this to the country and are still doing so today. On the importance of Ganga, CM Yogi said- In my childhood, my mother used to ask us to cultivate small beds near the house. We would water the plants, add fertiliser, and take care of them. When a plant got infested with insects or didn't bloom, we would complain to our mother about it. Then, my mother would say, 'Don't worry.' After that, she would bring Ganga water in a pot and sprinkle it on the plants. The surprising thing was that within four or five days, those plants would start blooming again. That's when we realized the importance of Ganga. Actually, on Saturday, CM Yogi inaugurated the 7th National Convention of Vigyan Bharati at Swatantrata Bhawan of Kashi Hindu University (BHU). Before this, BHU Vice-Chancellor Prof. Ajit Kumar Chaturvedi welcomed and honored the Chief Minister by presenting him with an angavastra. This national convention of Vigyan Bharati is being organized on June 13 and 14. Approximately 1200 delegates from India and abroad are participating in the 2-day convention. These include members of Vigyan Bharati, scientists, researchers, academicians, policymakers, industry representatives, and experts from various fields. See 3 pictures CM Yogi released the annual report of Vigyan Bharati.

stories.title: CM to gift ₹300 crore development projects today:Programme at Mahuapar in Chillupar; inaugurations for 197 social welfare schemes
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will reach Gorakhpur on Saturday afternoon for a three-day tour. On the first day, he will gift development projects worth 300 crore rupees to the Chillupar assembly constituency. These include 319 projects. At the program organised at Gandhi Inter College in Mahuapar, he will inaugurate 122 projects completed at a cost of 152.21 crore rupees and lay the foundation stone for 197 projects to be built at a cost of 143.25 crore rupees. There, the Chief Minister will also address the public gathering. The CM will reach Gorakhpur from Azamgarh. All these projects will not only ease traffic in Chillupar assembly and Bansgaon Lok Sabha constituencies, but will also strengthen education and health facilities, as well as flood protection measures. The program will start at 1 PM. People have arrived at the program venue. The Chief Minister is being awaited. Inauguration of these projects According to the district administration, the projects to be inaugurated include the widening and strengthening of the Uruwa-Dhuriapar-Shahpur Belghat road at a cost of ₹57.81 crore, the newly constructed Government Industrial Training Institute in Kohra Bujurg at a cost of ₹10.81 crore, and the development of smart classes and other facilities in more than 15 primary schools. Similarly, various works undertaken for strengthening the embankments along the Rapti and Saryu rivers are also included. On Sunday evening, the second day of his visit, the Chief Minister will participate in a program organised at Veer Bahadur Singh Sports College, where he will inaugurate and lay the foundation stone for development projects worth approximately ₹950 crore.

stories.title: ₹10 lakh recovered from Ram Mandir employee’s home:Cash hidden in cow dung pile; temple trust requests CM Yogi for probe
stories.summary: The row over claims of a ₹7 crore theft from donations at the Ayodhya Ram Temple is intensifying. According to sources, the temple trust on Saturday requested Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath to order an SIT (Special Investigation Team) probe into the alleged theft. Meanwhile, ₹10 lakh has been recovered from the house of temple employee Lavkush Mishra (27). He had allegedly hidden the cash under a pile of cow dung, while some money was also found inside a box. However, it is not yet known who the money belongs to. Lavkush’s father has also confirmed that the cash was recovered from their house. Sources said Lavkush was responsible for counting donation money at the temple. Lavkush’s father said his son had been working at the Ram Temple for the past four to five months. Lavkush is a resident of Minapur Thakuran Phagauli village in the Rudauli area of Ayodhya. His father, Bacchulal, said, “My son had been working at the Ram Temple for the last four to five months. During this period, the theft incident took place there. Some people came to our house as part of the investigation and carried out a search. During the search, ₹10 lakh was recovered. What had to happen has now happened. The house being built in Faizabad has no connection with my son. To construct the house, I mortgaged 10-12 bighas of farmland.” Villagers said the search team consisted of six people, including two in police uniform and four in plain clothes. The cash was found in cupboards and boxes inside Lavkush’s house, while some money had allegedly been buried under a pile of cow dung. Lavkush previously worked as a car mechanic. Villagers said his financial condition improved rapidly after he got the temple job. Whenever he visited the village, he spent money freely. On one occasion, he reportedly spent ₹50,000 at a liquor shop to treat villagers. Lavkush’s father, Bacchulal, works at the iron market in Ghaziabad. He has three daughters and one son, Lavkush. Lavkush got married eight years ago and has a six-year-old son and a two-year-old daughter. Nripendra Mishra arrived in Ayodhya on Saturday for the second time in five days. He attended a meeting of the temple construction committee. Before the meeting, he was questioned about the donation controversy. Question: What issues will be discussed today?Nripendra Mishra: I do not know. Question: What will be discussed in the temple construction committee meeting?Nripendra Mishra: I have come to review the progress of the construction work. Question: Allegations of a scam involving Ram Temple donations have surfaced. Will that also be discussed? Will you seek information about it?Nripendra Mishra: This is a construction committee meeting. My responsibility is to oversee the construction work. Earlier, after the donation controversy emerged on 7 June, Nripendra Mishra had also visited Ayodhya on 9 June. He held a meeting with members of the temple trust, where issues related to donation funds, their utilisation and financial records were discussed. Former account in charge said that removed after complaining to Champat Rai BJP leader wrote two letters to PM Modi Ayodhya's BJP leader Dr. Rajneesh Singh has written two letters to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He sent the first letter on 9 June. In it, he wrote that the Ram Temple is a center of faith for millions of devotees. In such a situation, complete transparency is necessary in any allegations or disputes related to offerings, donations, and temple administration. He said that if the allegations made are false, the truth should come out through an investigation. For this, an impartial investigation should be conducted by an independent and high-level agency, such as CBI or ED. Subsequently, on June 11, Dr. Rajneesh Singh wrote a second letter to the Prime Minister. In it, he made 6 demands- What leaders said on the claims of theft System for counting offerings in Temple Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust formed on 5 February, 2020

stories.title: TGT exam solver gang kingpin arrested in Varanasi:₹25,000 reward on him; 14 debit cards fake documents seized
stories.summary: Police have arrested Daulat Kumar, the alleged mastermind of a solver gang involved in the TGT examination in Varanasi, along with his associate Nitish Kumar. A ₹25,000 reward had been announced on Daulat, who had been absconding since the June 4 arrests. Both were caught from the Lakri Mandi area in Chaukaghat and later sent to jail. ACP Chetganj Shubham Kumar said that on June 4, solver Amrit Raj, who was appearing for the TGT exam in place of a candidate at Queen's Inter College, and his accomplice Chhotu Kumar were arrested. During questioning, they identified Daulat Kumar, a resident of Ward No. 2, Temabhela under Gwalpara police station in Bihar's Madhepura district, as the gang's mastermind, prompting a police manhunt and the announcement of a ₹25,000 reward. Apprehended with accomplice from Lakri Mandi According to the ACP, the police had received information that Daulat Kumar was present in the Chauka Ghat timber market area. Based on the information, he was arrested on the night of June 12 after being surrounded. Along with him, Nitish Kumar, a resident of Ratanpura, Supaul district, Bihar, was also apprehended. The police recovered several fake documents, 14 debit cards, and important transaction papers related to examinations from their possession. The recovered documents are being investigated. How he ran the solver gang Gang's network to be investigated Police say that by interrogating the arrested accused, information about other members of the gang and their network is being gathered. It is being investigated which competitive exams this gang has tried to infiltrate so far, and how many people are involved in it. Further legal action will be taken based on the investigation, and a campaign will also be launched to arrest other accused associated with the gang.

stories.title: Varanasi international stadium nears completion:92% work done; director says, 'ground will be match-ready within 30 minutes of rain'
stories.summary: The Ganjari International Cricket Stadium, a dream project of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, is nearing completion, with about 92% of construction work finished, according to Project Director Saroj Shukla. A trial match is planned by the end of this year, while the venue is expected to host its first international match in 2027. Stadium being built on Shiva theme-based architecture Spectator gallery to be crescent-shaped The stadium's roof has been designed inspired by the shape of the moon adorning Lord Shiva's forehead, while the spectator gallery is being developed on the lines of the famous Ganga Ghats' steps in Kashi. This will provide spectators with a unique experience of Kashi's spiritual culture along with the game. Project Director Saroj Shukla informed that a state-of-the-art drainage system has been installed in the ground. Even if it rains continuously for one or two hours, the ground can be made ready for play within just 30 minutes. This facility will place it in the category of the country's select modern cricket stadiums. Prime Minister laid the foundation stone in 2023 Ganjari Cricket Stadium will open new opportunities not only for players from Purvanchal but also for those from surrounding districts and neighboring states. Along with providing an international platform for sporting talents, its operation is expected to bring significant benefits to Varanasi's economy, tourism, and employment sectors. The foundation stone for this ambitious project was laid by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on September 23, 2023.

stories.title: 4 arrested in Lucknow, including UP police constable:CRPF sub-inspector absconding in ₹5 lakh hostage robbery case
stories.summary: Four people, including a UP Police constable, have been arrested in Lucknow for allegedly robbing two men after luring them with investment promises. The victims were called to invest in a private company, held hostage, and robbed of ₹5 lakh. They were also assaulted when they resisted. A CRPF sub-inspector and another accused were allegedly involved and are currently absconding. Police said the case was registered at Chinhat Kotwali on June 11 on a complaint by Prabhakar Singh of Vrindavan Colony. He alleged that his brother Diwakar Singh and friend Anoop Shukla were promised quick returns by investing in a company, but when they arrived with the money, they were robbed and beaten. Used to intimidate by posing as police officers The arrested accused revealed during interrogation that they worked as a syndicate. They would call people in the name of investment, intimidate them by posing as officers from various branches of the police, and extort money from them. They also committed robberies multiple times. DCP East Deeksha Sharma said that during the investigation of the case, the involvement of CRPF Sub-Inspector Jai Prakash Yadav came to light. He is currently absconding. Along with the Sub-Inspector, another accused, Anand Dubey, was also named in this case. Police arrested all four at night The arrested accused include Javed Hussain and Asif, residents of Gorakhpur; Pravesh Tripathi, a resident of Sant Kabir Nagar; and Pooran Singh, a resident of Rajasthan. All were arrested on the night of June 12 near the Hardasikheda canal culvert. Accused constable posted at Chinhat Kotwali DCP East Deeksha Sharma stated that UP Police constable Pooran Singh is currently posted at Chinhat Kotwali. In this case, 4 accused have been arrested. Police teams are continuously raiding to arrest the absconding sub-inspector. Along with this, information about the criminal history of the accused is being gathered from other districts and units.

stories.title: Gorakhpur power revenue drops by ₹5 crore:22 power engineers face action; major defaulters to lose connections
stories.summary: In Gorakhpur, the electricity corporation has taken a tough stance after electricity bill recovery fell behind targets. Revenue collection in May was around ₹5 crore lower than last year, prompting charge sheets against 14 JEs, 5 SDOs, and 3 Executive Engineers. Following the action, engineers have launched campaigns to recover dues from defaulting consumers. Along with ensuring uninterrupted summer power supply, engineers are also responsible for boosting revenue. The Chairman and Managing Director of Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited have been continuously reviewing recovery performance. Dissatisfied with Gorakhpur city's May revenue figures, the management initiated action against poorly performing engineers. Bills lower after shift from prepaid to postpaid meters Engineers say that one reason for the decrease in revenue is also the change in the meter system. Earlier, during the prepaid meter system, many consumers had deposited money in advance to avoid power cuts. Later, when the postpaid system was implemented, the same amount was adjusted in the bill. This resulted in lower bills for many consumers and affected recovery. Payment stalled, awaiting one-time settlement scheme Arrears are increasing in rural areas along with metropolitan areas. According to officials, many consumers are waiting for a one-time settlement scheme to arrive, so they are not depositing bills. Meanwhile, some people are citing financial difficulties and saying they will pay later. Superintending Engineer City Ranjeet Chaudhary informed that the campaign for arrears recovery has been intensified. Connections of consumers who owe more than one lakh rupees in electricity bills are being disconnected. Supply will resume only after payment. Action is also being taken against small defaulters. Action will also continue against engineers who show negligence in revenue recovery.

stories.title: Mother's dream, son's deception:22-year-old posed as army brigadier after NEET setbacks; Shahjahanpur police arrest youth
stories.summary: My mother wanted me to become an army officer. My father wanted to make me a doctor. I didn't want to disappoint my parents, so I tried everything. I took the NEET exam twice, but failed. To fulfill my mother's dream, I bought a uniform and became a Brigadier. I also hired two security guards, whom I provided with NGS commando uniforms. I had 'Doctor' and 'Army' written on my car. I also started driving with the army flag installed. This is what 22-year-old fake Brigadier Aryan Verma said. His father is an inspector in the horticulture department, and his mother is a government teacher. He had been roaming around Shahjahanpur wearing a uniform for two months. Former soldiers became suspicious of him. They, along with army officials, laid a trap to catch him. On Friday, the event was organised, and Aryan Verma was called. As soon as he arrived, army officials asked him questions related to the army. He was flustered by one question after another. He got nervous. After this, the officers apprehended him. Under strict interrogation, he confessed to the crime. He narrated his entire story. After this, the army handed him over to the police. See 3 pictures Read the entire incident in sequence Mother is a government teacher, father is an inspector Aryan Verma, a resident of the Roja area, comes from a well-off family and lives in a three-story house. His father, Anil Verma, is an inspector in the Horticulture Department in Powayan, while his mother, Manoj Devi, is a government teacher in Jalalpur. He also has a younger brother studying in Class 4. Failed NEET twice, then posed as army officer After completing intermediate, Aryan was sent to Delhi to prepare for NEET. He appeared for the exam twice but failed both times. During police questioning, he said that due to family pressure, he bought a Brigadier's uniform in Delhi in January, hired two boys, and told his family he had been selected for the Army. He then began moving around in the uniform. Know how officers laid a trap and caught him Fake ID, pistol, and baton recovered A fake pistol, forged documents, a baton (stick), and military insignia were recovered from Aryan. Late Friday night, Naib Subedar Amit Kumar filed a complaint against Aryan. Based on the army's complaint, an FIR was registered against him, and he was handed over to the police. He had also put up an 'Army Brigadier' nameplate outside his house. His car also had 'Army' and 'Doctor' written on it. Admin Commandant Colonel JS Jagran stated that a person roaming under suspicious circumstances in the cantonment area was taken into custody. Objectionable and suspicious material was found in his possession. All aspects are being thoroughly investigated.

stories.title: 22-year-old fake brigadier busted in UP:Hired 2 bogus NSG commandos driver; army officers lured him to an event before arrest
stories.summary: A 22-year-old man posing as a Brigadier was detained in Shahjahanpur by the Military Police. Dressed in a Brigadier's uniform, he was accompanied by two men in NSG commando uniforms and a driver. Authorities recovered a fake Army identity card, a replica pistol, and several Army-related documents. The youth, identified as Aryan Verma (22) from Roza city, had arrived at the Shaheed Sangrahalaya in the Cantonment area in a Harrier SUV carrying an Army flag. His suspicious behavior alerted ex-servicemen and museum staff, who informed the Army, leading to his detention. Full story in detail Fake ID, pistol, and baton recovered Military police recovered a fake army identity card, a fake pistol, and a baton (stick) used by Brigadier-level officers from Aryan's possession. He had also put up a nameplate with the name Brigadier at his house. He had hired a car driver, from whom a fake government identity card was found. In addition, two security personnel were also in NSG commando uniforms. Aryan's father, Anil Verma, is an inspector in the Horticulture Department in the Puwayan area, while his mother, Manoj Devi, is a government teacher in Jalalpur, Sadar Tehsil area. He also has a younger brother in the family, who studies in class four. Army Intelligence is interrogating Considering the seriousness of the matter, a special Army Intelligence team from Bareilly has reached Shahjahanpur. Currently, the youth is being interrogated by military officials. He has not yet been handed over to the local police. Further action will be taken after the army's interrogation is complete. Admin Commandant Colonel JS Jagran stated that a person roaming in suspicious circumstances in the Cantonment area has been taken into custody. Some objectionable and suspicious material has been found in his possession. The matter is being investigated under military rules, and all aspects are being thoroughly examined.

stories.title: UP cop alleges deep-rooted corruption:Constable says 'Posting depends on money'; are police officers really 'Black Englishmen'?
stories.summary: No constable in the police department wants to be involved in bribery, but officers will send them to bring okra for 10 rupees, and the okra costs ₹12. Then, on the way, they will call and say to bring pumpkin too. If they don't bring it, they will be removed, and problems will start. They will have to clean the bathroom. If they don't want to clean the bathroom, then make all arrangements for the sir. This is the statement of a UP Police constable, who is revealing the secrets of bribery in his department. Recently, Constable Sunil Kumar Shukla, posted at Lucknow Police Line, released a video calling police officers 'black Englishmen'. Sunil had said - police officers take money for every task. I myself have had to pay bribes. How much truth is there in Constable Sunil's words, to know this, Dainik Bhaskar's team investigated. We spoke to several policemen on a hidden camera. Some of them clearly stated how the rate for getting duty in lucrative and comfortable places is fixed. How does corruption work from top to bottom? Read the full revelation Know what Constable Sunil had said Constable Sunil Kumar Shukla said, In the Reserve Police Line of Lucknow Police Commissionerate, a zamindari system of loot is being run by 'black Englishmen' i.e., tyrannical officers. A constable-havildar pays 2 thousand rupees to get his duty assigned. RI (Reserve Inspector) sir cuts his share and presents the remaining money at the feet of these 'black English' officers. In a conversation with Bhaskar, Sunil narrated 3 incidents of transactions Incident-1: Money has to be paid to get HRA assigned Not only do you have to pay money to get a duty assigned, but you also have to go twice a year to get HRA assigned. For this, too, you will have to pay 200-200 rupees. Those who have a 'setting' get it done for 100 rupees. This means you will have to pay 100-200 rupees. Incident-2: Medical Babu took ₹4500 bribe from me My wife's delivery took place in Raebareli. I went to Medical Clerk Shailendra Kumar with the bill for a medical reimbursement of 50 thousand rupees. He said that I will get you 45 thousand rupees. In this way, I gave Shailendra Kumar a bribe of 5000 rupees. (In this matter, Clerk Shailendra Kumar, posted in Sitapur, says that he does not know Sunil Shukla, so he cannot say anything) Incident-3: Money goes up through the Guard Commander In Lucknow, too, money is taken in the name of duty. If you have to go on guard (special duty), you will have to pay ₹2 thousand per month, everyone knows this. Constables give, and guard commanders take. Money is collected through the guard commander. Then this money reaches the officers. To find out if Sunil was telling the truth, we spoke to Constable Mohit Kumar (name changed) posted in Kushinagar. At the constable's request, we are not disclosing his name and identity here. Reporter: Sunil Shukla has made serious allegations. Are they true? Constable: Yes, what he said is true. These things happen. Some places have it more, some less. Reporter: How are duties assigned? Constable: The Head Moharrir decides. Those who pay get favorable postings; those who don't are sent to stand at crossroads in the heat. Reporter: Does the location affect the amount paid? Constable: Yes. The more convenient the posting, the higher the payment. Everything works on a fixed system. Reporter: Is there a separate arrangement for crossroads duty? Constable: People who want to earn more pay accordingly and get better postings. It's all about money. Reporter: Does money also go to senior officers? Constable: It's a channel-based system. Money moves step by step from lower levels to higher levels. Reporter: What about police outposts and police stations? Constable: An outpost costs more than a crossroads posting. Those who pay nothing are often sent for post-mortem duty. Reporter: What's difficult about post-mortem duty? Constable: Many expenses come from your own pocket. You handle paperwork, bodies arriving at night, and other responsibilities. After this, we spoke to Constable Vivek Kumar (name changed), posted in Gorakhpur Police for the past 10 years. He also backed Sunil Shukla's claims. Constable: Everything Shukla ji said is true. Not a single word is wrong. Reporter: How widespread is bribery in the police department? Constable: New recruits don't want to take bribes, but the system forces them. If you're sent to buy vegetables worth ₹10 and the cost is ₹12, then more items are added later. If you don't manage it, you'll face trouble and be assigned undesirable work like cleaning bathrooms. Reporter: So other expenses come from your pocket? Constable: Yes. If an unidentified body is found and you're assigned duty, expenses from the post-mortem to the cremation often have to be managed personally. Reporter: Are all officers the same? Constable: No. Officers like Ajay Pal Sharma, Rohit Singh Sajwan, Durga Shakti Nagpal, Akash Kulhari, Navneet Sikera and Aseem Arun are different. They don't create undue pressure and ensure fair working conditions. Reporter: Shukla ji says an honest person cannot survive in the police department. Constable: Absolutely. It's very difficult for an honest person to survive, and if someone tries, it disrupts the existing system for others. Investigation revealed these points Who is Constable Sunil? Constable Sunil Shukla, posted in the Reserve Police Line of Lucknow Police Commissionerate, is a 2015 batch constable. He hails from Pure Ramsevak Mishra village in Gauriganj, Amethi district. His father, the late Harikaran Shukla, was a home guard. His wife, Sudha Tripathi, is posted as a Head Constable in Raebareli. Sunil has released 7 videos in a little over a month. Constable Sunil has been suspended after a departmental inquiry for making and sharing videos on police corruption, thereby tarnishing the department's image, and for ignoring rules. However, even after the suspension, his attitude has not softened. In a video released on May 10, Sunil directly questioned the Chief Minister, asking if he was a criminal, terrorist, or Naxalite, for which police were sent to his house at 1 am.

stories.title: 'Lost my son, yet couldn’t get Katra gang chief punished’:Ghazipur father waits 5 years for justice; alleges police protected criminal
stories.summary: Don’t take my photograph. Those people are dangerous. They have strong connections with the police and politicians. My son's murder case reached the court, but Shankar never appeared even once. As he says this, tears well up in the eyes of Vinod Singh, father of student Anshuman Singh, who was murdered five years ago by Shankar Pandey, the alleged leader of the Katra Gang. Following the recent daylight murder of hotel businessman Vineet Rai in Ghazipur, renewed attention has turned to Anshuman’s case. The court has now issued a non-bailable warrant (NBW) against Shankar. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to Vinod Singh, who has been fighting the murder case. He says: Why would Shankar ever be punished? The Ghazipur police use him for heroin trafficking. The police themselves nurtured and protected him. Kidnapping people, assaulting them and throwing them by the roadside was completely normal for the Katra Gang. He adds, Only after a major crime happened did everyone remember Shankar. Now old cases linked to him are being heard more actively. People know only a few stories about the Katra Gang because the police never recorded most incidents. Shankar got many people killed, but only the murders of Vineet and Anshuman were officially registered against him. Gang formed in class 10, first murder after class 12 Shankar Pandey has a luxurious house spread over nearly 2,000 square feet in the Gausabad area of Ghazipur city. The house is currently locked. His entire family is absconding, while his father is lodged in a jail in West Bengal in a drug trafficking case. Shankar studied in an English-medium school. According to local accounts, he began group rivalries and violent clashes while studying in Class 10 in 2014. After passing Class 12 in 2016, he allegedly turned crime into a full-time profession. That same year, Anshuman Singh from the village of Utarauli in Revatipur also completed Class 12. He had studied at Adarsh Inter College in Ghazipur city and later enrolled in a B.Com course at PG College. After some time, he joined a coaching institute in Lucknow to prepare for competitive examinations. Threats began after dispute with gang member During his school days, Anshuman had a dispute with Satyam Rai and some of his friends, who were associated with the Katra Gang. After the altercation, Shankar allegedly called Anshuman several times and threatened him. Anshuman remained disturbed but never discussed the issue with his family. Vinod Singh recalls, Anshuman had come home during the Holi holidays. We learned from his friends that he was troubled and that some boys were harassing him. We told him to stay in Ghazipur and focus on his graduation studies instead of returning elsewhere. He agreed. First attack foiled by residents Anshuman later began living in a colony in Ghazipur city along with his friend Raghvendra and a relative’s son. Vinod says, Everything was fine until February 2020, when Shankar and members of his gang carried out the first attack. They entered the colony, abused and assaulted Anshuman. However, residents came to help and chased the gang away. While leaving, they threatened, ‘We are going now, but you will not survive. Called for a compromise, then attacked On March 21, 2020, Satyam Rai called Anshuman and asked him to come near the Shah Junaid Pir Dargah in Saklenabad, saying they wanted to settle the dispute. Anshuman went there with his friend Raghvendra. He had no idea that Shankar Pandey and his associates would also be present. When they saw that the group was carrying sticks and rods, they tried to step back. However, the attackers immediately launched an assault. More than 10 youths, including Priyanshu Singh, Saurabh Singh, Bobby Sarkar, Ranjeet, and Abhishek, were allegedly present with Shankar. They brutally beat Anshuman and Raghvendra with sticks, rods, and hockey sticks before pulling out knives. Repeated attacks were made on Anshuman’s legs, arms, and neck. Raghvendra’s jaw was severely fractured. Believing both victims were dead, the attackers fled. People who heard the commotion near the shrine rushed to the spot and took them to a hospital. Anshuman could not be saved. Raghvendra was referred to Varanasi and survived after nearly a month of treatment. Police arrested four, Shankar escaped Vinod Singh says, ‘Based on details provided by Raghvendra, I filed a case against Shankar Pandey, Priyanshu Singh, Bobby Sarkar, Saurabh Singh and seven unidentified attackers.’ Four days later, police arrested Priyanshu, Saurabh, Ranjeet Rajbhar, and Abhishek Kumar from behind Ghazipur Railway Station. However, Shankar managed to evade arrest. BJP booth president says justice remains elusive Vinod Singh has been an active BJP worker for 42 years and currently serves as a booth president in Ghazipur. He says, 'I lost my son. I left no stone unturned. I fought this case from the police station to the courtroom with all my strength. Yet I could not ensure concrete action against Shankar Pandey.' He adds, ‘Only after Vineet was murdered in the same brutal manner did people remember Anshuman. Over the last five to six years, Shankar and his gang have been involved in four or five more murders. They have strong connections with police and politicians. Check Shankar’s record, he has never remained in jail for more than two months. In our case, he never appeared in court. Only his lawyer attended hearings.’ He further claims, ‘Katra Gang member Bobby Sarkar belongs to the family of mafia figure Ranjeet Singh. Their legal system is fixed, they spend some time in jail, and then secure bail.’ Breaking down while narrating his son’s story, Vinod says, ‘Why would Shankar be punished? Police personnel in Ghazipur use him for heroin trafficking. They raised and protected him. Kidnapping people or publicly assaulting them had become very easy for the Katra Gang. Only after this major crime did people realize what kind of criminal he really was.’ Court issues non-bailable warrant The Anshuman murder case is being heard in a Ghazipur court. Assistant District Government Counsel Akhilesh Singh, who is handling the case, said: 'Shankar was repeatedly failing to appear before the court. Police had already announced a reward of ₹1 lakh on him. We placed these facts before Additional District Judge Shakti Singh, after which a non-bailable warrant was issued. He has been ordered to appear before the court on June 25.' Other cases and ongoing search Akhilesh Singh also cited another case in which garment trader Sachin Chaurasia was allegedly assaulted and kidnapped in broad daylight on September 5, 2024, by Shankar Pandey and Kamlesh Chaudhary, who was later killed in a police encounter. According to Singh, traffic congestion prevented the accused from escaping with the victim, forcing them to abandon him and flee. A non-bailable warrant has also been issued in that case. If Shankar fails to appear, proceedings under Sections 82 and 83 can be initiated, declaring him a proclaimed offender and allowing attachment of his properties. Shankar faces 10 criminal cases, including murder, attempted murder, kidnapping, and assault. Two of his close associates, Alok Dubey and Sonu Yadav, are also absconding, with rewards of ₹1 lakh each announced on them. Police are conducting raids in Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, and Jharkhand. Although Ghazipur police have identified 49 gangs in the district, including the Katra Gang, no member of the gang has yet been arrested in the current crackdown. Shankar’s social media accounts continue to feature videos portraying power and influence, including clips in which police personnel are seen folding their hands before him.

stories.title: Pre-monsoon activity intensifies in UP:Rain in 20 cities, homes flooded in Kanpur; 4 dead in weather-related incidents
stories.summary: Pre-monsoon activity has intensified across Uttar Pradesh, bringing rain to around 20 cities, including Kanpur, Ayodhya, and Unnao. In Lucknow, dark clouds covered the sky at around 7:45 am on Saturday, followed by strong winds and heavy rainfall. Dust storms were reported in Kaushambi and Unnao, while Pratapgarh and Prayagraj witnessed daytime darkness before rain, and strong winds lashed the areas. Heavy rainfall caused waterlogging in several districts. In Hathras, rainwater flooded the Sadar police station premises, while roads were submerged. In Kanpur, rainwater entered residential houses, and several roads in Hardoi were seen inundated. At least four people lost their lives in weather-related incidents. In Unnao, a farmer died after being struck by lightning. In Kasganj, a husband, wife, and their daughter were killed when the roof slab of their house collapsed during the storm and rain. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rain alert for 54 districts and a thunderstorm warning for 22 cities today. According to the IMD, a fresh western disturbance has become active over the region, strengthening pre-monsoon conditions. As a result, thunderstorms and rainfall are expected to continue for the time being. During the last 24 hours, rainfall was recorded in 15 cities across the state. Jalaun remained the hottest district with a maximum temperature of 40.8°C. See 3 pictures from Friday- Lucknow's senior meteorological scientist, Atul Kumar Singh, said- The spell of pre-monsoon rain has started in UP. Now the spell of storms and rain will continue in the state until the entry of monsoon. In between, the heat will also show its intensity, but the rain will continue to provide relief from it.
