stories.title: Five-year-old asks when father will return:Deoria family mourns Merchant Navy worker killed after reported US strike near Hormuz
stories.summary: The family of Shivanand Chaurasia, a 38-year-old Merchant Navy crew member from Deoria district, is mourning his reported death in a U.S. strike while he was serving aboard the Singapore-registered oil tanker MT Settebello. His father, Ramji Chaurasia, said the family had borrowed nearly ₹6 lakh to finance his son’s Continuous Discharge Certificate (CDC), a mandatory seafarer’s document, and training for a maritime career. “We took loans to send him to work at sea. He was the only earning member of the family. We never imagined his first voyage would become his last,” the grieving father said. Ramji said that the hopes of the entire family were tied to Shivanand. After he got the job, happiness had returned to the house. Now there is only silence in the house. The screams and sobs rising from the house are making everyone's eyes moist. His wife is repeatedly fainting. His mother and sisters are in a terrible state from crying. Dainik Bhaskar reached Shivanand's village. Read the report… See 3 pictures Five-year-old son keeps asking for his father Shivanand is survived by his wife Sushila, a five-year-old son, Rajveer, and a two-year-old daughter, Vanika. According to the family, the young boy is unaware of his father’s death and repeatedly asks, “When will Papa come home?” His relatives are struggling to comfort him as the household copes with the tragedy. Journey from village to merchant navy A resident of Surauli village, around 10 km from Deoria district headquarters, Shivanand completed his schooling before leaving home in 2012 in search of work. He worked in several cities, including Dubai, Mumbai, Lucknow, Pune, and Solapur, before completing a Merchant Navy course and obtaining his CDC certification. The family financed the process through loans from relatives and villagers. In September 2025, he joined a shipping company in Singapore as an engine fitter with a monthly salary of around ₹45,000. Father says, ‘Decision to stay on ship proved fatal’ Ramji Chaurasia said the vessel had unloaded oil in China on May 23, after which some colleagues advised Shivaanand to leave the ship and take a break. However, hoping to repay the family’s debts quickly, he decided to remain on board. According to his father, another vessel operated by the same company had suffered technical problems before reaching the Strait of Hormuz, leading to cargo being transferred onto MT Settebello. The family says Shivaanand was killed when the vessel reportedly came under attack near Hormuz on Wednesday. They were informed of the incident through his younger brother, who received communication from the Indian Embassy in Oman. Wife recalls final conversation Sushila said her husband called on Tuesday evening and asked about the children’s well-being. “When the children started crying, he told me to put them to sleep first and call him back later,” she recalled. The call ended, and she never spoke to him again. The following day, after she failed to reach him, relatives eventually informed her that his ship had reportedly been struck. Family appeals for early repatriation of body Sanjay Chaurasia, Shivaanand’s brother-in-law, appealed to the government to ensure the body is brought back to India as soon as possible. He said the family has not yet received a clear timeline regarding the repatriation and is anxiously awaiting official information. Local administration assures assistance Additional District Magistrate Prem Narayan Singh visited the family to offer condolences and assured them that efforts were underway to bring Shivaanand’s remains back to India. Officials expressed hope that the repatriation process could be completed within the next few days. Younger brother returning From Dubai Shivaanand’s younger brother, Ram Pravesh Chaurasia, who had recently moved to Dubai for work, has returned to India after learning of the tragedy. He is expected to reach the family’s ancestral village after arriving in Gorakhpur.

stories.title: Minister Nishad furious over Ghazipur encounter:Says he will complain to CM Yogi; Maurya orders probe
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Minister Sanjay Nishad has raised questions over the encounter of Ghazipur’s Kamlesh Bind, saying that the main accused in the Vineet Rai murder case are still at large and similar action should be taken against them. He alleged that the action reflects bias against the Nishad-Bind community and claimed that some officials are creating an anti-government atmosphere. He also said he would complain to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, warning that such incidents could prove politically damaging in an election year. Meanwhile, Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya has clearly stated that the Ghazipur encounter will be investigated. He said that if any kind of negligence is found, strict action will be taken against those responsible. The case relates to the killing of hotel businessman Alok Rai’s son, Vineet Rai, on the night of 29 May in Ghazipur, when four miscreants allegedly shot him dead. Vineet’s father had named Katra gang leader Shankar Pandey, Sonu Yadav, Kamlesh Bind and Monu Tripathi in the FIR. Kamlesh Bind was killed in an encounter on the night of 3 June and carried a reward of ₹1 lakh. The other accused—Shankar Pandey, Sonu Yadav and Monu Tripathi—are still absconding, with rewards of ₹1 lakh on Shankar and ₹50,000 each on the others. First read what Keshav Maurya said Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya, who was in Prayagraj on Saturday, also took a swipe at the opposition. He said that police sometimes have to take strict steps to control crime, and if any complaint is received from the family or others, it is investigated. He added that the Ghazipur encounter case will also be probed. He also said that the Samajwadi Party has no moral right to question law and order, adding that some parties have become “unemployed” after losing power and are now raising questions against the government. Now read what Sanjay Nishad said Cabinet Minister Sanjay Nishad, speaking to the media at his residence in Vikramaditya Marg, Lucknow, said that criminals have no caste, but if someone was accused, they should have been punished through legal proceedings. He claimed that Kamlesh Bind was not the main accused in the Vineet Rai case and raised questions over police action. He demanded that if the police had to carry out an encounter, it should have been done against the main accused. He also said that the victim’s wife has alleged her husband was tortured at the police station before being killed in an encounter, and such allegations require an independent and fair investigation. He further said that the law allows accused persons to surrender in court, but now police are arresting people even from court premises and gates. He questioned why intelligence units did not anticipate possible backlash and also raised concerns over inadequate police arrangements during the handling of the body. Responding to threats of invoking the National Security Act (NSA) against rioters, Nishad said that if action is to be taken, it should be taken against him first. He alleged discriminatory treatment against the Nishad-Bind community and warned that it would not be accepted. He also said he would raise the issue with Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, alleging that some officials are working in a way that creates an anti-government atmosphere. He warned that such actions could have political consequences in the election year. Nishad also said he himself has faced police harassment and false cases in the past, and demanded investigation into such cases to ensure no innocent person is wronged in the name of law and order. Kamlesh's encounter took place on the 37th day of marriage Kamlesh Bind was married just 37 days before his encounter, on 27 April, to Manisha, a nursing student from Bihar. His wife has claimed that he was innocent and was picked up by police from Rampur. She alleged that she and her sister-in-law were detained at the police station and that he was beaten before being taken to a forest and killed in an encounter. Vineet Rai, on the other hand, had been married for a year and had a two-month-old daughter when he was killed on 29 May. Police say Shankar Pandey is a notorious criminal operating a gang called “Katra Gang,” which runs through a WhatsApp group used to coordinate crimes such as robbery and extortion.

stories.title: Lover kills Sitapur student after learning of her pregnancy:Bones, clothes recovered after 10 days from forest near Lucknow
stories.summary: After a BSc student from Sitapur became pregnant, her lover murdered her. The accused lured her to Lucknow and, after killing her, dumped her body in the forest. Police said- They had a love affair. After learning about the student's pregnancy, the accused became very disturbed. To avoid the responsibility of marriage, he murdered the young woman. After interrogation of the detained youth, police recovered bones, hair, clothes and slippers from a forest area in Mahipatpur, Lucknow. Police claim the recovered remains and belongings belong to the victim. The deceased has been identified as 19-year-old Mansi, a first-year B.Sc student from Sandana area of Sitapur. She left home for college on May 25 but never returned. Her family accused her boyfriend Vishal Pal of abducting her. When the girl was not traced, her family also staged protests. After this, police detained Vishal and began questioning him. Based on his information, police recovered skeletal remains from a forest in Lucknow on June 6. However, DNA and forensic tests are underway to confirm identification. Meanwhile, in Sitapur, Vishal Pal was shot in the leg by police while allegedly trying to escape from custody. 3 pictures of the crime scene Know the full story Mansi, daughter of Mahesh from Sandana village in Sitapur, was a first-year B.Sc student. Vishal Pal and his sister Shivani Pal, from Saraiya village, also studied with her. According to the father, Vishal, through his sister, lured Mansi into a relationship. On May 25, Vishal allegedly took Mansi with him. The father said she left for college as usual but never returned, causing concern in the family. Later, it was found that Vishal and his sister had taken her away after luring her. Her mobile phone was also switched off. The father filed a complaint, but immediate action was not taken. An FIR was registered on May 28. Protest after delay in FIR The father said he was not satisfied with the initial police response and continued meeting senior officials. After no action, he staged a protest with villagers. Following the protest on June 2, police began action. On assurances from officials that the girl would be traced within a few days, the protest was withdrawn. Father started protest when FIR was not registered The father said police later took him to Lucknow on Saturday, claiming his daughter had been found. However, they took him to a forest where they showed clothes, slippers, bones and hair. He alleged that only skeletal remains were found and not the complete body. He demanded strict action, saying others may also be involved and police officials responsible for delay should also be suspended. ACP said - identification will be done by DNA ACP BKT Vikas Pandey said- Remains of a young woman have been found in the forest. The father has identified her by his daughter's clothes and slippers. The deceased's lover has confessed to Sitapur police that they had an affair. The girl had become pregnant. The lover brought his girlfriend to Lucknow on a pretext and killed her. The remains recovered from the forest have been taken into custody and necessary action is being taken. DNA testing will be conducted. Police encountered the accused in Sitapur On June 6, while being taken for recovery of evidence, accused Vishal Pal allegedly tried to escape near a village road in Rampur Madhia area. He attempted to fire at police and flee. Police retaliated, injuring him in the leg. He was arrested and admitted to hospital. The police team retaliated with fire. Vishal Pal was shot in the leg. Police apprehended him and admitted him to the hospital. Killed for pressuring for marriage During interrogation, Vishal Pal said he was in a relationship with Mansi. She was around three months pregnant. On May 25, he took her on a motorcycle to a secluded area along the Kisan Path road in BKT area of Lucknow. They argued over marriage and living together. In anger, he strangled her. To destroy evidence, he placed a cement pillar on her neck and left the body at the spot before returning home.

Khan Sir’s guards allegedly opened fire, tampered with evidence:What happened during the June 2 coaching centre attack?
stories.summary: Khan Sir came out of his building. Guards were already stationed at the coaching gate. Several bouncers were also present there. Out of more than 20 people gathered, over 10 guards were carrying large weapons. After a brief conversation with the guards, Khan Sir allegedly said, “Fire, create fear.” Following this, firing started at the spot. It is also claimed that from the Dargha side, people arrived in 3–4 vehicles towards Khan Sir’s side. During Bhaskar’s investigation, these revelations were made by a student preparing for the Sub-Inspector exam. On June 2 night, vandalism had taken place at Khan Sir’s coaching institute. Following a firing video, police arrested two guards of Khan Sir in this case, and an FIR has also been registered against Khan Sir. In Bhaskar’s investigation, the reporter visited the ground reality of what happened on June 2 at Khan Sir’s coaching institute. In the Musallahpur Hat area, the reporter met teacher Sujal Rai, who was present at the time of the incident. Sujal is a physical education teacher and lives near the coaching institute. Reporter- Do you know what happened during the violence? Sujal- Nothing much happened, we were there the whole night. It was a mutual issue. Reporter- Was there firing? Sujal- No one was shot. People came from inside, fired in the air and went back inside. Reporter- A video shows Khan Sir’s guard firing. Sujal- Whoever is deployed there will have guards. If firing is needed, it will be done. No one fires directly at people; it is always in the air. Reporter- Does Roushan Sir also have guards? Sujal- They are falsely implicating Roushan by showing wrong things. Reporter- Was Khan Sir’s guard beaten? Sujal- That was not even Khan Sir’s guard; he was a cold storage guard. Reporter- But everyone says he was Khan Sir’s guard? Sujal- No, this is being exaggerated. Earlier Ravi Bhai was the guard but he moved to Danapur. A new guard had come in his place. Reporter- Who all were present there? Sujal- We were there, but from Khan Sir’s side, people also came in 3–4 vehicles from the Dargha side. Reporter- How did the situation escalate? Sujal- There was a minor clash, but it has been exaggerated. Reporter- What about banners? Sujal- It is a usual dispute over banners. No one intentionally tore banners; they fell during the scuffle. Reporter- Was firing done after the clash? Sujal- No, after a long gap Khan Sir came out with guards and then aerial firing happened. Reporter- Did Khan Sir have weapons? Sujal- Yes, he has a licensed weapon. Everyone saw it that day. Reporter- Who fired? Sujal- The guards fired to build pressure. Reporter- How many rounds were fired? Sujal- Around 3–4 rounds were fired, and they even collected the cartridges. Reporter- Why were cartridges collected? Sujal- No..no, look those people threw bricks. Everyone had calmed down. Later these people came and did the firing. Reporter- One thing is not clear, why was firing done in the air? Sujal- This was done to create an atmosphere. Reporter- Why did they pick up the shell casings? Sujal- Based on the shell casings, police would have caught them. Reporter- What is the main reason behind this controversy? Sujal- Look, the uncle of the entire building is close to Khan Sir, all those people want Gyan Bindu to be removed from there. Reporter- What do you think will happen now? Sujal- You will see, one day everyone together will remove Gyan Bindu's office, classroom and library from there. During the investigation, Bhaskar reporters also met student Rohan who was present at the spot during the incident. His name has been changed to protect identity, as there is fear of retaliation from coaching operators. The student described how firing allegedly took place in the presence of Khan Sir. According to him, the situation had calmed down but was later escalated again. Reporter- What were you doing there at the time of the incident? Rohan- 3 of us friends were walking towards our hostel after having tea at night, when the commotion started. Reporter- How did you get information? Rohan- Just a while ago, we had received information about a scuffle near Khan Sir's coaching, but the matter had completely calmed down. Reporter- When you were at the spot, what did you see? Rohan- We were passing by the coaching, when there was a commotion in the lane. We thought the scuffle had started again. We ran inside to see. Reporter- Was Khan Sir present there? Rohan- No, at that very time he came down with his guards, as soon as he came out, commotion started. Reporter- Who else were there with Khan Sir? Rohan- At the coaching gate, there were already about 20 people with him, including guards and bouncers along with some other people. Reporter- Did these people have weapons too? Rohan- Khan Sir had a weapon, it was visible. More than 10 guards present there with Khan Sir also had big weapons visible. Reporter- How did the firing happen, did you people see? Rohan- After talking to his people, Khan Sir told the guard to fire, everyone, create fear. Reporter- Did Khan Sir also fire? Rohan- No, Khan Sir went inside, as soon as he left, the guard fired 3 rounds one after another. Reporter- Then what happened, there must have been chaos? Rohan- Hearing the sound of the gunshot, we got scared and ran away from there. During the investigation, the Bhaskar reporter met students who were present at the spot at the time of the incident. In this sequence, the Bhaskar reporter met Rakesh, who was preparing for general competition. Fearing controversy and violence at the coaching center, he first refused to say anything, but after a while Rakesh told us the whole story. Reporter- What do you do? Rakesh- We prepare for general competition here. Reporter- What were you doing there at the time of the incident? Rakesh- I live in the lodge right next door, the mess is there, we were returning after having food. Reporter- How did you come to know about the commotion? Rakesh- We were returning after having food, during that time sounds were coming. We went inside. Reporter- When you reached the spot, what was happening inside? Rakesh- We were on the road itself, many people had gathered there. Suddenly there was a sound of gunfire, hearing the gunshot people started running out from inside rapidly. Reporter- Was Khan Sir present at the spot at the time of the incident? Rakesh- No, Khan Sir was not there. Reporter- Who was firing the gun? Rakesh- We didn't see that, but the shell was hot, the guard picked it up and put it in his pocket and went inside. Reporter- What happened after that? Rakesh- Now leave it, this is all coaching rivalry, whoever gets involved in this will get trapped. Reporter- That's right, but tell us something? Rakesh- Avoiding the topic, we have come here to study, if we get caught in their mess then our work won't get done either. Now know the complete story of the dispute Khan Sir’s coaching and Knowledge Bind coaching operate in the same lane. Both are good institutes and both produce results. Earlier they had fewer students, but gradually student numbers increased. Both started renting nearby buildings. Currently, there are 4–5 coaching institutes in the lane. Most buildings are rented by Khan Sir, while some are with Knowledge Bind. Both have offices, classrooms, and libraries there. The building where Knowledge Bind runs belongs to a person close to Khan Sir. It is said that Khan Sir has long wanted Knowledge Bind to vacate the place so that he can establish control over the area. On June 2, both institutes had called selected Bihar Police candidates for a felicitation event. Banners of both institutes were put up. During this, a dispute arose over one banner being placed over another. It is said that Knowledge Bind’s banner was placed under Khan Sir’s banner. Roshan Anand and his associates went there to object. The building guard stopped them, after which a clash took place. After this, stone pelting started from the Knowledge Bind side. The situation calmed down for some time. Later, a crowd gathered. Then Khan Sir came down with his guards and bouncers, and to escalate the matter into a bigger case, firing was allegedly done by his own guards so that action could be taken against Knowledge Bind. Reason for repeated disturbances is control over campus The dispute between Khan Sir and Roshan Anand of Knowledge Bind is old. Earlier also, staff and teachers of both institutes have faced each other several times. The main reason for repeated clashes is control over the entire campus area. On March 10, 2021, Khan Sir had also filed a case against Roshan, his brother, and 20 unknown people for allegedly entering the coaching with weapons, assaulting, and attempting to kill.

stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. CJP stages 5-hour protest at Jantar Mantar Cockroach Janata Party held a five-hour protest at Jantar Mantar over alleged NEET and exam irregularities, demanding Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation. Thousands of students and supporters joined Abhijeet Dipke, with Sonam Wangchuk’s backing. Police detained six as heavy security remained deployed across Delhi today. 2. Jesus’s ‘holy blood’ served in UP’s secret church An undercover investigation alleged a conversion network operating in UP’s Lakhimpur Kheri, where vulnerable people were reportedly persuaded to abandon traditional religious practices and embrace Christianity through prayer meetings and promises of relief from hardships. Organisers denied it was conversion, calling it “life transformation” instead. 3. Meerut CMO under probe for favouring ex-MLA Dr Ashok Kataria attached to Lucknow Health Directorate after claims of favouring firms linked to former Congress MLA Mukesh Srivastava. Probe alleges hospital contracts, unverified payments and procurement irregularities worth crores. Vigilance is also investigating the NHM scam and disproportionate assets case. 4. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi youngest Indian picked in men's cricket India announced squads for Ireland, England tours and Asian Games on Saturday, with Shreyas Iyer being named new T20I captain, replacing Suryakumar Yadav. Moreover, 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi was also selected for the Team India duties after his stellar form in IPL 2026. 5. Dimple Chaudhary shares second misbehaviour video Haryanvi dancer releases second video alleging repeated inappropriate behaviour by a youth during a Hathras performance. She says the incident caused severe mental distress, forced her to switch off her phone, and sparked questions from family and society. 6. Friend kills coaching operator for gold, hides identity in burqa Police arrested 18-year-old friend Mohit Dwivedi, who allegedly plotted the robbery for 15 days after spotting gold jewellery worth ₹10 lakh. Investigators say he watched Crime Patrol, searched YouTube for ways to avoid detection, disguised himself in a burqa and killed Vijay Gupta during a robbery attempt. 7. CBSE extends Class 12 verification and re-evaluation deadline The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) has extended the last date for applying for verification and re-evaluation of Class 12 board exam answer sheets from June 6 to June 7. 8. Johnny-Jojo who made Premanand Maharaj laugh go missing Comedian Rahul Mishra lost the famous puppet characters in an e-rickshaw after completing the Vrindavan parikrama. Police have launched a search after Rahul alleged the driver sped away when he tried to recover the bag containing the beloved puppets. 9. Yogi’s birthday marked with bulldozer cake cut near Eiffel Tower Supporters marked the occasion with special events across India and abroad. stories.title: 2-storey mosque demolished with bulldozer in Sambhal:55-foot minaret pulled down with crane; ‘I Love Mohammad’ posters found
stories.summary: A mosque named Mustafa Qadri, allegedly built on government cemetery land in Sambhal, was demolished using bulldozers on Saturday. The mosque, located in Kaserua village of the Nakhasa area, was first dismantled from the front portion and pillars before its 55-foot-high minaret was brought down using a hydra machine. The District Magistrate and Superintendent of Police were present at the site during the demolition drive. Officials recovered posters bearing the words “I Love Mohammad” and a green flag from the mosque’s first floor. The SP said action would be taken against those responsible for printing and displaying such posters. The demolition was carried out following an order from the Tehsildar Court, which directed the removal of encroachment from around 120 square metres of government land. Four bulldozers, dumpers, tractors and 20 sanitation workers from Sirsi Nagar Panchayat were deployed for the operation. Before the action began, members of the Muslim community offered prayers at the mosque. The administration then removed glass panels and gates. Police also evacuated houses around the mosque premises. More than 100 police personnel were deployed in the village to maintain law and order. See 5 pictures... Read the full matter The Tehsildar Court had passed an eviction order against the mosque committee on April 21. The committee later appealed in the District Magistrate’s court, but no stay order or relief was granted. Following this, the administration decided to proceed with the demolition. Tehsildar Dhirendra Kumar Singh constituted a special team for the operation and appointed Naib Tehsildar Deepak Kumar Jurail as the campaign in-charge. The revenue department sought four JCB machines, dumpers, tractors and 20 sanitation workers from Sambhal Municipality and Sirsi Nagar Panchayat. According to revenue records, plot number 409 is designated as cemetery land. The administration claims that the mosque had been constructed on nearly 120 square metres of this land. Three residential houses were also allegedly built on the same plot. Officials further stated that plot number 410, recorded as land reserved for manure pits, had around 600 square metres occupied by eight houses. Part of plot number 411, reserved for plantation, was also allegedly being used for cultivation. Around 1,000 people offered prayers at the mosque Mosque caretaker Zakir Hussain said the mosque dates back several generations and was rebuilt around 20–25 years ago at a cost exceeding ₹50 lakh. Villagers alleged that their side was not properly heard during proceedings in the Tehsildar Court. Local resident Javed said they received no prior information about the demolition and only learned about it on Saturday morning. He claimed the mosque was older than previous land consolidation exercises and had been used by local families for generations. He added that around 1,000 people offered Friday prayers at the two-storey mosque and that the village population itself was close to 1,000. Action will be taken against those who printed posters - SP Mosque committee could not provide evidence Tehsildar Dhirendra Kumar Singh said villagers had filed complaints seeking protection of cemetery land. During the inquiry, officials found that the mosque had been built on cemetery land, leading to proceedings under Section 67 of the Revenue Code. He said the mosque committee was given full opportunity to present its case but failed to produce any document or evidence proving that the structure stood on private land. The court subsequently issued an eviction order. For the operation, police personnel from several stations, including Nakhasa, Kailadevi and Raysatti, were deployed along with women police officers and 60 PAC personnel. FIR was registered earlier as well In January 2026, an FIR was registered against seven individuals based on a complaint by a revenue official. They were accused of submitting incorrect documents and facts in an attempt to have the land declared Waqf property and of illegally occupying village community land. Sambhal has witnessed several anti-encroachment drives on government land in recent months. Last year, authorities cleared encroachments in the Sher Khan Sarai area, while on June 5 an alleged illegal religious structure built on government land in Baghau village of Gunnaur was also removed. Officials said the campaign against encroachments on government land would continue and that future action would be based on revenue records. Administration's action so far in 4 points

stories.title: Man fires 10 rounds, pushes police officer in Mathura:Cop warns, ‘Put the gun down before someone gets shot’
stories.summary: A dramatic half-hour standoff unfolded on a Mathura road between a local strongman carrying a licensed revolver and a police officer who tried to disarm him. When the officer attempted to seize the weapon, the accused resisted, pushing and shoving him, issuing threats and engaging in a scuffle. The officer repeatedly warned him to put the gun down, saying it could accidentally go off. However, the accused refused to comply. After considerable effort, police finally managed to overpower him. The incident took place in Krishna Nagar, one of Mathura’s busiest and most affluent areas frequented by tourists. A large crowd gathered at the scene, causing a lengthy traffic jam on both sides of the road. Earlier, the accused had allegedly fired multiple rounds from his licensed revolver at Bhuteshwar Akhada. According to eyewitnesses, he arrived at the wrestling arena in a white Scorpio SUV on Friday night and opened fire immediately after stepping out of the vehicle. Panic spread through the area as people ran for safety. Hearing the gunshots and screams, local residents and wrestlers from the akhada rushed to the spot and informed the police. Before officers could arrive, the accused abandoned his vehicle and fled on foot while carrying the revolver. Frightened by the sight of an armed man running through the streets, people hid wherever they could. Police chased him for nearly a kilometre before finally catching him. Six empty cartridge cases were recovered from the accused. Police are examining video footage and CCTV recordings as part of the investigation. The incident took place around 9 pm in the Kotwali police station area. 3 Pictures- Now understand the entire matter in a sequential manner- Accused clashes with police on busy road Police intercepted the accused nearly one kilometre away in the Krishna Nagar area. He reportedly stood in the middle of the road holding the revolver, causing panic among bystanders. When officers asked him to hand over the weapon, he allegedly began threatening them and refused to cooperate. He then got into a scuffle with Krishna Nagar outpost in-charge Sanjeev Kumar and Sub-Inspector Mustaq Mohammad Mehndi. Police eventually dragged him to the roadside and forcibly seized the revolver. During a search, officers also recovered empty cartridge cases from his possession. The accused remains in custody and is being questioned. Six empty cartridge cases were recovered from the scene.

stories.title: Ayushman Bharat beneficiaries at BHU rise 35-fold since 2018:Over 34,000 patients treated under scheme; beneficiaries from Bihar and Jharkhand also seek care
stories.summary: The number of patients receiving treatment under the Ayushman Bharat Scheme at Sir Sundarlal Hospital of Banaras Hindu University (BHU) has increased significantly since the scheme was launched in 2018. According to data released by the university administration, the number of beneficiaries has risen nearly 35-fold over the years. Apart from Uttar Pradesh, a large number of patients from Bihar and Jharkhand are also receiving treatment at the hospital. Dr Rajeev, Medical Superintendent of BHU, said Sir Sundarlal Hospital is often referred to as the "AIIMS of Purvanchal" and treats more than 10,000 patients every day. He said cancer, heart disease, diabetes and other medicine-related ailments account for the largest share of patients receiving treatment under the scheme. Since 2018, a total of 34,363 patients have availed treatment benefits under Ayushman Bharat at the hospital. Bihar payment delays raised with Centre A dispute over delayed payments for Bihar patients treated under the scheme surfaced earlier this year. On February 5, concerns were raised that the Bihar government was not releasing payments for treatment costs on time. Following the issue, the BHU administration wrote to the Union Health Ministry seeking intervention. Buxar MP Sudhakar Singh also wrote to the Bihar Chief Minister, expressing concern over nearly ₹8 crore in pending dues for the treatment of Bihar patients at the hospital's Trauma Centre. Pending dues now being cleared Dr Rajeev said the pending payments have now started arriving, ensuring that patient treatment continues without any hurdles. He said the hospital never stopped treating patients despite delays in reimbursements. No patient was denied treatment, provided their documents were complete. Nearly 15,000 patients treated in last two years According to BHU administration data, 14,912 patients received treatment under the Ayushman Bharat Scheme at the hospital during the past two years. The beneficiaries included: Hospital officials said the scheme has helped thousands of economically weaker patients access specialised treatment that would otherwise be difficult to afford. Centre and states share scheme costs Ayushman Bharat is jointly funded by the Central and State governments. In most states, the Centre and states share the cost in a 60:40 ratio. For northeastern and Himalayan states, the funding pattern is 90:10. In Union Territories without legislative assemblies, the Central government bears the entire cost of the scheme.

stories.title: Dimple Chaudhary shares another video of man attempting to misbehave:Haryanvi dancer touched inappropriately in Hathras; demands justice
stories.summary: Haryanvi dancer Dimple Chaudhary has released a second video showing alleged misbehaviour during a stage performance in Hathras, Uttar Pradesh. The footage appears to show a young man crossing the barricade and attempting to touch her inappropriately while she was performing. Reacting to the incident, Dimple said she has been facing questions from family members and society ever since the video surfaced. She said she was forced to switch off her phone and has been mentally distressed and uncomfortable for several days. “I want justice,” she said. The incident took place on June 3 during a dance. During the performance, a young man allegedly touched Dimple's waist. In protest, she slapped him on stage. Dimple later shared a video of the incident, bringing the matter into the public spotlight. stories.title: Johnny-Jojo who made Premanand Maharaj laugh go missing:Comedian Rahul allegedly forgot them in e-rickshaw; Vrindavan police launch search
stories.summary: The teddy bear cartoons Johnny-Jojo that made Premanand Maharaj laugh have gone missing. Johnny and Jojo are puppets of Rahul, a famous comedian artist from Jaipur. Rahul Mishra had come to Vrindavan with his friend to do the parikrama. When he returned after completing the parikrama, he forgot his bag in the e-rickshaw. As soon as Rahul remembered his bag, he stopped the e-rickshaw driver, but instead of stopping, he ran away. Rahul has filed a complaint with the police about Johnny-Jojo going missing. Now Vrindavan police are engaged in searching for the e-rickshaw driver and Jojo. Comedian Rahul had come to Vrindavan for Parikrama Rahul Mishra had come to Vrindavan on Thursday with his friend to do the Parikrama. After completing the Parikrama that night, Rahul took an e-rickshaw from near Chamunda Temple. He was heading to Hotel Sukhdham located on Keshav Dham Road. Meanwhile, he remembered his bag, in which his cartoon characters Johnny Jojo were kept. It was around 1 AM at night. Rahul chased the e-rickshaw to get his bag, but instead of stopping, the e-rickshaw driver fled. Rahul became sad over Jojo's disappearance. He reached Vrindavan Kotwali on Friday and filed a complaint with the police. The police are searching for the e-rickshaw driver through CCTV cameras installed around the hotel. Rahul's emotional connection with Johnny-Jojo Saddened by the disappearance of Johnny-Jojo, Rahul said - I have an emotional connection with both of them. He has entertained Premanand Maharaj through Johnny-Jojo. Rahul said that somehow I should get my Johnny and Jojo back soon. The comedian has also made an emotional appeal on social media searching for Johnny-Jojo. He said that both of them are my life, whoever has taken them, please return them. Station House Officer Sanjay Pandey informed that a case has been registered in the matter and a search is being conducted for Johnny and Jojo. Had met Premanand Ji a year ago A year ago, during a meeting with Premanand Ji Maharaj in Vrindavan, Jojo and Johnny had conversed with him. At which he kept laughing continuously and said- 'How do these toys speak by themselves? This is a wonderful art.' He had also appreciated this art a lot. Rahul had said - Premanandji gave 500-500 as rewards to my Jojo and Johnny. He honored me and made me accept prasad. Young people like us are his devotees and follow his words and discourses. As soon as I came out, the Brijwasis surrounded me. Everyone started saying that we have never seen Maharajji laughing so much, you have done wonders. Rahul started his career with theater, but due to insufficient earnings in this field, he created a YouTube channel in 2015. His friends made him a puppet, with which he created videos. His videos went viral on TikTok, but real success came when he further refined his art and reached bigger platforms. Rahul has been part of many big shows. He reached the Bigg Boss set for a special performance. He has also showcased his art on India's Got Talent.

stories.title: Weather turns across 43 districts in UP:Heavy rain alert in Mau, Ghazipur; storm alert in 21 districts
stories.summary: The spell of thunderstorms and rain continues across Uttar Pradesh. Weather conditions changed suddenly on Saturday afternoon. After bright sunshine since morning, Mau and Ghazipur received heavy rainfall around 2 pm. Strong winds blowing at speeds of nearly 50 kmph accompanied thunderclouds. Gorakhpur also witnessed a dust storm. The change in weather brought relief from the intense heat that had prevailed since morning. Late on Friday night, Varanasi also received heavy rain accompanied by lightning. The weather turned pleasant after nearly half an hour of torrential rainfall. Kaushambi witnessed light drizzle in the morning. In Amethi, a mother and daughter died after a mud wall collapsed, while a boy sustained serious injuries. Earlier in the day, districts including Lucknow and Kanpur witnessed bright sunshine. However, humidity in the air kept temperatures slightly lower than usual. The Meteorological Department has issued a light rain alert for 43 districts across the state, while 21 districts are likely to witness thunderstorms and strong winds. Weather experts said the impact of the western disturbance will end within the next 24 hours. Atul Kumar Singh, Senior Meteorologist at the Regional Meteorological Center in Lucknow, said- Even today, there is a possibility of storms, strong winds, and scattered drizzles in UP. From tomorrow, all rain systems will cease. Then, there will be intense heat until the monsoon rains. Heatwave conditions will also develop. Considering the current circumstances, the monsoon is likely to enter the state via Gorakhpur by June 24. With that, the spell of rain and thunderstorms that has continued for the past 12 days is expected to come to an end. Temperatures are then likely to rise sharply, with mercury expected to jump by 5°C to 6°C and cross 45°C. A fresh spell of heatwave conditions is also likely to begin from June 9. During the previous 24 hours, strong winds and intermittent rain were recorded in districts including Lucknow, Mau, Bijnor and Agra. In most other districts, strong sunshine pushed temperatures higher. Varanasi was the hottest city in the state with a maximum temperature of 42.2°C, while Hardoi recorded the lowest night temperature at 22°C. Based on current weather patterns, the monsoon is expected to enter Uttar Pradesh through the Gorakhpur region by around June 24. Heavy rain lashed Varanasi late on Friday night, accompanied by thunder and lightning.

stories.title: Jesus’s ‘holy blood’ served in UP’s secret church:Pastor questions idol worship; reporter’s conversion caught on camera
stories.summary: "You people have done a lot of idol worship before coming here, what benefit did you get? You don't have to do all this now. If you go to a temple, don't eat prasad. This is the holy blood of Jesus (red colored juice), it will bring healing (end illness) to the body, you will get rid of difficulties." A pastor who had arrived from Nepal allegedly converted a Dainik Bhaskar reporter—who was posing as a labourer in front of him—to Christianity. According to inputs, such conversion meetings are held every Sunday in a “secret church” in a village in Uttar Pradesh’s Lakhimpur Kheri district. It is alleged that to avoid police scrutiny, only the religion is changed while names and caste identities remain unchanged. In the ongoing investigation, it has been reported that when the Bhaskar reporter reached the village in disguise, he was called inside and gradually influenced. The sacred thread (kalava) was allegedly removed, and instructions were given to stop worshipping traditional deities. The full investigation now reveals a pattern of alleged inducement, conversion attempts, surveillance, and systematic religious change. We were called to Pastor Vijay's house in Dalrajpur village of Lakhimpur Kheri district. Here again, 3 people surrounded the reporter and started tempting him... Shivprasad's wife: If you accept this (religion), you will get healed (disease will end) very quickly. Pastor Vijay: (Elaborating on the woman's statement) This is their face today. Tell us after 10-15 days. Shivprasad's wife: Oh, what 15 days, it will happen right now. Just accept it. We will pray. In their name. We did it immediately. We said - brother, free us from this. We have become very troubled. Reporter: We also want to accept it. Shivprasad's wife: (laughing) We understand your pain, brother, but it takes time. Baba has left Nepal. After agreeing to convert to Christianity, we left from there. He asked us to call at 1 PM. When we called, Pastor Vijay said - You come over, Guruji has arrived from Nepal. We reached the spot within half an hour. After that, the game of religious conversion began. Pastor Vijay: We will get you converted very soon, you will have to dedicate your life, you will have to give your life to the Lord quickly. Reporter: Whatever you say, we will do. Nepali Pastor Jeevan: If you want to convert, you can do it now. Reporter: If we convert, will the routine of life change somewhat? Will we have to do something? Nepali Pastor Jeevan: What is that right now you are a slave to sin, whatever it wants you to do, you do. When you accept Jesus, you come out of that sin. (After this, Pastor Vijay showed us Bible verses on his mobile) Pastor Vijay: So are you ready to give your life to the Lord? Reporter: Yes. Nepali Pastor Jeevan: This is not religious conversion, this is our life transformation. Today you have a life of addiction, tomorrow if you are cured, that is not religion, that is life transformation. We want to change your life. Pastor Vijay: Our caste hasn't changed. Language hasn't changed. Whatever is written on our Aadhaar card, it should remain the same. Reporter: Like the kalawa (sacred thread) was cut, there are many such worship items kept at home. Then what will be done about them? Pastor Vijay: We will reach your home. Gradually, that will be removed from your mind. After this, beginning the acceptance process, Pastor Vijay started the prayer and asked the reporter to repeat. Pastor Vijay: Lord, I am a sinful man. I confess all my sins and unrighteousness. Lord, you left heaven for me and came to this world. You took my sins upon yourself and gave your life. And I believe. God raised you to life on the third day. From today I accept you into my life calling you my Savior Lord. From today I accept you calling you my Master, calling you Savior. From today I surrender my life into your hands. From today may you take control of my life. Lord Jesus, these are your living names. Amen. Nepali Pastor Jeevan: Now that you have accepted Jesus, you have become a child of Jesus. Now to leave the bad habits, Pastor ji will fellowship with you. As you come into fellowship, the bad habits will be left behind. Reporter: Like we did the acceptance prayer, now what changes will come in our life? Nepali Pastor Jeevan: Now after going home, you will not do worship and all that. Pastor Vijay: Look, you are new, after waking up in the morning you can make a phone call. When waking up, at sleeping time we will do prayer. Reporter: The worship and incense sticks etc. that we light in the morning, should we do that or not? Pastor Vijay: (Shaking his head in refusal) Don't worship. Nepali Pastor Jeevan: It makes a difference from idol worship, because we don't do idol worship. Before you people came here, you had done a lot of idol worship, right? So what benefit did you get? You don't have to do all that. Whatever Pastor ji says, you have to do accordingly. Reporter: Do we need to tell anyone right now or not, in the family, among friends? Pastor Vijay: Don't tell anyone right now. Tell the family, but later. Nepali Pastor Jeevan: Right now you just say this - Jesus, heal me. After this, Nepali Pastor Jeevan offered a final prayer for the reporter. After the conversion, the reporter was advised to call Pastor Vijay morning and evening. We called Vijay twice daily for a week. He repeatedly asked to come home. Along with that, he kept reminding that you belong to Jesus and also tempted with the promise of ending the illness soon. Reporter: Guruji, I want to ask one thing - we are going home and my wife is very religious. She will want to do puja-paath (worship rituals), so should I stop her or what should I do? Pastor Vijay: Well, you haven't learned much from us yet, but when the whole family comes in line, it will be good. Just as you accepted Jesus that day. You became His son, became His servant, similarly we will make your wife accept too. The Lord has said that if one person trusts in Me, I will save his entire household. The Lord will definitely help, will change her (wife's) mind. She will also believe. Reporter: So right now we don't need to do anything, right? If my wife does puja-paath, we should let her do it, right? Pastor Vijay: Yes, let her do it for now. When complete peace comes to your mind, then we will all together explain to her. Reporter: We can't even light incense sticks, right? Pastor Vijay: Can't light them. In the conversation, Pastor Vijay mentioned that their network is connected to Nepal. Pastor Vijay: They (senior religious leaders) live towards Kathmandu. Your matter has been conveyed to them. They are also now praying for you. Reporter: I see, can I meet them? Pastor Vijay: Meeting them happens only with great fortune. We succeeded at every step of the conversion gang. When they were fully convinced, they called us for complete conversion after a week. This time we wanted to expose the entire racket of the gang. Therefore, we included two fellow reporters. We told Pastor Vijay that there are two people we know. One is a Sikh and the other is a Muslim. Both of them are also trapped in troubles, will their problems also end like ours? The pastor immediately asked to bring them to the secret church on Sunday. We reached the healing assembly at 8 AM on Sunday morning. There were 50 men and women in the hall. Pastor Vijay was in front of them. A cross was placed on the table. Vijay was delivering Jesus's teachings. We sat on the chairs arranged there. Where the game of complete conversion of the first reporter and starting the conversion process of the two reporters who accompanied him took place. Pastor Vijay: Today in the arrangement that has been made, you will be included (complete conversion). Reporter: Okay. Shivprasad Gautam: Those who are new people, they will not be included. Only you will be included in this arrangement. After this, prayers were held and people present there were given red-colored juice to drink one by one. This was called the sacred blood of Jesus. Reporter: What is this sherbet? Shivprasad Gautam: No, this is sacred blood. This will bring healing to your body. You will get relief from troubles. The pastor made the reporter stand and introduced him to everyone and then prayed for the reporter. This meant that the reporter's complete conversion had now taken place. Reporter: How can we reach the Guruji from Kathmandu? Pastor Vijay: Now they will only come if called. If everyone says so, we will call them. They will come. They are 60 years old now, but even today their face has more glow than yours. Reporter: What is their name? Pastor Vijay: The name is Ravi Sharma. Gang runs secret church due to fear of police, Shiv Sena and Bajrang Dal We spoke to those people who came to the healing gathering, who have converted from Hindu to Christian. They revealed many secrets related to the secret church and healing gathering... Reporter: What problem did you have? Follower: There was Satan, everyone in the family used to remain ill. Reporter: What does accepting mean? Follower: We start believing in Lord Jesus. Reporter: So then you don't have to do any worship or anything? Did you do worship before? Follower: Yes, we don't have to do worship. Earlier we used to worship a lot. We have even been to Kashi. We used to go carrying Kanwar. Reporter: Do you worship now? Follower: No, we don't worship now. Reporter: Don't you have to change your name or anything? Follower: No, we don't have to change our name or anything. Reporter: Can you go to a temple or shrine and eat prasad (offerings)? Follower: Even if we go to a temple, we don't eat prasad. Whether it's a temple or a shrine. If you have to eat it, then eat it considering it as Jesus's prasad. Reporter: Have your family members also accepted? How did you convince everyone? Follower: When everything started getting better, everyone accepted it. Baba ji also came home. He had explained. Reporter: Many people from your side must have joined then. Do all people also go to church? Follower: Some people go to Nighasan church. Reporter: Do you also go to church? Follower: This is also a church, where we went. Reporter: This is a house? Follower: No, it's a church. Reporter: Are you afraid, there's not even a photo displayed here? Why do you hide it? Follower: Shiv Sena and Bajrang Dal people harass a lot. That's why we hide. If they find out, they will destroy everything. Now know, what came out in our investigation?

stories.title: Meerut CMO under probe for favouring ex-MLA:Allegedly helped him gain crores; NHM scam charge resurfaces
stories.summary: Dr. Ashok Kataria, who was the CMO of Meerut, has been accused of corruption. Following this, he has been attached to the Health Directorate in Lucknow. The allegation is that Dr. Kataria illegally benefited the companies of former Congress MLA Mukesh Srivastava, who was involved in the National Health Mission (NHM) scam, to the tune of crores of rupees. Maintenance contracts for hospitals in Meerut and Shravasti were given to the firm of the former MLA's brother, and then bills were passed without verification. An investigation into these irregularities in the CMO office is being conducted at the Additional Director (AD) level. CMO handed over GeM portal ID to former MLA In 2024, a private firm was given a contract to administer Hepatitis-B vaccines in Muzaffarnagar. The firm was charging people 60 rupees for the vaccine, whereas it should have been free. When the matter came to light, the contract was cancelled, but no action was taken against the responsible Additional Chief Medical Officer Mahesh Chandra. It is alleged that Dr. Ashok Kataria handed over the department's GeM portal (an online public procurement portal of the Government of India) ID to Mukesh Srivastava. Mukesh used it from his private office in Lucknow. In January 2025, when an investigation was conducted at the government level, purchase orders worth approximately 3 crore rupees were cancelled. Later, orders were reissued based on old notesheets. In February, BJP leader from Meerut, Ankit Chaudhary, complained about this to CM Yogi. Former MLA is the main accused in NHM scam Mukesh Srivastava (now SP leader), who was a Congress MLA from Payagpur in Bahraich, is the main accused in the NHM scam that took place in Shravasti. He is accused of embezzling crores in the purchase of medicines, medical equipment and vehicles in hospitals in the district between 2017-22. The vigilance team registered a case on May 30 this year. Along with Mukesh, an FIR has been registered against 6 people including two former CMOs of Shravasti, Dr. Dinesh Kumar Singh and Dr. Vipendra Kumar Singh. Fake bills passed after taking 25% bribe In Shravasti, from 2017 to 22, vouchers were passed without creating a medical reimbursement register. Payments were made after taking 10 to 25% commission. The hospital maintenance work was given to Mukesh's brother's company RP Construction. The company got bills passed by showing work on paper. In the case, an FIR has also been filed against Rajendra Prasad Srivastava, proprietor of RP Group of Construction. A case of disproportionate assets has also been registered against Mukesh Srivastava. The vigilance investigation found that during 2017 to 2022, Mukesh earned approximately Rs 1.12 crore from all legitimate sources, while he spent approximately Rs 1.80 crore. Investigation into the difference between income and expenditure is ongoing.

stories.title: Friend killed coaching operator for gold worth around ₹10 lakh:Watched Crime Patrol, searched YouTube; wore burqa to hide identity
stories.summary: In Kanpur, the murder of coaching operator Vijay Prakash Gupta was allegedly carried out by his 18-year-old friend, Mohit Dwivedi. Police said the motive was robbery, not personal enmity. Mohit allegedly targeted gold bracelets and chains worth around ₹10 lakh. According to Police Commissioner Raghubir Lal, Mohit had been planning the crime for nearly 15 days. During this period, he searched YouTube for ways to kill a friend without revealing his identity and watched several episodes of Crime Patrol to learn how to evade police investigation. To avoid being identified, Mohit allegedly disguised himself in a burqa, ladies' slippers, a purse, a dupatta and gloves. On the night of May 31, he reached the coaching centre in an auto-rickshaw and attempted the robbery. Police said that when Vijay resisted, Mohit pushed him forcefully, causing him to fall and suffer a severe head injury. Vijay lost consciousness and later died. After the incident, Mohit allegedly dragged the body into another room before fleeing. The murder came to light on the morning of June 1, when a female teacher arrived at the coaching centre and found Vijay's blood-soaked body. She immediately alerted the police, who launched an investigation. See 2 pictures- Both went to visit Khajuraho together on Holi Commissioner Raghubir Lal informed- Coaching operator Vijay Prakash Gupta, a resident of Azad Nagar in Nawabganj, and accused Mohit Dwivedi had known each other for the past 18 years. Both ran coaching centers in the same building. They often spent time together. They used to drink alcohol together and also gambled. Mohit's wife had left him several years ago. Some time after this, his coaching center also shut down. Then he started working in labor supply for a company. During Holi, Mohit and Vijay had gone to Khajuraho together for sightseeing. It was there that Mohit's eyes fell on Vijay's gold bracelet and chain worth around 10 lakh rupees. From that very moment, he had started planning to loot these jewels. Bought burqa, ladies' slippers, purse, dupatta, gloves from the market Accused Mohit Dwivedi had planned the robbery around May 15. He watched several episodes of Crime Patrol. He also searched on YouTube how to commit murder by hiding one's identity. About a week before the murder, he went to the weekly Monday market in Nawabganj. From there he bought a burqa, ladies' slippers, purse, dupatta and gloves. He reached near the coaching center wearing a burqa. He also did reconnaissance of all the routes to escape after the robbery. He also checked which routes and places had CCTV cameras installed. Pretended to be mute, reached station to show Kannauj connection After completing the recce, on May 31 at around 3:30 PM in the afternoon, Mohit reached JK Cancer Hospital located in Swaroop Nagar in his car. After parking the car there, he went inside the hospital and came out wearing a burqa after some time. After this, he reached Anwarganj Railway Station by auto. At around 5:30 PM in the evening, he started waiting for the train coming from Kannauj, so that the police would think that the person who committed the crime had come from Kannauj. After the train arrived, Mohit came out of the station and sat in an auto. To prove himself mute, he gave the auto driver Vijay's coaching address written on a slip of paper. The auto driver took him to the coaching center with the help of Google Maps. Reached coaching on pretext of admission, snatched chain-bracelet by pushing Around 6:45 PM in the evening, Mohit got down from the auto about 20 meters before the coaching center. After waiting for about 10 minutes, he reached Vijay Prakash Gupta. He gave a slip and wrote about taking admission in the coaching. On this, Vijay asked him to wait for 10 minutes, saying he was going to take a bath. When Vijay returned after some time, Mohit tried to snatch his gold chain. When he resisted, there was a scuffle between the two. During this, Mohit gave Vijay a strong push, due to which he fell and became unconscious. After this, Mohit looted his gold chain and bracelet. The accused dragged Vijay to another room of the coaching center. Then he fled from the spot. After murder, reached Nawabganj from Swaroop Nagar Inspector Shiv Kumar posted in the cyber cell said - After the murder, the police started examining the footage of CCTV cameras installed nearby. During the investigation, a suspect wearing a burqa was seen at several places. The police examined about 500 CCTV footages. The footage revealed that after the incident, the person wearing the burqa reached Nawabganj through the lanes of Swaroop Nagar. From the guava market near Ganga Barrage, he took an auto and went towards the road leading to Gurudev. After getting down from the auto in Gurudev, he walked towards Rawatpur Station. From there, he took an auto and reached JK Cancer Hospital. After some time, a young man came out of the hospital and sat in a car, heading towards Nawabganj via Motijheel. The young man's face was clearly visible in the CCTV footage. Based on this, the police identified him. After that, Mohit Dwivedi, a resident of Azad Nagar, was taken into custody and interrogated. During interrogation, he broke down and confessed to the murder and robbery. Vijay Prakash's body was found in the coaching centre On Monday morning, the body of coaching operator Vijay Prakash Gupta was found at Data Expert Computer Coaching Institute located in Azad Nagar, Nawabganj. A female teacher who arrived at the coaching center in the morning saw his body lying in the room, after which she raised an alarm. She informed the people nearby. As soon as the information was received, police and forensic team reached the spot and started investigation. The deceased's brother Vikas Gupta had told the police that Vijay's gold chain and bracelet were missing, while 15 thousand rupees were found in his pocket. Based on this, the police had suspected murder after robbery. Accused has completed MA-LLB DCP Central, ADCP, Nawabganj Police and the Surveillance Team were able to reach the accused based on forensic evidence, CCTV footage and technical investigation. During interrogation, Mohit Dwivedi confessed to the entire conspiracy of murder and robbery. Police have recovered the stolen gold chain, bracelet and other crucial evidence from the possession of the accused. After this, he was arrested and sent to jail. The accused Mohit Dwivedi is educated. He has completed BA, LLB and MA. He had also recently appeared for the TGT examination.

stories.title: Pastor who fed 'Jesus' blood' for conversion arrested:Associate govt teacher also arrested; UP police raids secret church
stories.summary: After revelations of alleged religious conversions along the UP-Nepal border, police launched action and arrested Pastor Vijay and his associate, government teacher Shivprasad Gautam, on Monday. Both were produced in court and sent to jail. In Dalrajpur village of Lakhimpur Kheri district, Hindus were allegedly being converted to Christianity on a large scale. To investigate, a Dainik Bhaskar reporter posed as a laborer and spent 20 days in the village. Members of the group later approached him and allegedly offered inducements to convert. Using a hidden camera, the reporter exposed the alleged conversion network and those involved. After the report was published, Kheri police raided the secret church on June 6, but the pastor and his associates escaped. They were arrested on June 8 and later sent to jail by the court. Case registered under sections of religious conversion After Bhaskar's investigation, people who converted from Hinduism to Christianity came forward openly. This gang had also lured Mohit Chaudhary of the Tharu community. On Mohit's complaint, a case was registered against Pastor Vijay and teacher Shivprasad Gautam under 4 sections. Mohit said that Vijay took him to Dalrajpur, where he pressured him to adopt Christianity. He said, 'If you adopt Christianity, you will get money.' Master Shivkumar also arrived there. Then both of them pressured me to adopt Christianity and also offered temptations. When I refused, they started threatening to kill me.

stories.title: Minister Nandi stripped of expressway portfolio:UPEIDA to report directly to CM Yogi amid IAS row
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Cabinet Minister Nand Gopal Gupta 'Nandi' suffered a major setback on Monday as the state government withdrew his charge of the Uttar Pradesh Expressways Industrial Development Authority (UPEIDA). The government has shifted UPEIDA from the Industrial Development Department to the Infrastructure and Industrial Development Department, bringing all expressway construction and development work directly under Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. Until now, project, budget, and approval files related to UPEIDA were routed through Nandi's department. Under the new arrangement, they will be cleared directly by the Chief Minister's Office. Why did the government make the change? The government said the move will improve coordination between infrastructure and industrial development departments, speed up decision-making, and reduce project delays. However, political circles view it as a setback for Nand Gopal Gupta 'Nandi' following the controversy during the transfer season. The decision is also being linked to his ongoing tussle with Additional Chief Secretary Alok Kumar. Sources said Nandi had raised objections over officer appointments and deputations in UPEIDA and frequently intervened in its functioning. He had also recently complained to CM Yogi about Alok Kumar. To keep UPEIDA's operations free from such interference, it has now been shifted to the Infrastructure Department, which is directly overseen by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. Nandi also opened a front against the former Chief Secretary Last year, Nand Gopal Nandi had also opened a front against the then Chief Secretary Manoj Kumar Singh. He had advocated against giving him a service extension by complaining all the way to Delhi. The Government of India did not grant a service extension to Manoj Kumar Singh. However, CM Yogi had appointed him as the Vice Chairman of the Transformation Commission. UPEIDA formed in 2007 UPIDA was constituted on December 27, 2007, for the construction of expressways and the development of industrial corridors in the state. In later years, its role primarily focused on the construction of expressways and large infrastructure projects. Infrastructure is UPIDA's primary function Government officials say that UPIDA's core work is to develop infrastructure. Industries are promoted only after expressways, roads, and other large projects are completed. For this reason, it has been decided to bring it under the Infrastructure Development Department. Project monitoring to improve The order from the Secretariat Administration Department states that the new system will improve the monitoring, implementation, and coordination of projects between departments. Additionally, decisions related to expressways and other major projects will be made more quickly than before. Nandi stripped of the charge of Banda's Guardian Minister 5 days earlier The Yogi government had made a major reshuffle in the districts of guardian ministers about 5 days ago. During this, the guardian minister of Banda district was also changed. Dinesh Pratap Singh was made the guardian minister of Banda district. Before this, Nand Gopal Gupta 'Nandi' was the guardian minister of Banda district, who was removed. Now know about Minister Nandi Nand Gopal Gupta 'Nandi', a BJP MLA from Prayagraj South, was born on April 23, 1974, into a middle-class family in Prayagraj and is also a successful businessman. He first won the Allahabad South assembly seat on a BSP ticket in 2007 and became a minister in the Mayawati government. He later contested the 2014 Lok Sabha election on a Congress ticket but lost. Nandi joined the BJP in 2017, won the assembly election, and retained the seat in 2022 before joining the Yogi Adityanath cabinet. His wife, Abhilasha Gupta, has served as Mayor of Prayagraj. On July 12, 2010, Nandi survived a deadly remote-controlled bomb attack in Prayagraj in which he was seriously injured. Since then, he has celebrated July 12 every year as his 'rebirth' or 'recovered birthday.'

stories.title: ‘I can’t marry you, but I’ll keep meeting you’:Ayodhya preacher accused of rape goes missing after FIR; audio clip surfaces
stories.summary: After a rape case was registered against Ayodhya preacher Pawan Dev Maharaj (42), police launched a search for him. His residence was raided several times on Sunday night, but he was not found. Efforts to arrest him are ongoing. On Monday, Bikapur police also conducted the victim's medical examination. Meanwhile, a 6-minute-30-second audio clip of a conversation between Pawan Dev Maharaj and the woman from Bihar who filed the complaint has surfaced. Recorded two days before the FIR was lodged on June 4, the audio allegedly captures the preacher speaking emotionally with the woman. 2 pictures of the preacher In the audio that has surfaced, Pawan Dev Maharaj talks about giving land and property to the woman. Whereas, the woman repeatedly asks only for his name and the right of a wife. The woman told Bhaskar that this audio is of her conversation with the storyteller. Read the conversation between the preacher and the woman Preacher: What should I do? Where should I go? It's not my fault. I will give you all my property. Woman: I don't want anything, I just want your name. Preacher: How can I give you my name? My family won't agree. I have married you, applied vermilion to you, asked for you from God, but nothing more can happen now. Woman: I don't want anything. If you are not there, what will I do with the property? Preacher: So tell me, what should I do? Should I leave the world? Woman: No, I just don't want anything. In the leaked audio, Pawan Dev Maharaj allegedly asks the woman if she can live separately while he continues to support her, visit her, and stay in touch. He even suggests changing her appearance through plastic surgery so no one can recognise her. The woman rejects the proposal, saying she does not want land, a house, or a separate residence. She insists on living with him as his wife. Maharaj is then heard asking how he could bring her home as his bride, while the woman repeatedly says she only wants to live in his house as his wife, not alone. Complete case in 10 points Police registered a case Based on the woman's complaint, Bikapur Kotwali police registered a case on Saturday night (June 6). The matter is from the Bikapur area, about 25 kilometres away from the district headquarters. Police are investigating the allegations and raiding possible hideouts in search of the preacher. Police officers say that further action will be taken based on the investigation of the case. On Monday, Bikapur police conducted a medical examination of the victim woman. Meanwhile, since the registration of the case, silence has fallen over the storyteller's house. His family members are also avoiding coming forward. Know about Pawan Dev Pawan Dev Maharaj hails from Malethu Kanak village in the Bikapur police station area. He describes himself as a disciple of the famous preacher Devkinandan Thakur. In the last few years, he has made a name for himself in the religious world through his narratives. Pawan Dev Maharaj was appointed as the national spokesperson of Karni Sena on May 13, 2026. Since then, he also speaks on various social and religious issues related to the organisation. Along with religious platforms, he is also recognised as a young preacher and speaker. Pawan Dev's father, Ramakant Shastri, is a ritualist. He remains associated with him in religious rituals and worship at the family level. Police officers say that all aspects are being investigated based on the complaint. Further action will be taken based on the available evidence and statements from both parties. Considering the sensitivity of the matter, the police are engaged in verifying the facts.

He alleged that after controversies over land deals, money is now being taken directly from the donation box. 3. UP police aspirant in tears after exam, calls maths section tough; 2.8 lakh competing for 32,679 posts The UP Police recruitment exam for 32,679 constable posts is being held across the state. Candidates underwent strict checks, including admit card verification, biometric matching, and retina scans. In some centres, women were asked to open hair buns, while chains and spectacles were removed for inspection. 4. 32 dead, over 200 injured in Philippines earthquake A 7.8 magnitude earthquake struck the Philippines on Monday morning, causing damage to several buildings. Most of the affected structures include shops, offices, and commercial buildings. AP reported, citing officials, that the death toll from the quake has risen to 32. 5. 4 UP MPs fall ill during Ladakh tour; one admitted to AIIMS Four MPs from Uttar Pradesh fell ill during a visit to Leh-Ladakh due to high-altitude oxygen shortages. Lalganj MP was admitted to AIIMS after vomiting blood, while other MPs required oxygen support because of breathing difficulties. 6. Businessman’s murder accused killed in STF encounter; had 41 cases against him Bhanu Pratap Singh alias Bablu (38), a ₹2 lakh reward-carrying criminal wanted in a businessman’s murder case, was killed in an encounter with the UP STF in Ayodhya on Sunday night. Police said he was intercepted while fleeing on a motorcycle with an accomplice. 7. Iran says stopping strikes on Israel, will resume if Israel attacks Lebanon Iran's central military headquarters has announced it will halt strikes on Israel, but warned that it would launch a "more severe" response if Israel continues its attacks in southern Lebanon. The statement came after US President Donald Trump urged both countries to stop "shooting", following their first direct exchanges of attacks since the ceasefire agreed in April. 8. Haryanvi dancer seeks justice after on-stage molestation in Hathras A Haryanvi dancer has demanded strict action against a youth accused of molesting her during a stage performance in Hathras. Police have registered an FIR against an unidentified accused under Section 74 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). She said she wants such “beasts” punished. 9. ‘Gym trainer trapped my son, got him converted’; Shamli businessman alleges property grab plot A Shamli medicine businessman has alleged that gym trainer Chandni Qureshi trapped his 27-year-old son, converted him from Hinduism to Islam, and arranged a fake nikah to gain access to family property worth crores. He also claimed his son spent hours watching content from a Pakistani YouTube channel. 10. Parliamentary panel asks NTA to define ‘paper leak’ A parliamentary committee probing controversies related to the NEET paper leak and CBSE's On-Screen Marking (OSM) system has raised several pointed questions to the National Testing Agency (NTA) and CBSE.
