stories.title: ‘I became Muslim of my own free will’:Shamli trader’s son defends conversion; stands by gym-trainer wife
stories.summary: Ayush Malik, who converted to Islam after marrying a Muslim female gym trainer in Shamli, UP, appeared before the media on Monday. He said, No one pressured me to convert to Islam. I accepted Islam of my own free will. My parents perform puja, and I offer namaz five times a day. I have also kept a beard because it is a Sunnah in our Islam. Ayush claimed he had been studying Islam and Muslim customs for about 13 years and had married gym trainer Chandni Qureshi under Islamic rites four years ago. He said he kept the marriage secret because his sister was unmarried at the time. ‘I am now a Muslim. Both families are mine, and I will not abandon either of them,’ he said. Ayush's father, Devraj Malik, is a wealthy medicine businessman in Shamli with assets worth crores. On Saturday, he filed an FIR against Chandni, six of her family members, and three Maulvis, alleging forced conversion and illegal extortion. Police have arrested Chandni and her father and sent them to jail. Full statement of Ayush Malik alias Rehman Ayush Malik, alias Rehman, said he embraced Islam on his own and was not influenced by anyone. He said his interest in Islam began during his school years and deepened around 2012-13. He regularly watched videos of Pakistani Islamic preacher DrDr Israr Ahmed, which further strengthened his inclination. Ayush said he rarely visited temples as a child because he felt drawn toward Islam. He now offers namaz five times a day and keeps a beard, which he described as a Sunnah followed by Islamic prophets. He said he later met Chandni and, four years ago, wholeheartedly accepted Islam before marrying her according to Islamic rituals. According to Ayush, neither Chandni nor her family pressured him to convert, and the decision was entirely his own. He added that his family is upset because he left Hinduism and adopted Islam, but maintained it was a personal choice. He said he had planned to inform them gradually, but they learned about it earlier. In February, he publicly announced that he had accepted Islam. Ayush said, Lying is a sin in Islam, but Islam allows a truth to be concealed if the situation is not right, if life is at stake, or if someone's feelings are being hurt. Another reason was that my sister was not married yet. Chandni's family was also insistent on getting their daughter married quickly, so I converted to Islam and married Chandni, keeping it a secret from my family.Even if my family doesn't accept me, for me, both my family and Chandni's family are my own. I cannot leave anyone. I will stand by the full truth regarding the accusations my family has made against Chandni and her father. My mother still calls me by my childhood name, Lavkush, and I don't object. She is my mother, she can call me whatever she wants.Currently, I am a Muslim, and I am happy. I will never change my religion again, no matter how much pressure anyone puts on me. Islam also does not permit this. 2 pictures How the dispute started The case involves Dayanand Nagar and Qureshi Basti in Shamli. Devraj Malik, a medicine businessman, president of the Shamli Chemist Association, and resident of Dayanand Nagar, alleged that his son Ayush was influenced by Chandni, a gym trainer from Qureshi Basti. According to police, Ayush, who runs a medical store after completing B-Pharma, started visiting the 'Qureshi Plus' gym five years ago, where he met Chandni. Devraj claims Chandni drew Ayush into a relationship and secretly married him under Islamic rites four years ago. He further alleged that Ayush began changing his appearance about six months ago, first growing a beard and later regularly visiting a mosque. Photos have surfaced showing Ayush offering Namaz in a mosque and wearing a cap and kurta-pyjama at his medical store. Mahant released a video, then the matter came to light The matter came to light when, on June 4, Mahant Swami Yashveer of Yog Sadhana Ashram in Muzaffarnagar released a video. He stated that Chandni Qureshi has trapped the only son of the owner of Bharat Medical Store. Under pressure, the entire family has converted to their religion. After the matter came to light, Hindu organisations started protesting and threatened to stage a sit-in at the gym trainer's house. On Saturday, Ayush's father, Devraj Malik, reached the police station and filed an FIR. SP NP Singh stated that a case has been registered and an investigation has begun. This is 'property jihad' to usurp property worth 60-70 crores Religious leader Yashveer Maharaj said, This case is not just 'love jihad', but also 'property jihad' to usurp property worth 60-70 crores. He claimed that the accused Chandni Qureshi has extorted about one and a half crore rupees from the youth. The threads of this conspiracy are suspected to be linked to religious leaders in Delhi, Mumbai and Pakistan. Father said - I am a Hindu, my son was converted to Muslim Businessman Devraj Malik told Dainik Bhaskar that his son Ayush's conversion was carried out by gym trainer Chandni Qureshi and her family members. They had been extorting money from his son for 5 years. He stated that all this happened under a conspiracy. It also involves Munawwar Maulvi, a resident near Kadian Mosque in Azad Chowk, and 2 other unknown Maulvis. All of them together put mental pressure on his son. They forced him to adopt the Muslim religion. When we found out, we protested against it. My wife and I are still in the Hindu religion. We go to the temple for worship in the morning and evening.

stories.title: Suspended cop behind ₹2 cr Hapur robbery:Businessman’s family held at gunpoint; police arrest all five accused
stories.summary: The mastermind behind the ₹2 crore robbery at a businessman's house in Hapur was a suspended Uttar Pradesh Police constable, Vicky Gautam. Police arrested Gautam and his four accomplices late Sunday night following an encounter. During the encounter, two accused suffered bullet injuries to their legs. Police said the gang had surveyed timber businessman Narendra Agarwal's residence for four months before carrying out the robbery on June 2. The accused held the family hostage for nearly an hour and fled with 1.25 kg of gold, silver jewellery, and cash. All five suspects were captured on CCTV footage. Gautam had also been arrested about a year ago for possessing old currency worth ₹1.5 crore. Know how the robbery happened On the early morning of June 2, 17-year-old Siddhant, grandson of businessman Narendra Agarwal, returned home from a business tour to find robbers already lying in wait. As he entered, four armed men followed him inside. When Siddhant tried to raise an alarm, the robbers pointed a pistol at his temple and overpowered him. The gang then held Narendra Agarwal, his wife Sushila, and the watchman at gunpoint. They demanded ₹2 crore in cash, but Agarwal told them there was not that much money in the house. The accused then tied up everyone with bedsheets, locked them in a room, and spent about an hour ransacking the house. 1.25 kg of gold and lakhs in cash looted The robbers fled with around 1.25 kg of gold jewellery, silver, and lakhs of rupees in cash taken from cupboards and lockers. After they left, the family alerted the police. Senior officers, including the DIG and SP, reached the spot and began examining CCTV footage. The robbery at the home of a prominent businessman triggered outrage among traders. A trade association questioned the law-and-order situation and gave police a 72-hour ultimatum to solve the case, warning of market closures and protests. During the investigation, police found CCTV footage about 150 metres from Narendra Agarwal's house, showing three youths fleeing on a single motorcycle with a bag after the crime. The footage helped identify the accused. How police tracked down the robbers CO Varun Mishra said, Late Sunday night, police were checking on Sultanpur Road in the Kotwali Dehat area. During this, five suspicious youths on two bikes were seen approaching. When the police tried to stop them, the criminals increased the speed of their bikes and started firing at the police team.In retaliation, Rohit and Shahbe Alam, residents of Moradabad, were injured by police firing. Police cordoned off the area and apprehended suspended constable Vicky Gautam along with his three other accused. All five accused are in police custody. Both injured have been admitted to the hospital for treatment. Kept doing reconnaissance for four months Police investigation revealed that the gang had extensively reconnoitred the businessman's house before committing the crime. Initial investigation revealed two months of reconnaissance, while later investigation showed that the criminals had been monitoring the activities of the house and family for about four months. Information was gathered on visitors, security arrangements, people present in the house, and even the safe's location. Mason's son revealed the locker's location In the robbery case, police have also arrested Guddu, a resident of Rustampur Sarai (Moradabad), and Tinkoo, a resident of Sambhal Road. Tinkoo's father, Satpal, is a mason and had been working for the businessman for several months. According to the police, it was Tinkoo who provided the robbers with information about the location of the locker and its key in Narendra Agarwal's house. This is why the accused directly reached the places where cash and valuables were kept. Constable suspended for being absent from duty

stories.title: Claim of ₹7 cr theft from Ram Temple sparks row:Shankaracharya says, ‘This is what happens when a thief is made Guardian’
stories.summary: A political controversy has erupted over allegations that crores of rupees have been stolen from donation collections at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya. Speaking in Agra, Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand criticised the alleged incident, saying, “When a thief is made the protector, what else can be expected? Earlier, it happened in the name of land deals, and now money is allegedly being taken directly from the donation box.” Responding to Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav’s remarks, Uttar Pradesh BJP President Pankaj Chaudhary said, “Who is making these claims? Akhilesh keeps making statements, and we cannot keep responding to all of them. This is not a government matter; the temple administration will answer it.” Saint Varun Das Maharaj also attacked the SP chief, saying, “Akhilesh Yadav, who troubles devotees of Lord Ram, has no right to speak on this issue.” The controversy began after former SP minister Pawan Pandey alleged on Sunday that around ₹5 crore to ₹7.5 crore had been stolen from the Ram Temple’s donation funds. Akhilesh Yadav subsequently questioned the government's silence on the issue, calling it suspicious and demanding that the court take suo motu cognisance of the matter. In response to the allegations, Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust General Secretary Champat Rai issued a clarification. He stated that the trust conducts internal audits regularly, with representatives of both the trust and the State Bank of India participating in the process. According to him, the audit exercise is currently underway, and no evidence of any theft or irregularity has emerged so far. Reacting to Champat Rai’s statement, Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leader Sanjay Singh said the clarification did not categorically deny the alleged theft. “The official statement does not clearly say that no donation money was stolen. That means no clear explanation has been given,” he said. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to the saints about theft claims Read the entire matter in detail- Akhilesh wrote - Disappearance of money is shameful for the temple trust Akhilesh posted on X on Sunday and wrote - This is extremely sensitive news for devotees of Lord Ram across the world. Crores of rupees from Ram Temple offerings have been found missing. Akhilesh has also targeted the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust and the government. He wrote that the disappearance of crores of rupees is an extremely shameful situation for the temple trust. No one wants to come forward to give any clarification. The SP president has demanded that the court take suo motu cognisance, as it is directly related to the deep faith of the entire Sanatan society globally in Lord Ram. The government's silence is suspicious. Former Minister's Claim - Rs 7.5 Crore theft occurred Pawan Pandey was the State Minister for Forest and Entertainment Tax in the SP government. In conversation with Dainik Bhaskar, he claimed that the donation boxes kept inside the Ayodhya Ram Temple, where offerings are made, have been subjected to theft ranging from 5 to 7.50 crores. Names of BJP workers and some people from the Trust are emerging in this. I want to ask the country's government and UP CM Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath whether you will conduct an impartial investigation into this matter? Will an FIR be filed against those thieves? Because the faith of crores of people in the country is connected to that temple. He said that people had offered their hard-earned money, saving rupee by rupee, for the construction of that temple and at the feet of Lord Ram. If such theft happens, it is highly condemnable. The government should immediately take action on this, and whoever is guilty should be sent behind bars. He said that it is not yet clear how long this theft has been going on. Which members of the trust this money has reached should also be investigated. Champat Rai's clarification, Akhilesh's counter-attack - The clarification itself is not clear Message from Champat Rai, General Secretary of Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra, for everyone's information#vhp #rammandir pic.twitter.com/jEf75NtR — Nishant Rai (निशांत राय) (@Nishantrai13) June 7, 2026 After this, Akhilesh also counterattacked Champat Rai's clarification. Akhilesh wrote on X - The clarification itself is not clear. It seems this is a routine matter for them every week, and so very routine that they don't even consider it 'noteworthy' anymore. The facial expressions and body language are filled with desperation and disappointment. All members of the trust should be seated together and given a clarification, and CCTV evidence should be used to verify the figures. As soon as all the trustees sit together, the truth will immediately come out, because not everyone among them is the same. When no particular person is at the centre of this manipulation suspicion, then what is the importance of any one person's clarification? It should also be clarified why it took so many hours for a 40-second clarification to come, and why even speaking for 1 minute in the name of clarification is proving to be so difficult. Like the state government's silence, this clarification is also suspicious. It seems as if a verbal formality is being fulfilled in the name of clarification. The entire world's Sanatan society has become even more doubtful and hurt by this extremely weak clarification. Know about the system of counting offerings at Ram Mandir... ₹2,475 Crore spent on the Temple In a temple trust meeting on December 13, 2025, it was revealed that the trust has received a total of ₹4,575 crore so far. Over the past 5 years and 9 months, ₹2,475 crore have been spent on temple construction, expansion of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi complex, purchase of land and buildings, and various other works. At that time, the trust had approximately ₹2,100 crore remaining. Ayodhya's Ram Temple receives donations of over ₹1 crore daily Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust was formed on February 5, 2020

Loud sloganeering taking place The sloganeering by students sitting on a dharna against the university administration also continued. The students say that action is being taken to raise issues related to student interests. Whereas the university administration itself is adopting a stubborn stance and increasing fees manifold. Announcement to continue movement until demands are met The students sitting on dharna say that their movement will continue until the expulsion is withdrawn and positive decisions are made on other demands, including the fee hike. Meanwhile, no new response has come from the university administration in this matter so far. However, SP MP Awdhesh Prasad had appealed to the Vice-Chancellor at the dharna site itself to withdraw the expulsion of students.

stories.title: Exam special train to run between Gorakhpur-Lucknow:2 trains to run on Banaras-Azamgarh route
stories.summary: To facilitate candidates appearing for the Uttar Pradesh Police Constable Recruitment Examination, the Railway Administration has decided to operate several unreserved special trains on routes under the Gorakhpur Division. In particular, four special trains will run on the Gorakhpur–Lucknow route from June 8 to June 10, providing significant relief to candidates travelling to examination centres. According to railway officials, all coaches in these special trains will be unreserved, and additional coaches may be attached if passenger demand increases. The Railways have also decided to reschedule and regulate some regular train services during this period to ensure smoother operations. Four special trains between Gorakhpur-Lucknow 05005 Gorakhpur-Lucknow Junction Unreserved Examination Special Train will depart daily from Gorakhpur at 1:30 PM from June 8 to 10 and will reach Lucknow Junction at 6:15 PM via Khalilabad, Basti, Babhnan, Mankapur, Gonda, Karnailganj, Barabanki, and Badshahnagar. Meanwhile, the 05006 Lucknow Junction-Gorakhpur Special Train will depart from Lucknow at 1:30 PM during this period and reach Gorakhpur at 6:50 PM. Additionally, for the convenience of night-time passengers, the 05031 Gorakhpur-Lucknow Junction Special Train will depart from Gorakhpur at 7 PM and reach Lucknow at 12:55 AM the next day. On the return journey, the 05032 Lucknow Junction-Gorakhpur Special Train will depart from Lucknow at 6:15 PM and reach Gorakhpur at 11:55 PM. The Railway has informed that these trains will have a total of 12 coaches, including 10 coaches of General Second Class and Sleeper Class, along with two SLRD coaches. All coaches will be in the unreserved category. Special trains from Varanasi and Azamgarh are also on Gorakhpur route In view of the examination, special arrangements have also been made for candidates reaching Gorakhpur from various districts of Purvanchal. 05149 Varanasi City-Gorakhpur Unreserved Exam Special Train will depart from Varanasi City at 7:30 PM on June 8 and 9 and arrive at Gorakhpur at 2:15 AM. This train will stop at major stations like Mau, Belthra Road, Salempur, Bhatni, Deoria Sadar, and Chauri Chaura. On the return journey, 05150 Gorakhpur-Varanasi City Special Train will depart from Gorakhpur at 3:15 AM on June 9 and 10 and reach Varanasi City at 9:15 AM. Similarly, 05139 Azamgarh-Gorakhpur Unreserved Exam Special Train will depart from Azamgarh at 2:30 PM daily from June 8 to 10 and reach Gorakhpur at 7 PM. The 05140 Gorakhpur-Azamgarh Special Train will depart from Gorakhpur at 8 PM and reach Azamgarh at 12:30 AM the next day. Special services for Ballia and Azamgarh as well For the convenience of candidates appearing in the examination, several unreserved special trains will also be operated on the Banaras-Ballia, Azamgarh-Ballia, and Ballia-Azamgarh routes. These trains will make it easier to reach examination centres from the districts of Purvanchal. Some regular trains will be affected The railway administration has informed that in view of the operation of special trains, the timings of some regular trains have been changed. Candidates will get major relief Railway officials say that a large number of candidates are likely to travel for the UP Police Constable recruitment examination. Keeping this in view, special trains are being operated connecting major cities of Purvanchal, including Gorakhpur, Lucknow, Varanasi, Azamgarh, and Ballia, so that examinees do not have to face the crowd and travel-related problems.

stories.title: Some had wrong names, others found gender changed in marksheets:Over 4,000 UP board students have applied; marksheets will take time to arrive
stories.summary: UP Board students may have to wait longer for their corrected results, as thousands have applied for changes in their marksheets. A total of 4,697 applications have been received from around 10 districts under the Varanasi regional office. The requests involve various types of corrections, including errors in students' names, parents' names, date of birth, gender, and photographs. In several cases, students found mistakes in their own names, while others reported incorrect entries for their mother’s or father’s names. Some students also discovered that their gender had been recorded incorrectly. According to officials, the highest number of applications- 1,275, is for name corrections. This is followed by 1,139 applications for changes in fathers' names, 974 for mothers' names, and 786 for date-of-birth corrections. Additionally, 92 students have applied to correct wrongly recorded gender details, while 431 applications have been submitted for changes in photographs. The large number of correction requests is expected to delay the processing of updated marksheets and related results. Applications were taken from students till May 12 UP Board had released the examination results of 10th and 12th students on April 23. Errors were found in the online marksheets of many students. The board had sought applications from students to get these corrected. Applications were filled within the stipulated time frame by the DIOS of all districts. The last applications were submitted on May 12. This is why marksheets are likely to arrive by the end of June. Most applications for corrections have come from the Azamgarh district. From here, there are a total of 905 applications for High School and Intermediate. Among these, there are 696 applications for High School and 209 for Intermediate. Similarly, from Ballia, there are a total of 766 applications combining both classes, and 702 applications from Ghazipur. The least number of applications is from Varanasi with 237, and Sonbhadra with 207 applications. Marksheets will be issued after corrections Bhaskar Mishra, Regional Additional Secretary of the Board of Secondary Education, Varanasi, informed that applications for corrections have been obtained from the DIOS of districts and uploaded on the board's site. Marksheets will be issued after corrections. Marksheets are likely to be issued by the end of this month. Every effort is being made to ensure that there is no error in any marksheet.

stories.title: From ₹200 for his first song to concerts nationwide:Kashmiri singer says, 'Lucknow's biryani is delicious, Kashmir is peaceful'
stories.summary: Baabarr Mudacer, who earned just ₹200 for his first song, has emerged as one of Kashmir's rising musical talents and now performs concerts across the country. Known for his versatility in Sufi, rap, classical, and soulful melodies, he has performed in major cities including Delhi, Mumbai, and Kolkata. His passion for singing grew so strong that he left his studies in 2012 to pursue music. Since entering the mainstream music scene in 2018, he has steadily built a loyal fan base. Mudacer performed in Lucknow on June 6 and received an enthusiastic response from fans. Expressing his fondness for the city, he said, “I love Lucknow. The biryani here is delicious. I also had matka kulfi, which was excellent.” Speaking about his home state, Kashmir, he said that peace prevails there. During his second visit to Lucknow, Mudacer spoke to Dainik Bhaskar about his musical journey, career struggles, favourite singers and rappers, his affection for Lucknow, and his views on the killing of Punjabi singer Sidhu Moose Wala. Read the conversation... Question- When did your singing journey begin, and when did you first discover your passion for music? Answer- It started in my childhood. I have always been passionate about singing. Over time, that passion grew stronger, turned into an obsession, and eventually became my profession. Music has been an inseparable part of my life since my early years, and I share a deep emotional connection with singing. Question- Your mother once mentioned in an interview that your first earnings from singing was ₹200. Can you tell us the full story behind that? Answer- In first grade, I went on a picnic with my school teacher and classmates. All the children were sitting in a circle. I was asked to get up and sing there. I always used to get up. The school people also knew that I had more interest in singing. And when I sang there, a tourist was sitting in front. He was very happy and gave me a reward of ₹200. Question- What challenges do artists from Jammu-Kashmir face? Answer- Yes, see, first of all, an artist needs a platform. Artists from Kashmir emerge independently. Everyone works hard on their own. There is no government support for them. I want the government to provide some support so that upcoming budding artists don't have to face the difficulties that we have faced. Question- Did you face criticism in the early days? Answer- There were many challenges. Difficulties are a part of every profession, but when you choose a career that is uncertain, the criticism tends to be greater. My family opposed my decision when I was young, and society had its doubts as well. People will always have something to say; that is their nature. I learned not to be distracted by it. The key is to keep working hard, stay focused on your goal, and leave the rest to Allah. Question- Do you enjoy singing alone in valleys of Kashmir more, or performing before large audience? Answer- Singing in the valleys of Kashmir and performing before a crowd are two completely different experiences. Sometimes, when I am alone, I head to the hills and spend some time there. It helps me refresh myself because constant shows, travelling, and work can be exhausting. Everyone needs moments of peace and a change of atmosphere, and I find that calm and rejuvenation in the valleys of Kashmir. Question- What is your favorite song? Answer- I have many favourite songs, and it largely depends on my mood. When I'm travelling in the car, I usually listen to rap. If I'm sitting in the mountains, I prefer listening to ghazals. My musical preferences change with the moment and the setting. That's why it's a difficult question to answer, I can't pick just one favourite song. Question- Your song 'Mera Dil Ye Pukare Aaja...' sung in high notes received a lot of praise on social media. Did you feel you were getting a new identity? Answer- No, no. Things had already started before that. This song was actually sung by Lata ji a long time ago, so this song was very close to my heart. I just recorded it casually, and it went viral across the globe, so this song gave me a push. I am very grateful to the people. This song always makes people recognize me, saying, "This is the same person. You sang that song." Wherever I go, wherever I travel, people recognize me. All thanks to Lata ji and all the old composers and those who wrote this song. Thank you very much to everyone. Also, thanks to the new generation. They liked this song more in my voice. Question- You have been given the title of Mad Rockstar. How do you view this title? Answer- Yes, MAD stands for Music And Donate. I try to help people in my own way as much as I can. That's why people call me that, and I like it. A person should help someone through their art because if you have come into this world, then helping each other is important. Question- What do you like about the flavors of Lucknow? Answer- I’ve tried the biryani here, and I really like it. In fact, when I arrived in Lucknow yesterday, the first thing I had was biryani. I also tasted the famous matka kulfi in the evening after we landed. It was delicious; they make it really well here. Question- You are a favorite of many people. Who is your favorite singer? Answer- Very difficult question. A person doesn't have just one favorite singer, ... so currently there are 2, 4, 5 names. Ustad Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan Sahab, Jagjit Singh Sahab, Ghulam Ali Sahab, Mehandi Ali Sahab, and there are also two-four rappers like Sidhu Moose Wala ji was. Question- How much regret is there about Sidhu Moosewala ji's passing? Answer- Very much. It's a big loss. It was a huge loss. He was the only son of his parents, and his death was also a major setback for the Punjabi music industry. Every artist is unique; someone like him comes only once. Another artist may emerge, but they will have their own distinct identity. Sidhu Moose Wala's loss cannot truly be replaced. Such incidents are tragic and should not happen.

stories.title: Haryanvi dancer seeks justice after on-stage molestation:FIR filed in Hathras, says ‘I want to eliminate such beasts’
stories.summary: A Haryanvi dancer has demanded strict action against a youth accused of molesting her during a stage performance in Uttar Pradesh's Hathras district. Based on her complaint, police at Sasni police station have registered an FIR against an unidentified accused under Section 74 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). The incident took place on June 3 during a birthday celebration where the dancer was performing. She reached Hathras on Sunday and recorded her statement before police. A video of the incident had earlier gone viral on social media. ‘This fight is for all artists’ In a video released after the controversy, the dancer said her fight was not only for herself but for all women and artists who face harassment during public performances. “This fight is not just about my self-respect but for all those girls and artists who face such incidents. I want justice and will fight for it,” she said. She added that she was seeking justice for every woman who faces misconduct at public events and stage shows. ‘I want to end such beasts’ The dancer appealed to society to support women facing harassment. “If society stands with a daughter, no one can harm her. Today it is me; tomorrow it could be your daughter. I do not want to end myself. I want to end such beasts,” she said. Responding to online trolling, she said stage performances are her livelihood and help support her family. “I do not dance on stage as a hobby. I do this work to run my household. If money was my only concern, my sister, who is more beautiful than me, would also be in this profession,” she said. How the incident unfolded According to the dancer, the accused first approached her during the performance and allegedly tried to put money inside her dress in an inappropriate manner. She later shared a video of the incident on social media. She alleged that the youth returned to the stage during another performance and touched her waist. The dancer then slapped him on stage and confronted him in front of the audience. Videos of both incidents circulated widely on social media, triggering public debate and calls for action against the accused. Police are now investigating the case and trying to identify the youth seen in the viral videos.

stories.title: Businessman's murder accused killed in encounter:STF surrounded him, he fired bullets; 41 cases pending
stories.summary: A wanted criminal carrying a reward of ₹2 lakh, Bhanu Pratap Singh alias Bablu(38), was killed in an encounter with the Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force (STF) in Ayodhya late Sunday night. According to police, the STF received information that Bhanu Pratap was fleeing on a motorcycle with an accomplice. When the team attempted to intercept him near AMI Ghat in the Maharajganj police station area around 11 pm, he allegedly opened fire with a Sten gun. STF personnel returned fire, injuring him. Bhanu Pratap was taken to the Medical College for treatment, where he later died. His accomplice managed to escape under the cover of darkness. A resident of Gorakhpur, Bhanu Pratap faced around 41 criminal cases, including charges of murder, robbery, and extortion. He was considered a hardcore criminal by the police and had been on the run for a long time. Among the cases against him was the murder of a milk businessman. Police had been searching for him for several years. Pictures of the encounter- Ambulance didn't arrive, STF took him to hospital themselves According to police, on Sunday night, around 11.10 pm, STF Inspector JP Rai informed Maharajganj police about an encounter with criminals near Ami Ghat and requested help. Upon receiving the information, the Inspector-in-charge reached the spot with the police force. It was found that two criminals on a bike had a face-to-face encounter with the STF team. STF informed the ambulance. When the ambulance didn't arrive on time, STF themselves took Bhanu Pratap to CHC Pura Bazar. After initial treatment, doctors referred him to Medical College, Darshannagar. Bhanu Pratap Singh died during treatment at the Medical College. According to police, Azamgarh police had announced a reward of ₹1 lakh for Bhanu, Ambedkarnagar police ₹50k, Gorakhpur police ₹ 25k, and Basti police ₹ 15k. All 40 cases against Bhanu are registered in these districts only. Not visited the village for past 10 years Bhanu Pratap, a resident of Belghaat Vidhanapaar in Gorakhpur, was the second among three brothers. Elder brother Sablu Singh and younger brother Gyan Pratap Singh work in a company in Bengaluru. In the village, Bhanu's father, Man Singh, his mother, and the wives of both brothers live. Man Singh does farming. There was silence at the house. The doors were found locked from inside. Sounds of crying and wailing could be heard from within. When Dainik Bhaskar tried to talk to the villagers, people were not ready to tell anything. One person, on the condition of not revealing his name, said that Bhanu had not come to the village for 10 years. His family members also did not maintain any contact with him. Bhanu Pratap was involved in murder of milk trader in Azamgarh On September 19, 2023, the Gorakhpur SSP had announced a reward of ₹15k for the arrest of criminal Bhanu Pratap Singh alias Bablu Singh, who was absconding in an Arms Act case. Meanwhile, four serious criminal cases were registered against Bhanu Pratap in Azamgarh. These include three robbery cases. After being wanted in the 2023 robbery incidents, on October 28, 2025, he shot and killed milk trader Patiram Yadav in the Mubarakpur police station area. After this, the Varanasi Zone ADG Piyush Mordiya had announced a reward of ₹1 lakh for Bhanu Pratap.

stories.title: 'Lover converted to Islam to usurp property worth crores':Victim's father claims, 'Gym trainer trapped him and organised fake nikah'
stories.summary: 'My 27-year-old son was trapped in a love trap by gym trainer Chandni Qureshi. Then she converted his religion from Hindu to Muslim. Later, she performed a fake nikah (marriage).' This is the statement of Devraj Singh, a millionaire medicine businessman from Shamli. He said, " My son had According to the police, Chandni and Ayush Malik met in 2022. Both met at a physiotherapy centre. There, they exchanged each other's numbers and their conversations began. Within a few days, both joined the gym "Qureshi Plus". There, they used to meet daily. Their affair started from there. Chandni belongs to a very poor family. Her father runs a juice cart. Her siblings work in a mall. Chandni used to pretend to be rich. After befriending Ayush, Chandni would take money from him. She bought a gold chain with Ayush's money. She also made Ayush spend a lot more money. Chandni, along with her entire family, brainwashed Ayush. She asked him to become Muslim. After this, Ayush separated from his family. He left Hinduism and adopted Muslim customs and practices. Ayush separated from home 6 months after nikah Chandni and her family took Ayush to Delhi. There, they converted his religion. Then Chandni got married (nikah) there itself. Ayush's family members did not know anything about the nikah. Just 6 months after the nikah, Ayush separated from his family. He rented a house in the city area. Both of them started living there together. Ayush's father alleges that when we started opposing these things, Chandni's family also pressured us to change our religion. They also threatened to kill us. Chandni's brother, Aman Qureshi, used to work at Devraj Singh's shop. He taught Ayush everything about Islam. Father said - My son is very simple. Strict action should be taken against the accused Ayush's father, Devraj Singh Malik, says," We follow the Hindu religion. Puja is performed twice a day at home. I myself go to the temple twice a day. These people lured and deceived my son and converted his religion. My son is very simple. Strict action should be taken against all of them. These people have taken lakhs of rupees from my son''. SP says, 'Chandni's family wanted to usurp property' SP NP Singh says, investigation has revealed that a Muslim leader from Pakistan who carries out religious conversions, his page was made to be followed by Ayush. Chandni's younger brother had done this. A case has been registered against 10 people. Chandni Qureshi and her father, Islam, have been arrested. 8 others are still absconding. The role of a local doctor, Khurshid Anwar, is also being investigated in the case. Chandni and her family wanted to grab property worth billions of rupees. Police are now investigating every angle. Ayush had done B Pharma, Chandni is a physiotherapist Ayush Malik has three sisters. They are married. And, now parents are left at home. Ayush Malik's father, Devraj Singh Malik, has a big name among medicine traders. Ayush has done B Pharma. Chandni Qureshi has four sisters and two brothers. Parents are left at home. Chandni has done a physiotherapist course after passing 12th with Arts.

stories.title: UP police aspirant breaks down after exam:Candidates say maths section was tricky; 2.8 lakh competing for 32,000 posts
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Police constable recruitment examination for 32,679 posts was held today (Monday). The second shift began at 3 pm and concluded at 5 pm. Candidates were allowed into exam halls only after stringent checks, including admit card verification, biometric matching, and retina scans. Security measures varied across districts. In Jhansi, candidates were asked to remove their shoes and socks. In Saharanpur, gold chains and spectacles were removed for inspection. In Jaunpur, women candidates were asked to open their hair buns for checking, while in Kanpur, candidates with long hair or beards underwent additional screening. In Mainpuri, a woman candidate broke down after the exam, alleging that her OMR sheet was taken away eight minutes before the test ended. More than 2.8 lakh candidates are expected to appear for the examination over three days, June 8, 9, and 10. The exam is being conducted across all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh at 1,183 centres. Meanwhile, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath announced a 50% fare concession for candidates travelling on state-run buses upon showing their admit cards. See pictures Know about constable recruitment

stories.title: Weather changes in UP, heavy rainfall lashes Jalaun:Rain alert for Lucknow in next 3 hrs; winds expected to gust up to 70 kmph
stories.summary: The spell of thunderstorms and rain continues across Uttar Pradesh. Most districts began Monday with bright sunshine, while reduced wind speeds led to humid conditions. However, by around 10 am, the weather changed, with clouds covering districts including Lucknow, Barabanki and Hardoi, accompanied by cool winds. Earlier in the morning, Jalaun received heavy rainfall at around 8:30 am, providing relief from the heat. Meanwhile, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an alert for Lucknow, warning of thunderstorms, lightning, and rain over the next three hours. The alert, sent to mobile phones, predicts moderate rainfall and strong winds, with gusts reaching up to 70 kmph. According to IMD, this time monsoon may reach UP 4 to 6 days late. The pre-monsoon rain spell will start after June 11. Monsoon may enter the state by June 24. Then, within 10 days, it will cover the entire UP. Monsoon usually reaches UP between June 18 and 20. Talking about the last 24 hours, the maximum temperature in 12 districts of the state remained at 40 °C or above. Banda-Jhansi were the hottest cities, where the maximum temperature was recorded at 43.2 °C. Due to the scorching sun, it became difficult for people to step out of their homes. The effect of heat was also seen on animals. At Kanpur Zoo, a tigress sat in the water pool for hours, enjoying herself. The tiger was bathed with a pipe. Water sprinklers or fountains were arranged for the deer. Most animals were seen sitting in the shade throughout the day. Lucknow's meteorological scientist, Atul Singh, said- Pre-monsoon rains have not started yet. That's why it's hot. Heatwave conditions are developing. Pre-monsoon rains may start in 3-4 days. This will bring down the temperature. Along with relief from heat, a new spell of rain will begin.A tiger resting in the shade of a tree amidst intense heat at Kanpur Zoo. stories.title: SBSP finalises contenders for 44 seats:Stakes claim to 8 BJP seats; OP Rajbhar raises pressure on 5 constituencies
stories.summary: Amidst discussions of the UP assembly elections being held earlier than scheduled, political parties have started their preparations. Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP), which contested 19 seats with the SP last time, is preparing to contest 44 seats in 2027. Among these, 8 currently have BJP MLAs. There are 2 seats where Nishad Party candidates contested last time. OP Rajbhar has also finalized candidates for Ghosi, the seat of UP government minister Dara Singh Chauhan, and Madhuban, the seat of Energy Minister AK Sharma. 5 Prominent Seats Claimed by SBSP Ghosi- On this seat in Mau district, Dara Singh Chauhan of SP won by 22 thousand votes in 2022. Later, he resigned and contested the by-election from BJP, but lost to Sudhakar Singh of SP. Sudhakar Singh has also passed away. Suheldev Bhartiya Samaj Party (SBSP) has appointed State Vice President Phagu Singh as in-charge and National Spokesperson of Yuva Manch Jitendra Kumar Bharti as co-in-charge for this seat. Madhuban- Currently, BJP's Ramvilas Chauhan is the MLA from this assembly seat in Mau district. Energy Minister AK Sharma has an eye on this seat. SBSP has appointed National Vice President Dr. Santosh Pandey as in-charge and State President of Labor Cell Ritesh Mall as co-in-charge. Itwa- Currently, Leader of Opposition Mata Prasad Pandey holds this seat in Siddharthnagar district. In 2022, he defeated Satish Chandra Dwivedi, who was the Basic Education Minister, by 1662 votes on this seat. SBSP has appointed Purvanchal State Vice President Keshav Rajbhar as in-charge and District President Siddharthnagar Ramniwas Rajbhar as co-in-charge. Malhani- On this Jaunpur seat, SP's Lucky Yadav is currently the MLA. In 2022, he defeated JDU candidate Dhananjay Singh by a margin of over 17,000 votes. This time too, Dhananjay Singh is preparing to contest the election from here. He is strengthening ties with Suhaspa. Suhaspa has appointed Brijbhan Rajbhar as in-charge. Isauli- SP's Mohammad Tahir Khan won this seat in Sultanpur district by defeating BJP's Omprakash Pandey by 269 votes. Suhaspa has appointed party's senior leader Shivkumar Singh as in-charge and district organisation minister Manoj Sharma as co-in-charge. SBSP's focus is on strengthening the organisation in these districts Subhaspa is eyeing Ghazipur, Jaunpur, Varanasi, Chandauli, Bhadohi, Azamgarh, Mau, Ballia, Deoria, Kushinagar, and Maharajganj in Purvanchal. Meanwhile, it is also focusing on Ambedkar Nagar, Sultanpur, Siddharthnagar, Basti, and Barabanki in the Awadh region. Subhaspa is also looking at Hardoi and Sitapur in Central UP, and Banda in Bundelkhand. Additionally, it has its eyes on districts like Shamli, Bijnor, Moradabad, and Firozabad in Western UP. Om Prakash Rajbhar is busy strengthening his party in these districts by mobilising Rajbhars and the extremely backward classes. Strategy formulated in the national council meeting Subhaspa's National Council meeting was held recently in Varanasi. In the organisational meeting, held in the presence of National President Om Prakash Rajbhar and National Principal General Secretary Dr. Arvind Rajbhar, it was decided that before the 2027 assembly elections, the party should prepare strongly for at least 50 to 60 seats in the state. BJP-held seats on which SBSP has staked a claim ahead of seat-sharing talks In these assembly constituencies, an agreement has been reached to strengthen the organisation up to the booth level. For this, a target has been set to connect the deprived and extremely backward castes with the party. Nishad Party contested 2 seats, RLD's won 1 seat also under scrutiny OP Rajbhar, disregarding the coalition equations, has also fielded his candidates on these seats of the allies. Nishad Party (2 seats) : On the Atrauliya seat of Azamgarh, OP Rajbhar has already held a large public meeting after appointing his son Arun Rajbhar as in-charge. Here in 2022, Nishad Party's Prashant Singh lost to SP's Sangram Yadav by 17 thousand votes. SBSP has fielded Kaluram Prajapati on the Kalpi seat of Jalaun. Here, the Nishad Party had lost by 2,816 votes. RLD (1 seat) : On Shamli's Thana Bhawan seat, which was won by RLD's Ashraf Ali Khan in 2022, SBSP has appointed Pawan Kashyap as in-charge. SBSP's 5 'strongholds', where Rajbhar himself is in charge SBSP's eye on these 19 seats won by SP Subhaspa has deployed in-charges to strengthen its hold among the extremely backward and Rajbhar voters in areas influenced by SP. Jaunpur-Ballia-Chandauli- Kerakat (Ritesh Ram), Rasra (Shivendra Singh), Sakaldiha (Nityanand Pandey), Sikanderpur (Rajnish Srivastava), Phephna (Ajay Rajbhar). Azamgarh and Ambedkar Nagar- Bhadohi Sadar (Rakesh Verma), Phulpur Pawai (Khursheed Alam), Didarganj (Shailendra Singh), Azamgarh Sadar (Hemant Singh), Mehnagar (Ramdahin Paswan), Mohammadabad Gohna (Santosh Master), Akbarpur (Vichelal Rajbhar-MLC), Jalalpur (Ramtesh Dubey), Tanda (Radhika Patel). Other Districts. Rudhauli (Basti- Ramlalit Chaudhary), Moradabad Rural (Ravi Chaudhary), Shikohabad (Firozabad- Shishupal Yadav), Baberu (Banda- Lallu Singh Khangar), Najibabad (Bijnor- Mo. Shahabuddin). BJP also claimed these seats which it narrowly missed Isauli- On this seat in Sultanpur district, Shivkumar Singh, Senior Leader (In-charge), Manoj Sharma, District Organisation Minister Sultanpur (Co-in-charge). BJP lost to SP's Mohammad Tahir by just 269 votes. Dumariyaganj- On this seat in Siddharthnagar district, Ganga Ram Rajbhar, State Vice President (In-charge), Amjad Khan, Senior Leader (Co-in-charge). SP's Sayyada Khatoon won against BJP by a margin of just 771 votes. Basti Sadar- Vinod Rajbhar, National Secretary (In-charge), Brijbhushan Mishra, State President Intellectual Cell (Co-in-charge). SP's Mahendra Nath Yadav defeated BJP's Dayaram Chaudhary by 1779 votes. Pharenda- On this seat in Maharajganj district, Jitendra Singh, National Secretary (In-charge), Kabilash Rajbhar, State Vice President (Co-in-charge). Congress's Virendra Chaudhary won against BJP's Bajrang Bahadur Singh by just 1246 votes. Ramnagar- On this seat in Barabanki district, Sanjay Tiwari is the National Secretary (In-charge), and Anil Rajbhar is the State Secretary Madhyanchal (Co-in-charge). SP's Farid Mahfooz Kidwai had defeated BJP by 261 votes.

stories.title: 4 UP MPs fall ill during Ladakh tour:Lalganj MP vomits blood; admitted to AIIMS; Afzal Ansari put on oxygen support
stories.summary: 4 MPs from UP fell ill in Leh-Ladakh. Due to lack of oxygen at high altitude, the MPs experienced severe difficulty in breathing. One MP had to be admitted to Delhi AIIMS after vomiting blood from the nose and mouth. Meanwhile, other MPs had to remain on oxygen support from the car to the hotel. This tour started on May 16, 2026, led by DMK Rajya Sabha MP from Tamil Nadu, Tiruchi Siva. This team of 17 MPs included 4 MPs from UP. These MPs were part of the Leh-Ladakh and Jammu and Kashmir tour of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Industry. Health deteriorated at an altitude of 12 to 14 thousand feet The committee members reached Leh, located at an altitude of about 12,500 feet above ground, on May 19. The very next day, the team went to see the saltwater Pangong Lake, situated at an altitude of 14,588 feet. Due to the sudden ascent to such a high altitude, the oxygen levels of most MPs and their family members dropped rapidly. In the entire convoy, only 2-3 MPs did not require oxygen. The rest all fell ill. UP MP said - It's difficult to breathe there He said- It's a mistake by those who planned the tour; no rest was given MP Afzal Ansari says- My oxygen level dropped to 37, whereas it should be 91 to 100. There was a mistake by those who planned the tour. Upon reaching Leh, 48 to 72 hours of rest was necessary, which was not given. I had to stay on oxygen support from the car to the hotel. The oxygen cylinder remained with me. In Ladakh, zero or sub-zero temperatures and the lack of trees make life very difficult. 'Blood started flowing from my mouth and nose' MP Daroga Prasad Saroj said- As soon as I reached a high altitude in Ladakh, I started having difficulty breathing. Soon, blood started coming from my mouth and nose. Oxygen support was immediately provided. After returning from the 7-day tour, I had to be admitted to Delhi AIIMS, where my treatment is still ongoing under the supervision of doctors. Life there is extremely difficult. The salary of our soldiers protecting the country should not be less than 10 lakh rupees. Doctors' team with us, got treatment MP Rakesh Rathore says- The problem of oxygen always persists in Leh-Ladakh. Local people are accustomed to it, but it is natural for outsiders to face problems. The relief was that a complete team of doctors was present with the parliamentary committee, due to which everyone immediately received medical help. MP Chandan Chauhan from Bijnor seat in UP also went to Leh-Ladakh. His health also deteriorated due to a lack of oxygen. Dainik Bhaskar tried to contact him, but his phone was not answered. Afzal met arch-rival Manoj Sinha after 30 years During this visit, an interesting political incident also came to light. Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha welcomed the parliamentary committee at Raj Bhavan in Jammu. In Ghazipur politics, Manoj Sinha and Afzal Ansari have had a long-standing and deep political rivalry. This was the first meeting between the two leaders since 1996. Afzal Ansari said - Manoj Sinha ji welcomed me with great warmth and respect. Political differences are one thing, but his behaviour touched my heart. After the meeting, LG Sinha presented me with Mata Vaishno Devi's prasad, a traditional Kashmiri shawl, and saffron. Visited Pulwama and Pahalgam Members of the committee also visited those sensitive places where terrorist attacks had occurred. The team visited the site of the 2019 Pulwama attack and the site of the Pahalgam incident that took place last April. How Pashmina shawls are made, this was also learned. During the visit, MPs understood the intricacies of Kashmir's famous Pashmina shawl. Afzal Ansari stated that this world-famous shawl is made from the wool of special cows and sheep living in the high mountains of Ladakh, the price of which can be up to ₹5 lakh. During the Leh visit, various ongoing development projects there and their progress were also reviewed by the State Bank of India (SBI).

stories.title: Father killed daughter inside police station over love marriage:19-year-old girl stabbed multiple times in Banda during counselling
stories.summary: A 19-year-old woman was allegedly stabbed to death by her father inside a police station in Banda district after she refused to leave her husband, whom she had married against her family’s wishes. The incident took place at Badousa police station, about 43 km from the district headquarters. Police had brought the couple back from Madhya Pradesh According to police, Shivani had been in a relationship with 20-year-old Lalit Verma for nearly four years. The couple eloped and got married on May 18 in a temple and later registered their marriage. After her family filed a complaint, police traced the couple to Satna district in Madhya Pradesh and brought them to the police station on Friday. Both families were called for counselling. Father urged her to end the marriage During the counselling session, Shivani’s father reportedly told her that Lalit belonged to a different caste and that the marriage had brought “social disgrace” to the family. He asked her to divorce him. Shivani refused and insisted that she would continue living with her husband, saying she had married him by her own choice. Attack happened during counselling Police said that while several family members and officials were present, the father suddenly pulled out a knife and attacked his daughter multiple times within seconds. Officers immediately overpowered him and rushed Shivani to a nearby hospital. She was later referred to Banda Medical College, where she died during treatment. Her mother reportedly fainted after witnessing the attack. Father taken into custody According to Superintendent of Police Palash Bansal, the accused father has been taken into custody and a case has been registered against him based on a complaint filed by the victim’s mother. The body has been sent for post-mortem examination, and further investigation is underway.

stories.title: Varanasi nursing student's death linked to alleged rape:Police say fatal bleeding resulted from genital injuries, not abortion pills
stories.summary: A 19-year-old nursing student in Varanasi died due to severe bleeding caused by injuries sustained during an alleged brutal sexual assault, and not because of abortion pills as initially claimed by the accused, according to police citing the post-mortem report. On Friday, Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police (ADCP) Lipi Nagayach said the autopsy found injuries to the victim’s private parts consistent with a violent assault. The report listed the cause of death as hemorrhagic shock resulting from excessive blood loss. Following the post-mortem findings, police added charges of rape and destruction of evidence to the murder case already registered against the accused. Accused had earlier claimed death was linked to abortion pills During questioning a day earlier, the accused, Mohammad Sameer, allegedly told police that he and the victim had been in a relationship for two years and that she was around three months pregnant. He claimed that after doctors refused to perform an abortion without family consent, the two decided to terminate the pregnancy on their own and obtained abortion medication after researching online. Police have since said the post-mortem findings contradict the earlier explanation that abortion pills alone caused the student’s death. Student was found in a pool of blood at hostel The victim was discovered unconscious and covered in blood on the staircase of her hostel on Wednesday morning around 11:30 am by an electrician working on the premises. Security staff and others rushed to the spot and took her to a nearby nursing home, where doctors declared her dead. Her father serves as a constable in the police department. Police: Accused arrested after location rtacking The accused, Mohammad Sameer, a third-year nursing student from Jaunpur district and a classmate of the victim, was arrested from his residence after police tracked his location. According to investigators, he admitted that the victim had informed him of her pregnancy on June 9. He allegedly said they consulted medical books and watched YouTube videos before purchasing abortion medication. He further claimed that on the day of the incident, the victim initially refused to take the pills and instead suggested they get married. He alleged that he forced her to consume the medication against her wishes, after which heavy bleeding began and her condition rapidly deteriorated. Accused claims he panicked and fled According to police, Sameer told investigators that the victim began bleeding heavily and attempted to leave the room using the stairs because the lift was not functioning due to a power issue. He claimed she collapsed from blood loss and that he panicked after seeing the amount of blood, locked his room, and fled to his hometown in Jaunpur by bus. Previous abortion allegation under investigation Police had earlier stated that painkillers and other medicines were recovered from the victim’s belongings. The accused also claimed that the student had undergone an abortion about seven months earlier. Investigators have recovered photographs, videos, and chat records from the accused’s phone and are examining them as part of the probe. Hostel guard says student visited repeatedly The boys’ hostel guard told police that the student had been visiting the hostel over the previous two days. On Tuesday, she was seen walking around the campus for an extended period, and on Wednesday morning she entered the building alone before later being found critically injured. Doctors warn against unsupervised use of abortion medication Gynecologist Dr. Sandhya Yadav said abortion pills should not be used in pregnancies of around three months without medical supervision, as such cases require proper clinical management. Another specialist, Dr. Kirtika Agrawal, noted that abortion medication can trigger severe bleeding, intense abdominal pain, weakness, and breathing difficulties. She emphasized that patients experiencing such complications should receive immediate hospital care, adding that timely treatment can be life-saving.

stories.title: 27-year-old MBBS doctor found dead in Etawah:NEET-PG aspirant's left emotional note saying she could not continue struggling anymore
stories.summary: A 27-year-old MBBS graduate in Uttar Pradesh’s Etawah district died by suicide after allegedly hanging herself at her residence. Before her death, she left behind a note stating that she could no longer cope with depression, anxiety, and despair. The deceased, identified as Soumya Dixit, had completed her MBBS from Rama University in Kanpur and was preparing for the NEET-PG entrance examination. The incident took place in the Friends Colony police station area. Suicide note refers to videos stored on tablet In the note recovered from the room, Soumya wrote that two videos were saved on her tablet and mentioned that the device’s password was the same as her father’s mobile phone password. She also stated that no one else was responsible for her decision and apologized to her family and loved ones while expressing gratitude and affection toward them. Father found the room locked from inside Soumya lived with her parents in the Arjun Nagar Pakka Bagh locality of Etawah. Her father, Ravikant Dixit, runs a cold storage and brick kiln business, while her mother had been visiting the family’s son in Bengaluru. According to police, Ravikant returned home around 8:30 pm and found the main door locked from inside. After receiving no response despite repeated knocks, he sought help from neighbors to break open the door. He then found his daughter hanging inside the room and alerted the authorities. Family says she had attempted suicide earlier Soumya’s maternal uncle, Pallav Dubey, said that after reviewing the videos found on her device, the family learned she had allegedly attempted suicide 16 days earlier, on May 26, but had changed her mind at that time. Police recover note and electronic devices Police and a forensic team examined the scene and recovered the suicide note along with electronic devices, including a tablet and laptop. Officials confirmed that several videos were found and are being examined as part of the investigation. The post-mortem examination was conducted under the supervision of a panel of three doctors, and the process was videographed. Soumya’s mother and brother returned from Bengaluru on Friday morning, and her last rites were performed later that afternoon on the banks of the Yamuna River in Etawah. Investigation continues Friends Colony Station House Officer Amit Mishra said that investigators are analyzing the tablet, laptop, videos, and other evidence recovered from the scene. Further legal proceedings and investigation are underway.

stories.title: PIL seeks CBI probe into Ram Temple donations:High Court petition also demands CAG audit over alleged irregularities in offerings
stories.summary: The controversy surrounding alleged theft and misappropriation of donations at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya has reached the Allahabad High Court’s Lucknow Bench. On Friday, Lucknow-based advocate Mohit Ashok filed a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) seeking an investigation by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and a special audit by the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG). The matter is expected to come up for hearing early next week, possibly on Monday or Tuesday. The petitioner has also requested the court to direct registration of an FIR if deemed necessary. Petitioner says devotees’ faith has been hurt In the PIL, Mohit Ashok argued that millions of Hindus are emotionally connected to Lord Ram and that allegations of embezzlement involving temple offerings have deeply hurt devotees’ sentiments. He contended that an impartial investigation and financial audit are essential to ensure transparency. The petition names the Central Government, Uttar Pradesh Government, CBI, CAG, and the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust as respondents. State minister says, 'Trust has begun internal inquiry' During a visit to Ayodhya on Friday, Uttar Pradesh minister Surya Pratap Shahi said the issue was an internal matter of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust. He stated that the Trust had already initiated an inquiry and assured that necessary action would be taken. He added that no one would be allowed to undermine devotees’ faith. BJP leader again writes to Prime Minister seeking transparency Ayodhya-based BJP leader Dr. Rajneesh Singh has once again written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, urging that the Trust’s income and expenditure records be made public and calling for a CBI investigation into the matter. He had earlier submitted a similar complaint to the Prime Minister’s Office. Samajwadi Party leaders demand independent investigation Former Samajwadi Party district president Paras Nath Yadav also demanded a CBI probe into the alleged donation irregularities, saying the investigation should be conducted under the supervision of the Supreme Court. He alleged that theft involving offerings linked to devotees’ faith was unfortunate and emphasized the need for a transparent and impartial inquiry. He also reiterated that the Samajwadi Party respects all religions and communities and highlighted India’s tradition of communal harmony. BJP leader put forward 6 demands to PM Modi In his letter to the Prime Minister, Dr. Rajneesh Singh argued that donations made by millions of devotees from India and abroad represent public faith and therefore deserve complete transparency. He urged the government to direct the Trust to publish comprehensive details on its official website, including: Former Uttar Pradesh minister Pawan Pandey had earlier claimed that between ₹5 crore and ₹7.5 crore had been stolen from the Ram Temple donations. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav also questioned the government’s silence on the issue and suggested that the matter should be examined by the courts. In response, Trust General Secretary Champat Rai had said that no such irregularities had come to light. Former temple accounts in-charge makes fresh allegations Mahipal Singh, who describes himself as the temple’s former accounts in-charge, alleged in an interview that while he was posted there, no proper records were maintained for donated gold, silver, jewellery, or utensils. He claimed that only Champat Rai and another individual known as “Tinnu” knew where such valuables were stored. Singh further alleged that despite overseeing multiple depositors during the temple donation campaign, he was not permitted to sign bank deposit vouchers or access key financial records. Shankaracharya alleges irregularities and calls for answers Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand also commented on the controversy, alleging that irregularities had existed since the early stages of the Ram Temple project. He claimed that reports of cash recoveries and arrests had surfaced and said those who had previously accused Akhilesh Yadav over unrelated matters should now respond to allegations concerning temple donations. He further asserted that some saints in Ayodhya had also spoken of repeated thefts, although these claims remain allegations.

stories.title: High-speed car crashes into parked truck in Unnao, 4 die:Bodies found stuck inside crushed vehicle
stories.summary: A devastating road accident on the Ganga Expressway in Unnao district claimed the lives of four people on Friday afternoon after a Tata Punch car rammed into a truck parked on the roadside. According to eyewitnesses, the car was travelling at an estimated speed of around 100 kmph when it crashed into the stationary truck in the Asivan police station area. The impact was so severe that the front portion of the vehicle was completely crushed, trapping the occupants inside. Two died on the spot, two succumbed in hospital Two of the car’s occupants died instantly, while the other two succumbed to their injuries during treatment at a hospital. Rescue teams had to cut open the vehicle’s doors to extricate the victims, whose bodies were found pinned to their seats due to the force of the collision. Victims identified Police identified the deceased as Uday Singh (26) and Anupam Gupta (32), residents of Jafarpur in Phulpur, and Vijay (25) and Aman (28), residents of Babuganj town in Prayagraj district. Pictures related to the accident Truck was parked after developing a fault According to police, the accident occurred around 3:20 pm after the truck driver had parked the vehicle on the roadside because of a mechanical breakdown. The speeding Tata Punch, approaching from behind, crashed directly into the truck. Overspeeding suspected as primary cause Eyewitnesses told investigators that the car appeared to be travelling at more than 100 kmph, causing the driver to lose control before hitting the parked truck. Following the accident, local residents alerted the police, who reached the scene and used a crane to remove the wrecked vehicle from the expressway. Beer bottles found inside car; probe underway During the investigation, police recovered beer bottles from inside the car, raising suspicion that intoxication may have contributed to the crash. However, officials said the exact cause of death and the role of alcohol, if any, would be determined after the post-mortem examination and further investigation. Station House Officer Pradeep Singh visited the scene with a police team, and the victims’ families have been informed. Authorities said all aspects of the incident are being examined.

stories.title: Akhilesh claims Ram Mandir offerings are being looted:Says, 'protesters face encounters'; former MP Kunwar Devendra joins Samajwadi Party
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav has alleged that the offerings made at the Ayodhya’s Ram Temple were being “looted” and claimed that the BJP government does not tolerate dissent. Addressing a gathering in Kasganj on Friday, Yadav said, “There is robbery in the donations made to the Ram Temple. The BJP cannot accept opposition. If anyone protests, they are met with encounters or sent to jail.” The remarks came during an event where former MP Kunwar Devendra Singh Yadav formally joined the Samajwadi Party. Devendra had switched to the BJP ahead of the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. Jibe after being presented a crown by a seer During the event, a seer placed a ceremonial crown on Akhilesh Yadav’s head. Reacting humorously, the Samajwadi chief remarked that the seer resembled “someone else” and appeared more interested in getting photographed and making social media reels than in his spiritual duties. Four major points raised by Akhilesh Yadav 1. ‘The BJP government exists only to loot’ The former Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister accused the BJP government of widespread corruption and misgovernance, saying no previous administration had engaged in such extensive “loot.” He blamed rising inflation for hurting farmers and questioned the sharp increase in fuel prices since 2014. Yadav also alleged that petrol currently contains 20% adulteration and criticized the Centre’s explanation that global conflicts were responsible for rising fuel and LPG prices. According to him, India’s foreign policy had contributed to the economic burden on ordinary citizens. He further claimed that electoral dishonesty helped the BJP retain power and alleged delays in panchayat elections while calling the “One Nation, One Election” concept a failure. He said villagers were prepared to “teach the BJP a lesson” due to shortages of fertilizers and rising fuel costs. 2. ‘People will shut down those responsible for leaks’ Targeting the government over smart meters and paper leak controversies, Akhilesh alleged that authorities were preparing to “loot” people through new systems and referred to the ruling party as “people of leaks.” He also criticized India’s global positioning, saying BJP leaders often claimed the country would become a “Vishwaguru” (world leader), but failed to demonstrate leadership during international crises. He argued that India had become overly dependent on the positions of other countries despite being one of the world’s largest markets. 3. ‘BJP is Swadeshi in speech, foreign in mind’ The SP chief accused the BJP of promoting “swadeshi” publicly while favoring foreign interests in practice. He alleged that major sectors of the Indian market had been handed over to foreign companies, adversely affecting the domestic economy and farmers. Referring to the now-repealed farm laws, Akhilesh said hundreds of farmers lost their lives during the protests and claimed that although the laws were withdrawn, farmers were still not granted meaningful legal protections or rights. 4. ‘Inflation, corruption and injustice have increased’ Akhilesh claimed that over the past decade, poverty, inflation, corruption and injustice had all increased while Uttar Pradesh had fallen behind in development. He compared expressways built by the Samajwadi Party and the BJP, asserting that roads constructed during the SP government were “world-class” and offered a smoother driving experience. Visits family of late Samajwadi Party leader Asad Hussain After the public meeting, Akhilesh Yadav visited the residence of former SP Minority Cell district president Asad Hussain, who died of a heart attack on May 10 at the age of 38. He met Hussain’s mother Rehana, wife Shela Rizvi and seven-year-old daughter Batul Hussain, offering condolences and assuring the family of support, including assistance with the child’s education and other needs.

stories.title: Getting Ayushman cards is now easier in Gorakhpur:Eligible beneficiaries can complete entire process from home
stories.summary: Beneficiaries of the Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY) in Gorakhpur will no longer need to visit government offices, hospitals, or public service centers to obtain their Ayushman cards. The Health Department has simplified the process by introducing a digital, mobile-based system that allows eligible individuals to generate their cards from home in just a few steps. Once the process is completed, users can download the Ayushman card in PDF format and use it whenever required. No more queues or repeated visits The new digital initiative is expected to benefit thousands of families across both urban and rural areas of Gorakhpur. Previously, applicants had to visit service centers and often wait in long queues. In many cases, they were required to make multiple trips for document verification and other formalities. With the mobile-based system, beneficiaries can now save time and complete the process conveniently from home. OTP verification required to generate the card To create an Ayushman card, beneficiaries must have the following documents and information: Verification is completed using a one-time password (OTP) sent to the registered mobile number, after which the card can be generated and downloaded. Step-by-step process to create the Ayushman card Eligible users can create their Ayushman card by following these steps: Officials say the new system will expand access Dr. A.K. Singh, Nodal Officer for the Ayushman Bharat Scheme, said that the smartphone-based facility will make the programme more effective and accessible. According to him, the simplified digital process will enable more eligible families to enroll in the scheme, ensuring quicker access to healthcare benefits and extending the reach of the government’s health protection initiative.

stories.title: Woman occupies judge’s chair in Varanasi court:Claims she will hear cases and demands witnesses; police remove her from bench
stories.summary: A dramatic scene unfolded at the Varanasi District Court on Friday morning when a 50-year-old woman climbed onto the district judge’s dais, occupied the judge’s chair, and declared that she would preside over court proceedings. Shouting “Order, Order” while striking the judge’s hammer on the desk, she told lawyers present in the courtroom, “Today I am the District Judge. Present your witnesses and evidence. I will hear all the cases. Tell me whatever work needs to be done.” The incident reportedly continued for nearly an hour before police intervened and took her into custody. Woman flips through case files, refuses to leave According to reports, court staff had placed files for the day’s scheduled hearings in the courtroom when Vandana Gupta (50), wife of Buj Gupta and a resident of Shivpur, entered the premises. After asking about the district judge’s arrival time, she walked to the dais and sat in the judge’s chair. She began examining files and repeatedly struck the gavel while calling out “Order, Order.” When lawyers stood up in surprise, she instructed them to remain seated and asked them to present witnesses and evidence before her. The unexpected spectacle left advocates stunned, and several began recording videos. This reportedly angered the woman, who refused repeated requests to vacate the chair. Police remove her from the bench As news of the incident spread, more lawyers gathered in the courtroom and urged Vandana Gupta to step down. However, she remained seated and allegedly shouted at those approaching the dais, even warning them not to come closer. Female police personnel were then called to the courtroom. Officers escorted her down from the judge’s chair and took her to Cantt Police Station for questioning. Sources said the district judge was on leave on Friday, and the incident took place around 9 a.m. Additional district judge orders inquiry into security lapse After being informed of the incident, Additional District Judge Yajuvendra Vikram Singh visited the courtroom and expressed displeasure over the absence of security personnel on duty. He directed officials to seek explanations from those responsible for the lapse. Following the episode, the court administration instructed security staff posted at all entry gates not to allow the woman to enter the court premises in the future. The incident has also raised serious concerns about security arrangements inside the court complex. Woman had allegedly created similar disturbances earlier According to local lawyers, Vandana Gupta does not have any case pending before the court. They claimed that she has previously entered the court premises on multiple occasions and occupied the judge’s chair in a similar manner. Police officials said they are questioning her to determine the reason behind her actions. When asked whether she might be suffering from mental health issues, officers stated that the exact circumstances would become clear only after the investigation is completed.
