stories.title: Why questions rose over Ram temple donations:Padmanabha uses judicial supervision; Sanwaliya Seth allows public participation in counting
stories.summary: The system for counting donations at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya has come under scrutiny after allegations of financial irregularities surfaced. On June 7, former Uttar Pradesh minister Pawan Pandey claimed that nearly ₹7.5 crore had been stolen from temple offerings. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav also alleged misappropriation of donations. As the controversy escalated, Ram Temple Trust General Secretary Champat Rai denied the allegations, stating that the donations were currently under audit and that no theft had been detected. However, on June 10, the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) sought a report from the temple trust on the matter. The controversy has drawn comparisons with other major temples in India—including Tirupati Balaji, Shirdi Sai Baba, Sanwaliya Seth, and Padmanabhaswamy—where donation management systems are considered highly transparent and tightly monitored. How Ram Temple donations are managed At the Ram Temple, donations are counted daily under CCTV surveillance. Key concerns raised Now know what is the system of other big temples in the country Padmanabhaswamy temple: Donations monitored by a district judge Keralam’s Padmanabhaswamy Temple, regarded as one of the world’s wealthiest temples, follows a system supervised by an administrative committee constituted under Supreme Court directions. The District Judge of Thiruvananthapuram chairs the committee, and donation boxes are opened under CCTV surveillance in the presence of bank officials, security personnel, and committee members. Periodic audits ensure transparency. Tirupati temple: Devotees can watch the counting process The Tirumala Tirupati Venkateswara Temple in Andhra Pradesh receives approximately ₹4–4.5 crore in donations every day. Counting takes place in a dedicated high-tech facility called the "Parakamani Hall," which features glass walls allowing devotees to observe the process. Only Hindu men aged 35 to 65 who are serving or retired government employees, public sector workers, or bank officials are permitted to count donations. Those involved must wear traditional white dhotis and angavastrams without pockets and are prohibited from carrying mobile phones, wallets, or personal jewellery. Sanwaliya Seth temple: Public can participate in counting At Rajasthan’s Sanwaliya Seth Temple in Chittorgarh, donation boxes are opened every month on Krishna Paksha Chaturdashi. The counting takes place in an open hall over several days, and daily press releases disclose the amount of cash and precious metals counted. Notably, ordinary devotees are allowed to participate in counting after providing Aadhaar identification. Officials at the Additional District Magistrate level, temple board members, and Bank of Baroda staff supervise the process, while around 200 people count the notes under CCTV and live video recording. Gold and silver donations are electronically weighed and documented before being stored securely. The temple reportedly received donations exceeding ₹337 crore during the 2025–26 financial year. Shirdi Sai Baba temple: Government audit and bulletproof counting hall The Shirdi Sai Baba Temple in Maharashtra also follows a transparent system. Donation boxes are opened in the presence of the Chief Executive Officer and bank officials, while counting takes place inside a bulletproof glass enclosure. Employees handling donations wear pocketless clothing and undergo metal detector screening before entering the counting area. Importantly, audits are conducted by Maharashtra’s Local Fund Audit Department rather than private auditors. How the Ram temple controversy began On June 7, former minister Pawan Pandey alleged that nearly ₹7.5 crore had been stolen from Ram Temple donations. Akhilesh Yadav subsequently called for judicial scrutiny of the matter. Champat Rai dismissed the allegations, saying no such discrepancies had been found. The controversy intensified when former accounts in-charge Mahipal Singh alleged that thefts had been occurring since 2021. He claimed that there was no written record of gold and silver donations and that photographs of precious metal offerings were merely sent to General Secretary Champat Rai. According to Singh, only Rai and his driver, Ramshankar Yadav (also known as Tinnu), knew where such donations were ultimately stored. He further alleged that vouchers for depositing cash in banks were processed without obtaining his signatures. Following the allegations, BJP leader Dr. Rajneesh Singh wrote to the Prime Minister on June 9 seeking a CBI investigation. The next day, the PMO requested a report from the Ram Temple Trust. On June 10, Ram Temple Construction Committee Chairman Nripendra Mishra also convened a meeting with trust members to discuss issues related to donations, their utilization, and accounting procedures.

stories.title: IndiGo flight makes emergency landing in Lucknow:Bomb threat note found in aircraft toilet; message is written on tissue paper
stories.summary: An IndiGo flight from Ahmedabad to Delhi via Lucknow made an emergency landing in Lucknow on Friday. While the plane was still in the air, a threat to blow up the plane was found written on a tissue paper in the toilet. The pilot informed Air Traffic Control (ATC) and requested permission for an emergency landing. ATC alerted the Airport Authority and security agencies, then granted permission for landing. Subsequently, the aircraft (6E-2111) was landed at Lucknow Airport. All passengers were deplaned. The bomb disposal squad and other agencies inspected the entire aircraft. However, no suspicious object was found. The aircraft is currently parked at Lucknow Airport. Passengers include IPS BP Ashok. An IndiGo spokesperson said: A threat was received inside the flight. Following this, senior officials were informed as per security protocol. Security protocols were followed. The aircraft will depart for Delhi after necessary checks. See pictures-

stories.title: 5 express trains resume old route operations:Gorakhpur passengers get relief; services on Mumbai-Pune corridor return to normal
stories.summary: There is good news for passengers traveling from Gorakhpur to Mumbai, Pune, and Surat. The railway has restored the routes of five express trains that were changed due to ongoing concourse construction work at Lucknow station. Now these trains will run via Kanpur Central-Lucknow (Northern Railway)-Barabanki, as before. This will save passengers from the inconvenience of the changed route. According to the railway administration, these trains were temporarily running on a different route due to work being carried out by RLDA at Lucknow station of Northern Railway. Considering the convenience of passengers, the railway has decided to resume operations on the old route. Routes of these trains to and from Gorakhpur have been restored The 11080 Gorakhpur-Lokmanya Tilak Terminus Express, departing from Gorakhpur on June 13 and 20, will now go to Mumbai via its scheduled route. Meanwhile, the 11079 Express, running from Lokmanya Tilak Terminus on June 11 and 18, will arrive in Gorakhpur via the same route. The 15066 Panvel-Gorakhpur Express running from Panvel on June 12, 13, 15, 16, 17, 19, 20 and 22, and the 15030 Pune-Gorakhpur Express running from Pune on June 13 and 20, will also reach Gorakhpur via the old route. In addition, the 19053 Surat-Muzaffarpur Express running from Surat on June 12 and 19 will also operate via the Kanpur Central-Lucknow-Barabanki route. This decision by the railways will provide convenience to passengers from Purvanchal, including Gorakhpur, during their journey.

stories.title: ‘Ram Mandir Trust needs religious leaders’:Shankaracharya targets Champat Rai; says every donation belongs to god
stories.summary: Questions should first be raised about the donations received for the Ram mandir, says Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar during his visit to Mathura as part of the Go-raksharth Dharmarth Yatra, he says every donation made to the mandir belongs to God and is considered sacred in Sanatan Dharma. He says if there are doubts about how the money has been used, those questions must be answered and properly investigated. The Shankaracharya also questions the formation of the current Ram mandir Trust. He says an earlier trust already existed, which included four Shankaracharyas, five Vaishnavacharyas and the heads of 13 Akharas. According to him, there was no need to create a new trust when one was already in place. He further alleges that Champat Rai is not honest and claims that if Shankaracharyas and other religious leaders had remained part of the trust, no irregularities could have taken place. He started the journey from Kashi on May 3. This journey will pass through all 402 assembly constituencies of UP. Approximately 25 followers are accompanying him on the journey. Question: You are constantly raising questions about the Ram mandir donations and trust? Answer: Fundraising for the Ram mandir has been going on since the foundation stone laying ceremony, and there has been a free-for-all (misappropriation). Questions have been raised repeatedly about this, but a proper answer has never been given. Question: What is your biggest objection regarding the Ram mandir Trust? Answer: The battle for the Ram mandir was not fought in court by the BJP or its associated organisations. It was fought by Shankaracharyas and other Hindu litigants. A trust already existed, which included four Shankaracharyas, five Vaishnavacharyas, and the heads of 13 Akharas. When that trust was already there, what was the need to form a new trust? Question: There is also discussion regarding the honesty of Champat Rai of the Ram mandir Trust? Answer: Champat Rai is a trusted person, there is no dispute about that. But being trusted and being honest are two different things. The two cannot be considered the same. Champat Rai stated that the donations for the Ram mandir are audited and there are no irregularities. However, now money is being recovered, people are being arrested, and CCTV footage has also been found deleted. This means a major theft has occurred. Don't you consider this a serious incident? Question: A case was filed against you in Prayagraj, what do you have to say about it? Answer: This matter is currently in court. The court has also advised not to speak much on the case. Therefore, it would not be appropriate to comment on this issue at present. Everything will come to light when the time is right. Question: WhatsApp chats have become public, in which names of officials have also come forward? Answer: The government did not conduct any investigation into this entire matter. After this, civil society conducted an investigation under the chairmanship of former CBI director Nageshwar Rao. His report stated that there was misuse of state power against the Shankaracharya of Jyotirmath. Now the facts that are coming to light are strengthening that very report. Question: There is a discussion that the dispute that arose in Lucknow was given by your team to the opposition as an issue? Answer: We don't have any team. If we have to say something, we say it ourselves. It is not our job to give an issue to any political party. These are all just discussions and speculations. It is not our job to fire a gun at someone's behest. What fear do we have? If there is something to say, we will say it ourselves. Question: Jagadguru Rambhadracharya is saying that his life is in danger? Answer: That is his subject. Why should we comment on what is between a guru and his disciple? This is his personal matter. Question: What is the main objective of the 'Go-Raksharth Dharmarth Yatra' (Journey for the Protection of Cows and Righteousness)? Answer: This journey has set out for the protection of the life and dignity of Mother Cow. For 78 years, we trusted this party sometimes, that leader sometimes. stories.title: 4 face FIR for posts targeting Akhilesh’s daughter:Cases registered in Kanpur and Pratapgarh; reputation of family allegedly damaged
stories.summary: An FIR was registered in Kanpur-Pratapgarh on Thursday regarding objectionable posts made on social media about Akhilesh Yadav's elder daughter Aditi Yadav (23). In Kanpur, a case has been registered against IDs named Bharat Patel, Nageshwar Singh Baghel, and Vinod Yadav, and in Pratapgarh, against an ID named Sheetla Sujan Kavi. It is alleged that these individuals made objectionable posts against Aditi on social media. In Kanpur, Praveen Yadav, National Secretary of the Advocates' Council, and in Pratapgarh, Abdul Qadir Jilani, General Secretary of the SP, lodged a complaint. They said that the posts tarnished the image of Akhilesh Yadav and his family in society. This has caused considerable anger in society. Therefore, strict action should be taken against them. Meanwhile, BJP MLA Rajeshwar Singh has objected to the objectionable posts. He said- Spreading derogatory remarks about the SP chief's daughter on social media is extremely unfortunate. The respect for daughters is above politics. Society should stand united against such wrongdoings. The matter should be investigated.Meanwhile, Adarsh Yadav, a junior from Aditi's Delhi college, has written a post on Facebook. He said - These fools don't know that elder sister Aditi Yadav is studying at Delhi University, not London College University. Action should be taken against such people.Aditi Yadav is currently studying 'Politics and International Relations' at University College London (UCL) in London.National Secretary of Advocate Sabha said - Akhilesh's family's image was tarnishedIn Kanpur, Praveen Yadav, National Secretary of Advocate Sabha, lodged a complaint at the cyber police station. Following this, a report has been filed against the three under the IT Act for tarnishing the woman's image, fraud and forgery with the intent to damage her reputation. DCP Crime Shravan Kumar Singh said that based on the complaint, a report has been registered and investigation into the matter has begun.Praveen Yadav wrote in the FIR: "An objectionable comment was made on Akhilesh Yadav's daughter Aditi from an ID named Bharat Kumar Patel on social media. Bharat Kumar Patel wrote from his ID that Akhilesh Yadav is talking about a 7 crore theft at the Ram Temple here, while his daughter, who is studying in London, has been missing for a few days."He has edited and posted a photo of Aditi and an unknown person on his social media account, which has been completely fabricated. Character assassination of a daughter from a respected family and defaming her by circulating it on social media is a serious crime.This post has tarnished the image of Akhilesh Yadav and his family in society. This has caused considerable anger in society. Nageshwar Singh Baghel and Vinod Kumar Yadav have also made very vulgar comments on this post. Action should be taken against all three.Advocate Sabha's National Secretary Praveen Yadav filed a case.SP General Secretary said - Woman's dignity and image were harmed, action should be takenIn Pratapgarh, SP General Secretary Abdul Qadir Jilani wrote in the FIR that wrong and objectionable things are being spread about Akhilesh Yadav's daughter Aditi Yadav from a fake ID named "Sheetla Sujan Kavi Patrakar" on Facebook.Private allegations have been made in these posts, which can harm the dignity, respect, and image of a woman. This can spread confusion in society and also disrupt social harmony. Therefore, an FIR should be registered and action taken.Leaders of SP Lohia Vahini had filed a complaint at Hazratganj Kotwali.Aditi's junior wrote - The news is completely falseAdarsh Yadav, a junior of Aditi from Delhi College, has written a post on Facebook. Adarsh has written that RSS-bred Brahmin-Baniya are upgraded Manuvadis. To hide the theft that happened in Ram Mandir, they can do such a despicable act, it's unimaginable.These fools are making cheap comments regarding elder sister Aditi Yadav, who is based at London College University. But these fools do not know that for the past one year, Aditi has been studying Law Graduation from Delhi University's Law Faculty.These days, semester exams are going on, and since I am also their batchmate in the Law Faculty, we meet after every exam. Aditi completely embodies the values and ethics inherited from her grandfather Mulayam Singh and father Akhilesh Yadav.Meeting all children and showing them respect is her daily habit. The fake news of her disappearance is completely false. I am a daily eyewitness. Adarsh Yadav, a junior from Aditi's Delhi college, wrote - The fake news of her disappearance is completely false. I am a daily eyewitness. Read what people said about the objectionable post on Aditi YadavRajeshwar Singh, BJP MLA from Sarojininagar seat in Lucknow, said - It is normal to have political differences in a democracy, but targeting someone's family, especially daughters, with false accusations and insults is against society and public decency. I demand from the administration and cyber cell that this matter be investigated impartially and strict legal action be taken against the culprits.Rajeev Rai, SP MP from Ghosi seat in Mau, had said - This is the lowest level of politics and the height of mental derangement. Obscene and dirty posts are being made on social media about Akhilesh Yadav's daughter. UP Police has not taken any action yet. Is it because she is not the daughter of a BJP leader? Shame on you.Former minister and SP leader from Ayodhya, Pawan Pandey said- When Akhilesh Yadav raised questions about theft in the Ram Temple offerings, BJP leaders resorted to personal attacks instead of giving a factual answer to the allegations. Targeting Akhilesh's family is cheap politics. This is not just an attack on a political family, but an assault on the dignity of every daughter, every sister, and every mother in the state.SP MP from Sitapur, Anand Bhadauria said- Slinging mud on character is the pride of cowards, respecting daughters is India's identity. Those who want to defame a daughter with fabricated stories, do they also know the consequences of public anger?SP MLA Ragini Sonkar said- Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao is just a hollow slogan of the BJP government. The way BJP's troll ecosystem is making indecent and extremely cheap comments on Akhilesh ji's family, the whole country is watching it. But no action is being taken against people making such comments, nor are such misleading and indecent things being stopped.

stories.title: CJP chief Abhijeet detained during students’ agitation in Lucknow:Calls it ‘greatest act of patriotism’, urges protesters to join June 20 Delhi protest
stories.summary: Nearly 6,000 students and candidates preparing for one-day competitive examinations staged a protest at Eco Garden in Lucknow on Friday. Cockroach Janata Party chief Abhijeet Dipke joined the demonstration, remained at the venue for about 40 minutes, addressed the gathering, and urged participants to join a protest in Delhi on June 20 before leaving. “Protesting is the greatest act of patriotism” In his address, Dipke said that India was shaped by mass movements and that protests had played a crucial role in securing both independence and democracy. “Our country was built through a movement. Without such struggles, we would not have gained freedom. If there had been no movement against the Emergency, democracy would not exist today. Protesting is the greatest act of patriotism,” he said. He also demanded accountability in alleged examination paper leak cases, saying that everyone responsible—whether related to Lekhpal, UPSI, NEET or CBSE examinations—should resign. Arrived with a copy of the constitution, left after 40 minutes The protest began at 10 AM, while Dipke reached Eco Garden around 1:30 p.m., carrying a copy of the Constitution. Police escorted him to the protest site under security arrangements. After spending around 40 minutes at the venue, he departed in a cab. More than 1,500 personnel from the Rapid Action Force (RAF), Provincial Armed Constabulary (PAC), and local police were deployed during the demonstration. Students raise slogans, some oppose political participation Hundreds of students and supporters attended the protest carrying posters and banners, chanting slogans such as “Stop paper leaks” and “Release the UPSI scorecards.” However, some students and recruitment aspirants objected to the participation of the Cockroach Party and Abhijeet Dipke. They argued that their movement was independent and unrelated to the party, alleging that political involvement could undermine their campaign and delay the recruitment process. Dipke had arrived in Lucknow at around 2:20 a.m. on Thursday night wearing a Team India T-shirt. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar at Amausi Airport before the event, he said the demonstration would remain peaceful, similar to previous protests held in Delhi and Pune. “We are not doing anything wrong. We are simply exercising our constitutional right to express our views in a democracy,” he said. The Cockroach Party had earlier organised demonstrations in Pune on June 11 and at Jantar Mantar in Delhi on June 6. stories.title: Stone-pelting reported on Mohan Bhagwat’s train:E-1 coach of Shatabdi Express targeted during journey from Kanpur to Delhi
stories.summary: Stones were thrown at the train carrying RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat in Firozabad on Thursday evening. A stone hits the same coach in which he is travelling, shattering a window pane. Bhagwat is travelling from Kanpur to New Delhi on the Shatabdi Express. UP Police arrest two men for stone attack on a train carrying Mohan Bhagwat Bhagwat is seated in the Executive Class E-1 coach. The stone was thrown at the coach while the train was passing between Makkhanpur and Firozabad. He remains safe and unharmed in the incident. Due to security concerns, the train is not stopped anywhere en route. After receiving information about the incident, senior officers of the Railway Protection Force (RPF) and Government Railway Police (GRP) reached Tundla Junction with a heavy security presence. As soon as the Shatabdi Express arrives at Platform No. 1 of Tundla Junction at 7:34 pm, security is tightened around the train. After inspection at the station, the train leaves for Delhi at 7:41 pm. Joint teams of the RPF and GRP also launch a search operation in areas around the Makkhanpur-Firozabad railway section. Earlier in the day, at around 2:30 pm, Bhagwat attended a blessing ceremony for the daughter of Neetu Singh. She is the elder daughter of former BJP MP Satyadev Pachauri from Kanpur. Neetu Singh’s daughter, Vasundhara, is set to marry Yash on June 21. After spending some time at the event, Bhagwat leaves. During the ceremony, Neetu Singh seeks his blessings, while other family members also greet him. Several prominent leaders attend the function, including Uttar Pradesh Assembly Speaker Satish Mahana, state ministers Suryapratap Shahi, Yogendra Upadhyay and Bhupendra Chaudhary, along with other VIPs. Special security arrangements are made across the city for the event. Neetu Singh’s family has long been associated with the RSS.

stories.title: Strong winds and rain lash Uttar Pradesh:Roads submerged and hospitals flooded; trees and poles uprooted, 75 districts on alert today
stories.summary: Pre-monsoon conditions have become active across Uttar Pradesh. Since late Thursday night, intermittent heavy rain has been reported in Agra, Mathura, Saharanpur, Hapur, Shamli and Hathras. In Saharanpur, the rain along with strong winds was so intense that roads were submerged. Water reached knee level in many areas and also entered residential homes. In Shamli, municipal office premises and hospitals were flooded up to waist level. Hapur also experienced strong winds, while in Hathras, trees and electricity poles were uprooted, causing power outages for several hours. In the early hours of Friday, heavy rainfall was recorded in Barabanki, Lakhimpur Kheri, Farrukhabad, Etah, Bijnor and Baghpat. Lucknow remained under cloud cover with light drizzle reported in some areas. The Meteorological Department has issued an alert for thunderstorms and rain across all 75 districts today, with a possibility of hail in 16 districts. According to the IMD, a new western disturbance has become active, strengthening pre-monsoon conditions and sustaining the spell of stormy weather. People have been advised to remain cautious and stay in safe places during adverse weather conditions. In the past 24 hours, 52 cities, including Gorakhpur and Meerut, witnessed thunderstorms with heavy rain, recording 4.9 mm rainfall against a forecast of 1.5 mm. However, rainfall between 1 and 11 June has remained below normal, with 11.8 mm recorded against the expected 17.3 mm. In the last 24 hours, heavy rain with storms occurred in 52 cities, including Gorakhpur-Meerut. During this period, 4.9 mm of rain occurred. Whereas, scientists had estimated only 1.5 mm of rain. However, rain between June 1 and 11 has been disappointing. Experts stated that 11.8 mm of rain occurred. It should have rained 17.3 mm. Atul Kumar Singh, a senior meteorologist in Lucknow, said- The pre-monsoon rain spell has started in UP. Now, the spell of storms and rain will continue in the state until the monsoon's entry. Intermittently, the heat will also show its intensity, but the rain will continue to provide relief. Currently, the spell of storms and rain will continue till June 15-16. The monsoon will enter the state by its scheduled time, i.e., June 20. How will the weather be for the next 5 days

stories.title: Youtuber Saleem Wastik breaks silence on allegations:Denies murder claims, says jail authorities legally release him on parole
stories.summary: Ex-Muslim YouTuber Saleem Wastik, who was released from Delhi's Tihar Central Jail on a 28-day parole, says the jail administration itself advised him to take parole. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, he says he is happy to be out of jail, plans to restart his YouTube channel and will continue making videos. Saleem says he stands with the truth and is not afraid to speak openly. He says he was convicted in a kidnapping and murder case, but claims he is not a murderer and alleges that his lawyer failed him. He also says he was innocent when the case took place. On Thursday, Saleem visited Dasna Temple and offered prayers before Goddess Mahakali. He is serving a life sentence in a kidnapping and murder case. Earlier, he had gone absconding after being released on parole and was arrested by Delhi Police on April 25. Question: 2 videos have surfaced speaking about jihadis, what do you have to say? Answer: These videos are from outside Tihar Jail in Delhi at night. On the night of June 9, I received 28 days of parole. Jail officials told me that my conduct is good, and I should take care of my health. Get treatment from doctors. After completing 28 days, you will have to come back. I have given a statement for jihadis in the video, this is the truth. Question: On what grounds did you ask for parole? Answer: I have not asked for parole, I was arrested by Delhi Police, presented in court, and sent to jail. After that, I stayed in jail, where I also received good conduct. All other inmates also respected me. The jail administration itself asked me for parole. I am happy that I am out of jail and making this video. Question: Yati Narsinghanand welcomed you by garlanding you, what would you say? Answer: This is a great fortune for me. Maharajji is my guru, he has supported me. I have come to the temple. I have taken Maharajji's blessings. Here I have seen Maa and Mahadev. I bowed my head and took blessings. Question: At the time of the attack, what did you feel, would you survive? Answer: I didn't feel at all that I would die. Not for a single moment. My ribs were broken by the beating, and I survived. Both my attackers were killed in encounters. Yogiji did the right thing. He did it at the right time. It is not right for someone who kills another person to live. The decision that was made was correct. Such a person does not have the right to live. Question: Why did Delhi Police arrest and send him to jail? Answer: It was a murder case, but I had nothing to do with that case. I had not committed kidnapping and murder, but it was a court case. How can I say that I am not a murderer? I was right, that's why I was acquitted. Otherwise, I wouldn't have been acquitted so quickly. I was convicted of murder and kidnapping. The judge told me that my lawyer was doing something wrong. I was a child at that time, naive. I couldn't stop the lawyer. After that, the court sentenced me. I was in jail for 6 years, after coming out of jail, I was out for 25 years, at my home. Delhi Police never came to my house, nor did they ever search for me. Then they declared me absconding, arrested me, and sent me to jail. Question: Will you restart the YouTube channel? Answer: Yes, I will restart my channel. I will work well. I am on the side of truth, I am not a coward. As I used to give statements before, I will do so again. I am not a servant of God. I am on the side of truth, I do not believe in Islam. If Islam were correct, why would I leave it? The government has made the correct law for triple talaq. Women should also have rights. Question: Bulldozers are running on illegal madrasas, what do you say about that? Answer: Dargahs and madrasas that are illegal should be removed. The government's action is correct. Encounters are also happening correctly. If it happened with innocent people, it would be wrong, but it is happening with wrongdoers, which is correct. Those who killed Surya Chauhan of Ghaziabad on the day of Eid al-Adha (Bakrid) should be hanged. They should be hanged in the public square. Question: Surya Chauhan's murderer was killed in an encounter, what do you say about that? Answer: It has been excellent. I salute the UP Police. I salute Yogi Ji 4 times. The four accused should not have been sent to jail; they should have been hanged in the town square. Punish for theft and robbery, but if someone takes a life, such murderers should not be kept alive; such people should be eliminated. The court should also make decisions in such cases. Why did Salim Wastik come into discussion these days, know more ahead Salim Vastik Bowed His Head at Dasna Temple Salim Vastik came out of Delhi's Tihar Central Jail late in the evening on June 9. Two days later, on Thursday, he reached Ghaziabad. Dasna Temple's security in-charge and Chhote Yati Narsinghanand Anil Yadav brought him along. Mahant Yati Narsinghanand Saraswati welcomed him. He bowed his head at the temple. Two videos of Salim Vastik surfaced. In the first video, he is seen standing near a tower. In it, he is pointing towards the tower and stating his location as outside Tihar Jail. Salim is seen holding a stick in his hand. In the second video, he is seen sitting in a house. First Video: Jihadis, now is the time to brace yourselves Saleem Wastik made 2 videos after coming out of Tihar. In the first, he is seen standing near a tower. Pointing towards the tower, he is stating his location as outside Tihar Jail. Salim is seen holding a stick in his hand. Saleem Wastik says- Yes brothers, Jihadis, look, see what place this is. It's the place outside Tihar Jail. Jihadis, now is the time to brace yourselves. I will lead Muslims towards education. I will lead Muslims towards progress. Second Video: A true man can never be troubled Salim said in his second video- I am out, a true man can never be troubled. There might be some minor obstacles. From the situation I was involved in, a person cannot come out. Only that person can come out who is right. Your brother has stayed there with respect. I would have been released after 10 days, but they told me that they would release me only after Bakrid. Now I will work for the Muslim community. I don't want to see them become Maulanas. Salim Vastik left Islam 7 years ago Saleem Wastik's ancestral home is in Shamli district. 20 years ago, he moved from Shamli and settled in Ashok Vihar Colony, Loni area of Ghaziabad. Besides him, his family includes his wife and a son, Usman Khan. Salim previously worked in construction. For some time, he also worked as a cleric (Maulvi). Later, he became disillusioned with Islam. Seven years ago, he left Islam and added 'Vastik' to his name. Salim bought land in Ali Garden Colony, about one and a half kilometres away from his house, and built a house there. He opened his office there and started working from there. Salim had agreements with various TV channels, where he used to participate in religious debates. He debated there as an ex-Muslim and presented views related to Islam. Later, he created his YouTube channel named Salim Vastik 0007 and started questioning Islam and the education in madrasas. He often talked about Halala, Hadith, and triple talaq. While discussing these topics, he used to quote verses from the Quran. Many people from the Muslim community would write abuses and give threats on his videos. Saleem Wastik was stabbed 14 times Saleem Wastik came into the limelight when two real brothers launched a deadly attack on him. They slit his throat with a knife and fled, thinking he was dead. This incident took place on February 27, 2026, when Saleem Wastik was fatally attacked after intruders entered his office. According to the police, masked assailants who arrived on a motorcycle without a number plate repeatedly stabbed Salim with a knife and tried to slit his throat. Upon his screaming, the attackers left him half-dead and fled. Hearing the noise, neighbors arrived and informed his family. His family took Salim to the hospital, from where he was referred to Guru Teg Bahadur Hospital (GTB). He was stabbed 14 times on his body. He remained admitted to Delhi's GTB Hospital for about a month. He underwent two operations there. Two real brothers attacked, both killed in police encounter After the deadly attack on Salim Wastik, the police started an investigation. The police identified the attackers as Gulfam and Zeeshan. Both of them were real brothers. The police killed both of them in an encounter. The police claim that Salim Wastik used to make videos on Islam and point out the shortcomings of the religion in most of his videos. For this reason, Zeeshan and Gulfam attacked him. Discharged from hospital, then arrested from home by Delhi Police After being injured in a deadly attack, Salim Wastik was treated at Delhi's GTB Hospital. He was discharged after his throat wound healed. He returned home on April 2, 2026. Meanwhile, Delhi Police arrested Salim Wastik from his home on April 25. According to the police who came to arrest him, Salim Khan alias Saleem Wastik used to give martial arts training in a school in Delhi. In the same school, Sandeep, the 13-year-old son of a businessman from North-East Delhi, also studied. Salim, along with his accomplice Anil, had kidnapped Sandeep while he was going to school. Both called from a PCO and demanded a ransom of 30 thousand rupees. When the demand was not met, they threatened the businessman's father with the murder of his child. Later, both killed the child. Subsequently, the Delhi Police recovered the child's body at the instance of Salim and Anil. Salim was put on trial. In 1997, the court sentenced Salim and his accomplice Anil to life imprisonment. Following this, Salim filed a petition in the Delhi High Court demanding the cancellation of the life sentence. However, in 2011, the High Court, while delivering its verdict, upheld the life sentence.

stories.title: AIIMS Raebareli under scanner over appointments:Candidates with less experience become professors, OBC posts allegedly given to general category applicants
stories.summary: A case of irregularities has come to light in the appointments of 2 faculty positions at AIIMS Raebareli. The recruitment of a Professor of General Medicine and an Assistant Professor of Dermatology is being called fraudulent. It is alleged that reservation rules were ignored for these appointments. The experience required for the post was also overlooked. Against this, RTI activist Sanjay Mishra filed a complaint with the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) in April. However, AIIMS Raebareli's Deputy Director Colonel (Retired) Akhilesh Singh misled the investigation. Following this, Sanjay Mishra has now demanded a CBI inquiry. Know what the whole matter is AIIMS Raebareli issued an on August 22, 2024, for the recruitment of a total of 95 posts. These included posts for Professor, Additional Professor, Associate Professor, and Assistant Professor. Among these, irregularities have come to light in 2 departments- 1. General Medicine Department- In this, 4 posts were to be filled. 1 post of Professor was for the General Category. Out of 2 posts of Associate Professor, one was reserved for SC and the other for EWS. 1 post of Assistant Professor was reserved for ST. 2. Dermatology Department- Here too, recruitment was announced for a total of 4 posts. Among these, 1-1 post each for Professor, Associate Professor, and Assistant Professor were reserved for OBC. 1 post of Additional Professor was for the General Category. Know what fraud happened 14 years of experience sought, 4 years of experience made Professor Dr. Jalish Fatima and Dr. Madhukar Mittal had applied for the post of Professor in General Medicine. For this, 14 years of teaching or research experience in the relevant subject was required. Dr. Mittal's total experience at that time was only 12 years and 4 months. His experience of teaching General Medicine was only 4 years and 3 months. In the provisional list of December 16, 2024, Dr. Jalish Fatima was fully qualified. Whereas, Dr. Madhukar Mittal was provisionally qualified due to the lack of an NOC. However, in the final list released on December 24, 2024, Dr. Mittal was selected. Dr. Fatima was placed on the waiting list. Dr. Mittal received illegal promotion in KGMU Dr. Madhukar Mittal was made Associate Professor at KGMU, Lucknow, in just 4 years and 3 months, before completing 5 years of experience. After this, the proposal to increase medical college seats went to the Medical Council of India (MCI). When the records of medical teachers posted at KGMU were investigated, the MCI objected to Dr. Mittal's promotion. As a result, the proposal to increase medical seats at KGMU was rejected. Along with this, Dr. Mittal's promotion was also cancelled. Dr. Mittal's NOC came after the interview - When applying to AIIMS Raebareli, Dr. Mittal was a Professor in the Department of Endocrinology and Metabolism at AIIMS Bhopal. As per recruitment rules, NOC from the current employer had to be submitted by the application deadline of October 5, 2024. At the time of application, Dr. Mittal had not submitted the NOC from AIIMS Bhopal. In such a case, his application should have been cancelled. However, Dr. Mittal's interview took place on December 28, 2024. Much later, after filling a penalty bond of Rs 5 lakh, AIIMS Bhopal issued the NOC on March 26, 2025. Retired Doctor Made Committee Chairman- Rules were also broken in the formation of the Standing Selection Committee that conducted the interviews. Dr Padma Srivastava was made the chairman of the committee. She had taken VRS from AIIMS New Delhi on October 16, 2023. As per the rules, the chairman of the committee should have been a person working in the institute. OBC Seat in Dermatology department given to general category Similar irregularities occurred in the recruitment for the Dermatology department. Here, the post of Assistant Professor was reserved for the OBC category. In the provisional list of December 16, 2024, Dr. Anjali Agarwal was declared 'unqualified' because she belonged to the General Category. In the same list, OBC candidate Dr. Chingshubam Vikas Singh was provisionally qualified. In the final list of December 24, 2024, Dr. Anjali Agarwal was not only considered qualified but was also appointed to the reserved seat in the result declared on January 28, 2025. False information given to PMO to protect favorites Against this entire fraud, RTI activist Sanjay Mishra sent a complaint to the Ministry of Health on January 14, 2026, and to the PMO on April 18, 2026. However, AIIMS Raebareli's Deputy Director Colonel Akhilesh Singh showed cunning instead of conducting an impartial investigation into the matter. He uploaded Dr. Jalish Fatima's documents instead of Dr. Madhukar Mittal's documents on the PMO's public grievance portal, so that the irregularity could be concealed. Director said - Candidates were not available in the reserved category Dr. Amita Jain, Executive Director of AIIMS Raebareli, stated that all appointments were made according to rules. Regarding the matter of changing reservations and appointing general candidates instead of OBC, at that time there was a provision that if candidates were not found in the reserved category in any department, it could be filled by general candidates. Now this rule has been abolished.

Crossroad renamed Surya Chowk in Surya’s honour:Khoda locals write CM Yogi’s name, demand approval
stories.summary: A square was named Surya Chowk on the thirteenth-day ritual (terahvin) of Surya Chauhan from Ghaziabad. During the condolence meeting held on Wednesday, local residents decided to name the square located near his house. After this, an iron board was installed on the cemented pole at the square. The board has 'Surya Chowk' written on it in red letters. Below it, Ward No.-13, Lane No.-1, Navneet Vihar, Khoda Colony, Ghaziabad is printed. CM Yogi's name is also written on the lower part of the board. A video of the board being installed has also surfaced. In the video, several youths are seen holding the board, while one youth is seen climbing an electricity and cement pole to tie it. The people of Khoda said that a proposal will be put forward and passed by the local councilor in the municipal board meeting to get official recognition for the chowk. 3,000 people attended Surya's Teharvin (13th-day ritual) On the Teharvin, Surya's mother Saroj demanded CM Yogi to ensure strict punishment for the accused. She said, "The accused should not be released from jail under any circumstances. If the accused are set free, they might devastate another mother's lap." Saroj Thakur has also expressed her wish to meet the Chief Minister. Meanwhile, the local councilor has also stated that he will propose officially naming the road 'Surya Chowk' at the Municipal Board meeting. Police forces are still deployed in the area to maintain law and order during the event. Mother cried inconsolably at the thirteenth-day ritual on Wednesday Surya Chauhan's thirteenth-day ritual was held on Wednesday. During the condolence meeting in Khoda, mother Saroj cried inconsolably. The mother said - So far, one person has been killed in an encounter. The rest are in jail. The only demand from the government is that they should not be allowed to come out of jail. A mother has lost her son. At least these people will not be able to kill any other mother's son now. Meanwhile, Surya's elder brother Yash Chauhan, who is ill, said that he will definitely meet CM Yogi ji. He has supported us a lot. Asad, who murdered my brother, was killed within 24 hours. The accused's house has been sealed and is slated for demolition. The government and administration have helped us a lot. Called on Bakrid day and stabbed Surya in the stomach Surya (17) was murdered on Bakrid day (May 28). According to a minor friend, the main accused Asad called Surya by phone. He surrounded him with his companions and repeatedly stabbed him with a knife. Before killing him, he asked Surya - "Have you ever seen a goat being halal slaughtered? Come, we'll show you." Its CCTV footage had also surfaced. Accused Asad has been killed in an encounter, while the other 4 accused have been arrested by the police and sent to jail. These include Asad's father Nawab (45), Farhan (19), Atif (19), and Sarik. Accused Farhan had told the police that Nawab had incited Asad to murder Surya. He had said, "End Surya's story on Bakrid."

stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi boldly proclaimed that the INDIA alliance is already the victor of the 2029 Lok Sabha elections. He stressed the vital importance of uniting the opposition to challenge the BJP's perceived encroachment on democratic institutions and the silencing of dissenting voices.

stories.title: 'Body preserved with water bottles': Indian sailor dies on vessel off Oman coast; union cites aid delay amid regional tensions
stories.summary: The Forward Seamen's Union of India is seeking assistance after a 35-year-old officer died on a vessel off Oman's coast. His body has been onboard for over two days without proper refrigeration, leading to a health risk for the crew. The union alleges delayed medical help due to regional tensions and is demanding body preservation, repatriation, and an investigation.

stories.title: US goes misanthropic over Anthropic AI, orders it to suspend access for frontier models to all foreign nationals
stories.summary: The US government has ordered AI firm Anthropic to suspend access to its newest frontier models for all foreign nationals, citing national security. This move, impacting non-American employees and international partners like India, highlights AI's growing geopolitical significance and prompts calls for sovereign AI development.

stories.title: Looking for domestic help? Dubai police issues alert on hiring maids, hourly workers
Abraham George, first Indian-American chairperson of Texas GOP, loses re-election. Reactions are shocking
PM Modi to hold bilateral talks with Trump at G7 Summit; first meeting in 16 months
Russian woman tourist found dead in Kasol homestay, cause under investigation
stories.summary: A 29-year-old Russian tourist was discovered deceased in a Kasol homestay on Saturday. Her friend found her unresponsive in the washroom. Authorities were alerted, and a police investigation is underway. The body has been sent for a post-mortem to ascertain the cause of death. The Russian Embassy has been notified.

stories.title: Delayed hospital for lottery ticket: UK mum jailed for life for murder of 7-week-old baby
'RSS most misunderstood': Mohan Bhagwat explains best way to understand Sangh
stories.summary: Addressing the RSS centenary celebrations, chief Mohan Bhagwat declared the organization the world's largest voluntary body, yet "most misunderstood." He explained the outreach aims to clarify misconceptions, noting external views range from paramilitary to gymnasium. Bhagwat emphasized direct engagement as the best way to understand the Sangh's true nature and its century-long mission of national welfare.

Forced to work 16 hrs daily, abused: West Bengal woman rescued from Gurugram flat
stories.summary: In a shocking incident, a woman from Birbhum, West Bengal, was freed from a high-security apartment in Gurugram after being reportedly trapped for more than two years under the horrific conditions of forced domestic servitude. Each day, she toiled for 16 hours amidst appalling abuse, her escape thwarted by stringent security measures.

The basement problem: Why safety concerns keep resurfacing in Delhi
stories.summary: A devastating fire at a Delhi hotel trapped eight members of the Agarwal family in the basement, leading to their tragic deaths. The incident highlights a pattern of basement misuse and safety violations in the capital, with similar tragedies involving students in flooded basements also reported. Despite regulations, enforcement remains a critical issue.

stories.title: Found in Epstein files: Clue about missing German model surfaces after 11 years - report
stories.summary: A German model, Michele, missing for 11 years, has reappeared in the Jeffrey Epstein files. Model recruiter Daniel Siad allegedly discussed her with Epstein before her 2015 disappearance. Her family fears the worst. Authorities could not launch an active search without evidence of a crime. Her fate remains unknown.

stories.title: Nipah outbreak: ICMR team arrives in Kozhikode; containment measures in place
stories.summary: Kozhikode is on high alert as a Nipah virus case is confirmed, triggering immediate action from the Indian Council of Medical Research. Health officials are actively evaluating containment strategies for the deadly zoonotic virus that poses significant risks. Although initial screenings of close contacts returned negative, health authorities are ramping up vigilance throughout the district.

stories.summary: Live elephant at Texas GOP convention: At the Texas Republican convention, a surprising guest made waves: Paige, an elephant. This unexpected appearance became a hot topic, with Democrats dubbing its urination on the floor a 'spot-on allegory' for the party's situation.

stories.title: The empty room upstairs: What happens when children leave home
stories.summary: Across Indian cities, adult children are moving out, leaving parents in larger homes. This shift redefines family closeness, moving beyond shared walls. Families are inventing new ways to stay connected, from daily video calls to simple texts, navigating a balance between care and independence. Scheduled visits now carry the weight of condensed family time, highlighting the loss of ordinary moments.

stories.title: Congress never a sinking ship! Sanjay Raut urges former Congress allies to reunite
stories.summary: Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut urged former Congress allies to reunite, emphasizing the need to strengthen the party against the BJP. He dismissed claims of the Congress being a "sinking ship" and appealed to Sharad Pawar to lead the reunification efforts. Raut also criticized the BJP's historical contributions and accused Amit Shah of attempting to break opposition parties.

stories.summary: Iran's embassy in India has dismissed US President Trump's accusation of a drone attack on Indian vessels in the Strait of Hormuz as "baseless." The embassy stated that Washington is attempting to divert attention from recent US strikes on three Indian-crewed ships, which resulted in the deaths of three Indian sailors.

stories.title: 'Pizza order' call helps Sharjah police rescue expat woman allegedly threatened by husband
Evening news wrap: IAF AN-32 aircraft crashes in Assam, 5 dead; Delhiites to pay more for electricity from next month & more
stories.summary: In a heartbreaking incident, an IAF AN-32 went down close to Jorhat, Assam, resulting in the loss of five lives. On a different front, the Centre has appointed Lt Gen Dhiraj Seth to take the helm as Chief of Army Staff. Economic concerns arise as electricity bills in Delhi are expected to climb from July owing to increased surcharges.

stories.title: 'New levels of frustration': BJP counters Sanjay Raut's 'aghori' remark on PM Modi
stories.summary: BJP strongly countered Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut's remarks comparing PM Modi to Aurangzeb, accusing the opposition of frustration and insulting Gujarat. Raut's sharp attack questioned Modi's character, calling him "cruel" and from the "land of Aurangzeb," sparking immediate BJP condemnation for crossing political discourse limits.

INDIA bloc hits reset button: Why 5-point truce plan of opposition alliance may not work
stories.summary: The INDIA bloc attempted a reset with a five-point plan to counter the BJP, but internal state-level rivalries remain a significant hurdle. Despite national unity efforts, allies like Congress and Samajwadi Party, or Congress and AAP, clash in state elections, undermining the coalition's strength and relevance. Addressing these deep-seated conflicts is crucial for lasting opposition unity.

J&K CM's advisor calls for revival of panel to oversee Kashmiri Pandits' return, rehabilitation
stories.summary: Jammu and Kashmir advisor Nasir Aslam Wani has called for the revival of the apex committee. This body will oversee the return and rehabilitation of Kashmiri Pandits. The committee, previously disbanded, will facilitate discussions between government representatives and the Kashmiri Pandit community. Its aim is to evolve a roadmap for a safe and dignified return to their homeland.

stories.title: 'You're not supposed to say that!': Jaishankar jokes after Finnish FM mentions 'many deals'; watch
stories.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar and Finnish Foreign Minister Elina Valtonen shared a light-hearted moment discussing defence cooperation during the Kultaranta Talks. Jaishankar also met with Finnish President Alexander Stubb, emphasizing diplomacy amidst global challenges and highlighting India's energy procurement driven by national interests.

stories.title: Amit Shah directs committee on demographic change to study border districts
stories.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah has directed a high-level committee to study demographic shifts in border districts, metro cities, and industrial towns. The committee will assess changes due to illegal migration and other unnatural causes, aiming to suggest solutions for national security and social structure preservation.

stories.title: 'Under the price cap': Finland minister backs India on Russian oil imports
stories.summary: In a recent statement, Finland's foreign minister Elina Valtonen expressed support for India's decision to acquire Russian oil, emphasizing that New Delhi is operating within the framework of the Western-imposed price cap. She underlined that the intention of the cap is to limit the profits of Russia rather than disrupt international trade.

The Air Force Academy also celebrated the successful completion of pre-commissioning training for its flight cadets.

stories.title: 'Abhishek is like my son': Kalyan Banerjee softens tone after calling TMC leader 'arrogant'
stories.summary: TMC leader Kalyan Banerjee softened his stance on Abhishek Banerjee, calling him 'like his son' after recent criticism. 'Won't let Indus waters reach patrons of terror': Rajnath Singh's strong message to Pakistan
stories.summary: Defence minister Rajnath Singh declared India will not allow Indus river waters to reach "patrons of terror," reinforcing a firm stance against Pakistan. Singh also detailed India's global role, defence sector growth, and the NDA government's achievements, contrasting them with past corruption.

1,569 days and counting: Russia-Ukraine war now longer than World War I
stories.summary: The Russia-Ukraine war has surpassed World War I in duration, now exceeding 1,569 days. What began as a swift Russian operation has become Europe's longest and bloodiest conflict since WWII, defying early predictions. Despite diplomatic efforts and Western support for Ukraine, a durable peace remains elusive, with no clear end in sight.

stories.title: From Lebanon ceasefire to nuclear talks: What are the terms proposed by Iran in 'Islamabad Agreement'
stories.summary: Iran has outlined conditions for a potential US agreement, prioritizing sanctions relief and maritime access over immediate nuclear program discussions. Tehran insists on lifting the US naval blockade and a new arrangement for the Strait of Hormuz, while also seeking to include Lebanon in the deal.

stories.title: Hair Dye under Regulator’s Lens; Firms asked to prove safety compliance
stories.summary: India's drug regulator is now demanding hair colour manufacturers prove their products meet safety standards and carry clear warnings. Companies must adhere to Cosmetics Rules and BIS norms regarding ingredients, restrictions, and labelling, including mandatory patch-test instructions. This move highlights growing scrutiny on cosmetic safety, urging firms to re-evaluate formulations and consumer information for this booming market.

stories.title: ICMR, Gates Foundation launch Rs. 1-Crore challenge to fight anaemia
stories.summary: India's ICMR and Gates Foundation are launching a Rs. 1-crore challenge to create appealing, iron-rich foods for women and girls battling anaemia. The initiative aims to move beyond traditional supplements, seeking innovative, affordable products like fortified snacks and beverages that fit daily diets. This aims to boost consumption and combat the widespread health issue.

stories.title: 'Driven to London by masked men': Indian-origin man Gagandeep Singh sentenced to 34-years for kidnaping, raping woman
stories.summary: An Indian-origin man, Gagandeep Singh, has been sentenced to 34 years in prison in the UK for kidnapping, torturing, and raping a woman. The 34-year-old was convicted of multiple serious offenses after a trial. He will serve 28 years in custody, followed by an extended license period, and will be deported after completing his sentence.

stories.title: Paraguay's president will be at USA's FIFA World Cup 2026 opener, but is Donald Trump attending?
stories.summary: As the United States prepare to open their FIFA World Cup 2026 campaign against Paraguay, attention has shifted off the pitch after Paraguayan president Santiago Peña confirmed he will attend the match in Los Angeles while US president Donald Trump will not. Trump instead offered support via a phone call to the squad, adding a political subplot to a high-profile opener between the hosts and returning South Americans.

stories.title: Trump's message to USNMT revealed as president calls squad before FIFA World Cup 2026 opener against Paraguay
stories.summary: The United States received a morale boost ahead of its 2026 FIFA World Cup opener after President Donald Trump personally called the squad to wish them luck. Speaking with head coach Mauricio Pochettino and captain Tim Ream, Trump backed the team's chances on home soil as preparations intensified for the clash with Paraguay, adding to the growing anticipation surrounding the hosts' tournament debut.

stories.title: Psych evaluation of parents a must in child custody disputes, rules SC
stories.summary: Writing the judgment, Justice N Kotiswar Singh said, “While it is important to make an assessment as to how a child will respond to either of the parents, it is equally important to ascertain mental and psychological conditions of the parents themselves to deal with the needs of the growing child.” SC said the assessment of the parents’ psychological conditions must be conducted prior to a similar assessment of the child to understand compatibility with each of the parents.

stories.title: Bangladesh border guards raise pushback issue at BSF meet
SC asks ex-judge to mediate IAS Rohini vs IPS Roopa feud
stories.summary: Asking them to appear before Justice Joseph in July, the bench stayed proceedings before trial courts in the cross-defamation suits filed by the two officers against each other. In Feb 2023, Roopa had posted a series of social media posts against Rohini, including disproportionate assets allegations. Rohini successfully moved court to restrain Roopa from making defamatory remarks.

stories.title: NDA looks to boost numbers in Lok Sabha, Sena UBT may also split
stories.summary: Sources within NDA suggest one of the parties that may see desertion from its ranks is Sena UBT, a possibility being talked about since the alliance swept the assembly polls in Maharashtra but has gained traction now. The Uddhav Thackeray-led party has nine MPs in Lok Sabha and six of them will have to merge with another party — Shiv Sena led by deputy CM Eknath Shinde seen as the most probable option — to avoid losing membership under the anti-defection law.

stories.title: Why did Clavicular get so emotional? Looksmaxxing streamer faces intense reactions during recovery stream
stories.summary: Kick streamer Braden Peters, better known as Clavicular, went viral after becoming emotional during a livestream while recovering from facial surgery. The moment happened during his “Ascension Week” content series when a text-to-speech donation criticized his appearance. The clip sparked debate about cosmetic procedures, online criticism, and the growing influence of looksmaxxing content among young audiences.

stories.title: Rebels claim 19 MPs in ‘real TMC’ fight, set to meet Speaker
stories.summary: While none from the rebel camp contested the screenshots, almost everyone voiced grievance against Abhishek Banerjee. Lashing out, Abhishek said, “BJP has been trying many tactics — from creating rift in our party to intimidating party workers, taking over party offices, and destroying our organisation. But no matter what they do, they cannot deny the fact that 2.6 crore people voted for us and we got a 41% votes. We will continue to fight against this oppression.”

stories.title: Govt notifies order to cap bulk fuel buys during crunch
stories.summary: Institutional, industrial and commercial consumers can be directed not to procure petrol or diesel from retail outlets and instead source their requirements through authorised bulk channels. Retail outlets may be barred from selling more than 200 litres of diesel to a customer or vehicle in a day, while fuel procured under the provision cannot be resold.

stories.title: Despite rift, Rahul Gandhi says DMK with opposition on ‘idea of India’
stories.summary: Alleging BJP steals elections, Rahul said he had warned “friends in TMC”, who were confident that they were sweeping Bengal polls, that they were in “dreamland” — stating he had seen it in Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Haryana and Maharashtra. He said BJP can’t win the next polls, “which is already won”, because people are angry, but the hurdle is that elections will not be free and fair.

stories.title: Who is Chanida Natalie? Marlon’s proposal puts influencer girlfriend in spotlight with xQc weighing in
stories.summary: Chanida Natalie is an influencer known for lifestyle and fashion content and for her relationship with streamer Marlon. The couple, reportedly together since 2025, recently got engaged. Natalie shared the proposal video on Instagram, drawing attention from fans and creators. Felix “xQc” Lengyel praised the engagement, while Twitch streamer Cinna reacted with surprise to the news.

stories.title: Ex-RCom execs Doshi & Seth arrested by ED in ADAG case
stories.summary: ED’s case against Ambani and his group entities and associates is handled by a special investigation team constituted at the agency’s headquarters here. The duo, along with Amitabh Jhunjhunwala, who is in judicial custody, comprised the core leadership team of Ambani. Doshi was earlier arrested in 2011 by CBI in its 2G spectrum scam case and was behind bars for seven months before he was granted bail.

stories.title: 'No writs after polls begin': Supreme Court rejects Meenakshi Natarajan's plea
stories.summary: After an hour-long proceeding, during which senior advocate Mukul Rohatgi for the BJP candidate whose election was facilitated by Natarajan’s disqualification and solicitor general Tushar Mehta for MP govt cited a judgment where SC had refused to entertain a similar plea against rejection of nomination papers, the bench said the SC or HC cannot entertain writ petitions in exercise of their jurisdictions under Articles 32 or 226 of the Constitution. Once the election process commences with the notification of polls.

stories.title: Price cap on 2 key cancer drugs increased by 50%
stories.summary: The regulator has also revised prices of anti-tetanus immunoglobulin and three key childhood vaccines to ensure their continued availability. The decision, for which a gazette notification has been issued, was taken at NPPA's 147th meeting on Thursday, where the authority invoked its extraordinary powers under Para 19 of the Drug Price Control Order (DPCO), 2013, to revise prices of formulations considered critical for public health.

stories.title: Did Candace Owens hint at Donald Trump's involvement in Charlie Kirk case? Laura Loomer responds
stories.summary: Candace Owens stirred debate after reacting to a New York Times report about a reported phone call between Donald Trump and Charlie Kirk. Laura Loomer claimed Owens accused Trump of killing Kirk, but Owens never directly made that allegation. The exchange divided social media users, with some supporting Owens’ questions and others criticizing her claims.

stories.title: Candidates get 15 minutes extra time for NEET retest
stories.summary: The retest comes after cancellation of the May 3 exam following paper leak, which is being probed by CBI. In a notice, NTA said the exam — for admissions to medical colleges — will be held from 2 pm to 5.15 pm. The additional 15 minutes will accommodate mandatory formalities (attendance signing and other procedures).

stories.title: Forecasts indicate El Niño to grow stronger during monsoon: IMD
stories.summary: “El Niño conditions are present over equatorial Pacific Ocean and are expected to strengthen during monsoon season,” IMD said, while announcing the advent of the condition — warming of ocean waters in central and eastern equatorial Pacific — that’s invariably linked with weak monsoon in India. The latest forecast could be used by policymakers to immediately activate contingency measures in all 197 districts across the country that have been identified by the agriculture ministry as most vulnerable to impacts of El Niño.

stories.title: 'Lethal actions against commercial shipping not justified': Jaishankar lodges 'strong protest' with Rubio
stories.summary: Jaishankar's remarks came in the aftermath of a US military strike on the commercial tanker MT Settebello in the Gulf of Oman, which claimed the lives of three Indian crew members. The vessel was targeted on Wednesday after US forces alleged that it had breached the naval blockade imposed on Iranian ports. Of the 24 Indian nationals aboard the tanker, 21 were rescued, while three were later confirmed dead.

stories.summary: As per a UN Motorcycle Helmet Study, motorcyclists are 26 times more likely to die in road crashes than drivers of cars and wearing an appropriate helmet “improves their chances of survival by 42% and helps avoid 69% of injuries to riders.” Similarly, as per World Health Organisation, seat-belts are approximately 50% effective in preventing fatalities in crashes in which motorists would otherwise die.

stories.title: Planning of cities must be people-centric, says Manohar Lal as Brics forum adopts urban pact
stories.summary: Cities must prioritize people and their needs, according to Housing Minister Manohar Lal, as BRICS nations adopted a declaration for inclusive urban development. The 'Cities for People' forum stressed equitable access to housing and services, with India facing significant future urbanization. Strengthening local governments and embracing digital solutions were also key takeaways for creating sustainable, liveable urban centers.

stories.title: Amarnath Yatra: Amit Shah orders multi-layered security, pushes tech-driven pilgrim safety
stories.summary: Home Minister Amit Shah has ordered a robust, multi-layered security grid for the Amarnath Yatra, utilizing advanced technology like drones and CCTV. He stressed securing tourist spots for safe pilgrimage and tourism. The 57-day yatra, starting July 3, will see strict regulation of pilgrim movement and enhanced essential services, with QR code IDs for local support staff and animals.

The Civil Aviation Minister reiterated commitment to a thorough and objective determination of the accident's causes.

The TMC has labelled the case politically motivated amidst the party's internal dissent and recent election results, with investigations now underway.
